If a repair cannot be completed, we will explain why and discuss the remedy available under your warranty. You can ask us to review a decision about cover or raise a complaint if you are unhappy with our service. Your warranty does not affect your statutory rights.

If you need a warranty repair in Midlands, contact Halvard Home through the support details shown in your warranty documents. Describe the fault and tell us how it affects normal use. We will ask for proof of purchase and information from the appliance label so that we can check your warranty and arrange suitable support.

We assess claims against the terms of your warranty. Acceptance means that we have agreed to arrange support under those terms, based on the information available. The engineer may need to inspect the appliance to confirm the cause of the fault and whether the repair is covered. We will explain any concerns about cover before asking you to approve chargeable work.

In Midlands, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 76 hours of a claim being accepted. We will contact you to offer an appointment and confirm the address, access arrangements and details of the reported fault. This commitment concerns the offer of a visit; it does not mean that the repair will be completed during that visit.

Parts for warranty repairs in Midlands arrive within 58 working days. If your repair needs a replacement part, we will explain what is required and how the repair will proceed. An engineer may need to return to fit the part and check that the appliance operates safely. We will keep you informed about the arrangements for completing the work.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Clear the surrounding area and tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything at the property that could affect the visit. If you have accessibility needs or require communication support, let us know when arranging the appointment so that we can discuss suitable adjustments with you.

Do not continue using an appliance if you believe it is unsafe. Follow the safety advice in its instructions and contact us for guidance. Do not remove protective covers or attempt internal repairs yourself. If it is safe to do so, leave the appliance in its installed position so that the engineer can assess the fault and the installation.

Where the fault and the required work are covered by your warranty, we will not charge you for the warranty repair. If the engineer identifies an issue outside that cover, we will explain the findings and any proposed charge. You can decide whether to authorise work that falls outside the warranty.

If you cannot attend the agreed appointment, contact us to rearrange it. Please also tell us if the fault changes or the appliance has been moved. Once the repair is complete, the engineer will explain the work carried out and any relevant care advice. If you remain concerned about the repair, contact Halvard Home so that we can review the matter with you.

cell.item: POL-WAR/Wales and West/Warranty repairs in this region

result.text:
If your Halvard Home appliance develops a fault in Wales and West, contact our customer support team using the contact details in your warranty documents. Explain what has happened and whether the appliance appears safe to use. We will guide you through the warranty claim process.

Please have your proof of purchase and the appliance identification details available. We may ask for photographs or a description of the fault to help us assess your claim. If you cannot find the requested information, tell us so that we can explain what other evidence may be suitable.

We will check whether the fault is covered by your warranty and confirm whether your claim has been accepted. Acceptance means that we have agreed to arrange a repair under the warranty, based on the information available. We will explain if an inspection is needed to establish the cause of the fault.

In Wales and West, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 46 hours of a claim being accepted.

This commitment concerns the offer of a visit, rather than completion of the repair. We will contact you to discuss access and agree an appointment. Please tell us about accessibility needs, parking restrictions or anything else that could affect the engineer’s ability to reach and inspect the appliance safely.

Parts for warranty repairs in Wales and West arrive within 57 working days.

A repair may depend on replacement parts being available. We will explain whether parts are needed and how this affects the repair arrangements. The engineer may need to return to fit them. We will keep you informed about the arrangements and confirm when the appliance is ready to use.

Before the visit, make sure the engineer can reach the appliance without obstruction. Keep children and pets away from the work area. Do not move a heavy appliance or disconnect fixed services yourself. If access requires specialist assistance, discuss this with us when arranging the appointment.

If the appliance appears unsafe, stop using it. Disconnect it only if you can do so safely, and follow the safety instructions supplied with it. Do not attempt a repair yourself while waiting for advice, as this could cause injury or further damage.

The engineer will assess the fault and explain the proposed work. If the inspection identifies damage or work outside the warranty cover, we will explain the reason and discuss the available options. We will seek your agreement before carrying out work that you would need to pay for.

After the repair, the engineer will explain what has been done and provide relevant advice about safe use. Keep the repair record with your warranty documents. If the fault remains or you are unhappy with the service, contact customer support so that we can review the matter.

Your warranty operates alongside your statutory rights. Nothing in these repair arrangements limits the rights you have under consumer law, including rights you may have against the retailer.

cell.item: POL-WAR/London and South East/Warranty repairs in this region

result.text:
Warranty repairs in London and South East are arranged through Halvard Home or an authorised service partner. Please contact our customer support team to make a claim rather than booking a repair yourself. We will check your warranty cover, discuss the fault and confirm whether your address falls within this regional service area.

To help us assess your claim, please have your proof of purchase and warranty details available. Tell us what has gone wrong and whether there are signs of damage or a safety concern. We may ask for photographs or suggest checks that are safe to carry out. Do not dismantle the appliance.

A claim is accepted when we confirm that the information provided supports a repair under your warranty. Acknowledging your message or asking for further information does not mean that the claim has been accepted. We will explain our decision and tell you how the repair will be arranged.

In London and South East, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 60 hours of a claim being accepted.

We will contact you to offer an appointment and explain the access arrangements. Please tell us about parking restrictions, building entry requirements or anything that could affect safe access. If the offered appointment is unsuitable, contact us so that we can discuss an alternative.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely and that an adult with permission to authorise access is present. Keep the surrounding area clear and secure pets away from the work area. Let us know if you need adjustments to help you use our repair service.

The engineer will inspect the fault and explain the proposed repair. Work covered by your warranty is carried out without charge for labour or replacement parts. If the inspection identifies work outside your warranty, we will explain the reason and seek your agreement before arranging chargeable work.

Parts for warranty repairs in London and South East arrive within 60 working days.

If a replacement part is needed, we will explain how it will be supplied and how the fitting appointment will be arranged. The visit offer and the arrival of parts are separate service commitments. Neither statement promises that the repair will be completed during the engineer’s initial visit.

If the appliance appears unsafe, stop using it and contact us for advice. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. Do not attempt a repair or allow an unauthorised person to carry out work while we are assessing the fault.

After the repair, the engineer will explain the work completed and provide relevant care or safety advice. Contact us if the fault remains or you are unhappy with the service. We will review your concerns and explain the available next steps. Your warranty does not affect your statutory rights.

cell.item: POL-WAR/Northern Ireland/Warranty repairs in this region

result.text:
If you need a warranty repair in Northern Ireland, contact Halvard Home through the support details provided with your warranty documents. Explain the fault and tell us where the repair is needed. Have your proof of purchase available so that we can check your warranty cover and confirm whether your claim is accepted.

We may ask you to describe what happens when the fault occurs or send photographs if these would help us assess the problem. We will explain what information is needed and how to provide it. Please do not dismantle anything or attempt work that could put you at risk.

In Northern Ireland, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 30 hours of a claim being accepted. We will contact you to arrange access and explain what to expect from the visit. Tell us about any accessibility needs, restrictions on entry or other circumstances that could affect the engineer’s ability to carry out the repair safely.

Please make sure the repair location is accessible and that the surrounding area is clear. Someone authorised to discuss the fault and allow the work must be present. If you cannot keep the agreed appointment, contact us so that we can rearrange it and update the engineer.

The engineer will inspect the fault and explain the proposed repair. Work covered by your warranty includes the labour and replacement parts needed to correct an accepted warranty fault. If the inspection identifies work outside your warranty cover, we will explain why and seek your agreement before proceeding with that work.

Parts for warranty repairs in Northern Ireland arrive within 15 working days. If parts are needed, we will explain how they will be supplied and arrange any return visit required to fit them. Please leave the fitting of warranty parts to an engineer authorised by Halvard Home.

If the engineer finds that a repair cannot be completed safely or is not suitable, we will explain the available options under your warranty. We will discuss the proposed solution with you rather than assume your agreement. Any arrangements will reflect the nature of the fault and the cover that applies.

After the repair, the engineer will check the work and explain any relevant care or safety advice. Keep the repair record with your warranty documents. If the fault remains or returns, contact us and describe what has happened so that we can review the repair and advise you.

Your safety remains important throughout the claims process. If you notice smoke, a burning smell, exposed wiring or another sign of danger, stop using the affected item and seek advice. Do not continue using it simply because a warranty visit has been arranged.

This warranty repair service does not affect your statutory rights. You may also have rights against the retailer from whom you bought the item. If you are unhappy with how your claim or repair has been handled, contact Halvard Home and ask for the matter to be reviewed through our complaints process.

cell.item: POL-WAR/Island Areas/Warranty repairs in this region

result.text:
In Island Areas, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 89 hours of a claim being accepted. Halvard Home will confirm when your claim has been accepted and explain how to arrange the visit. Please check that the contact details and repair address you provide are correct.

When making a claim, describe the fault clearly and tell us whether it affects the safe use of your appliance. We may ask for proof of purchase and information from the appliance label so that we can check warranty cover and identify the repair support needed.

If the appliance appears unsafe, stop using it and contact us for advice. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. Do not attempt a repair yourself or remove protective covers. Tell us about signs of damage, unusual smells or leaking.

Our service team will discuss access with you before arranging the visit. Please tell us if your home depends on ferry travel, has restricted vehicle access or requires permission for an engineer to enter. We will explain the proposed arrangements and ask you to confirm that they are suitable.

Parts for warranty repairs in Island Areas arrive within 59 working days. This commitment concerns the arrival of parts, rather than completion of the repair. We will explain whether parts are needed after assessing the fault and keep you informed about arrangements for fitting them.

An engineer visit does not necessarily mean that the repair can be completed during that visit. The engineer may need to inspect the appliance, confirm the cause of the fault or request a suitable part. We will explain the findings and discuss what happens next.

Please make the appliance accessible and clear the surrounding space of belongings that could obstruct safe working. Keep children and pets away from the work area. If the appliance is installed behind fitted panels or in an enclosed space, tell us when arranging the repair.

Repairs covered by the warranty are carried out without charging you for the covered work, required parts or agreed engineer travel. If an inspection suggests that the fault falls outside the warranty, we will explain why. Chargeable work will require your agreement before it begins.

Weather, transport disruption or unsafe access may affect the arrangements for reaching your home. If this happens, we will contact you, explain the position and discuss an alternative appointment. You do not need to arrange private transport for an engineer unless you have expressly agreed to do so.

After the repair, the engineer will explain the work completed and provide relevant care or safety advice. Contact Halvard Home if the fault remains or you are unhappy with the service. We will review your concerns and explain the available remedy. Your statutory rights are not affected by this warranty.

This policy explains how returns and refunds work at Halvard Home. It is for customers who buy directly from us for personal or household use, and for people helping them with a return. If you bought through a retailer or marketplace, please contact the seller about its returns process.

Here you can find guidance on requesting a return, providing proof of purchase, preparing goods for collection or delivery, and receiving a refund. The policy also explains how we handle goods that arrive damaged, develop a fault or do not match their description, as well as requests made because you have changed your mind.

We aim to make the process clear, fair and straightforward. Our customer support team can explain what applies to your circumstances and help if you need an accessible way to contact us. This policy does not affect your legal rights as a consumer.

You can return an unwanted appliance within 80 days of delivery. This applies if you have changed your mind, whether the appliance does not suit your home or you simply no longer want it. Please contact our customer support team to arrange the return rather than sending the appliance back without letting us know.

When you contact us, have your order confirmation ready and tell us which appliance you would like to return. We will explain how to prepare it and confirm the available return arrangements. You do not need to give a reason for changing your mind, although we welcome feedback if you would like to share it.

You may unpack and inspect the appliance as you would in a shop. Please handle it carefully and avoid using it beyond what is needed to check its nature, features and operation. If handling or use has reduced its value, we may make a deduction from your refund where the law allows. We will explain the reason for a deduction and how we have assessed it.

Please return the appliance with its supplied accessories, instructions and removable parts. Use the original packaging if you still have it. If you do not, let us know so we can advise on suitable protection. Missing packaging does not automatically prevent a return, but the appliance must be packed securely enough to protect it during transport.

Before the appliance is collected or sent back, remove your belongings and make sure it is clean, dry and safe to handle. Where relevant, disconnect it safely and remove any personal information stored on it. If disconnection requires specialist help, arrange this with a suitably qualified person. Our customer support team can explain what preparation is needed, but please do not attempt work you cannot carry out safely.

We will tell you whether collection is available and whether you will be responsible for return transport costs before you agree to the arrangements. Please tell us about access restrictions or anything that could make collection difficult. Keep your collection receipt or proof of postage until your return has been resolved.

Refunds are paid within 5 working days of a returned appliance arriving at our warehouse. We will send your refund to the payment method used for the purchase and confirm when it has been issued. Your payment provider controls when the refund appears in your account.

These terms cover returns because you have changed your mind. They do not limit your statutory rights, including rights that may apply when you cancel a purchase made online or when an appliance is faulty, damaged or not as described. If your return concerns a problem with the appliance, please tell us so we can handle it under the appropriate terms.

If your delivery arrives damaged, please contact Halvard Home so we can help. We understand that damage can be disappointing and inconvenient. We will explain the options available and arrange a suitable resolution, taking account of the condition of the delivery and your legal rights.

Report damage found on delivery within 73 hours.

Please use the contact details provided in your order confirmation or on our website. Tell us what has happened and include your order reference, your contact details and a clear description of the damage. Let us know whether the damage affects the packaging, the contents or anything else delivered with your order.

If it is safe to do so, please take clear photographs of the damage and the packaging. These can help us understand the problem and decide how to handle the return. If you cannot provide photographs, tell us. We will discuss an alternative way to assess the damage rather than automatically refuse your request.

You may refuse a delivery if you can see that it is damaged. Ask the delivery driver to record the reason for refusal, where possible, and contact us to explain what happened. Accepting a delivery or signing a delivery record does not remove your right to report damage or seek a remedy.

Please do not use anything that appears unsafe. Avoid attempting repairs or handling exposed or broken parts. Keep the delivery somewhere secure, away from children and pets, if you can do so safely. Tell us about any hazard so we can give appropriate advice about collection.

Keep the packaging if it is available and safe to store. It may help protect the contents during collection and support our assessment. Missing or damaged packaging will not, by itself, prevent us from helping you. Please tell us if you need suitable packaging or assistance preparing the return.

We will explain whether collection is needed and agree the arrangements with you. We cover the reasonable costs of returning a delivery that arrived damaged. Please contact us before arranging your own return service, so we can confirm a suitable method and explain how any agreed costs will be reimbursed.

Depending on the circumstances and your legal rights, you may be entitled to a repair, replacement or refund. We will discuss your preferred remedy and explain any relevant limitations. We will not require you to accept store credit instead of a refund to which you are legally entitled.

A replacement for a damaged delivery is sent within 19 working days.

If a replacement is unavailable, we will contact you to discuss an appropriate alternative or refund. Any refund will be returned through your original payment method unless we agree otherwise with you.

If you discover damage outside the reporting window, please still contact us. The reporting request helps us investigate delivery problems; it does not limit your statutory rights. We will consider the circumstances fairly and explain our decision clearly, including how to raise a complaint if you are unhappy with the outcome.

An appliance that develops a fault within 100 days of delivery can be returned for a full refund. If you believe your appliance is faulty, contact Halvard Home customer support so we can help you arrange its return. Please describe the fault and explain how it affects the appliance.

We may ask for proof of purchase, such as an order confirmation, receipt or bank statement showing the purchase. We may also ask for photographs or a description of any visible damage. Please do not attempt to reproduce a fault if doing so could be unsafe.

Stop using the appliance if you notice signs that it may be dangerous. Disconnect it from the power supply if this is safe to do, and keep it away from children and pets. Do not dismantle it or attempt a repair to support your return request.

Our support team will explain how the appliance should be returned and arrange a suitable collection or return method. Tell us if its location, condition or installation could make removal difficult. Please do not send it back without contacting us, as we need to provide the correct return instructions.

You do not need the original packaging to return a faulty appliance. However, the appliance must be prepared for transport safely. We will explain what protection is needed and discuss suitable arrangements if you cannot pack or move it safely yourself.

Please remove personal belongings and follow our instructions about emptying, cleaning or disconnecting the appliance where relevant. Tell us if the fault prevents you from doing this. If the appliance stores personal information, remove that information where you can do so safely.

Returned faulty appliances are tested within 11 working days of arrival. Testing helps us understand the reported problem and assess the appliance’s condition. We will consider your description of the fault alongside our findings, including whether the problem occurs only under particular conditions.

We will explain the outcome of our assessment in plain language. If we cannot reproduce the fault, we will discuss the findings with you and consider any further information you provide. A fault that does not appear during testing will not automatically be treated as an unfounded claim.

Where a refund is due, we will normally return it through the payment method used for the purchase. We will explain how any applicable delivery charges are handled. Please tell us if the original payment method is no longer available so we can discuss an appropriate alternative.

Damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or failure to follow safety instructions may not qualify as a fault for the purposes of this policy. We will explain any decision to decline a return and the evidence supporting it. We will not reject a claim simply because packaging is missing.

These terms do not limit your statutory rights. Depending on the circumstances, you may be entitled to a repair, replacement or refund under consumer law. If you disagree with our decision, contact customer support and ask for your complaint to be reviewed.

If you would like to return your Brio kettle, please contact Halvard Home customer care before sending it back. Tell us whether you would prefer a refund or a colour exchange, and whether the appliance has been opened, used or damaged. This helps us give you the right return instructions.

Please provide proof of purchase, such as your receipt or confirmation email. If you cannot find it, contact us so we can help check your purchase details. If you bought your Brio kettle from a retailer rather than directly from Halvard Home, please contact that retailer about its returns process.

For a change of mind, keep the appliance in its original condition and include the accessories, instructions and packaging where available. Please tell us if anything is missing or if the packaging has been discarded. We will explain whether this affects your return before you send the appliance.

A restocking charge of 29% of the price applies to an opened Brio kettle. This charge applies to change-of-mind returns accepted under our voluntary returns policy, not where you are exercising a statutory right that prevents such a charge. We will explain any applicable deduction before you decide whether to proceed.

The Brio kettle can be swapped for another colour. An exchange for a different colour must be requested within 54 days. This period runs from delivery of the appliance. Please tell customer care which colour you would prefer. Exchanges depend on availability, and we will discuss the options with you if your preferred colour is unavailable.

Before packing your Brio kettle, unplug it, allow it to cool and empty out any water. Make sure the appliance is dry. Do not send it with water inside, as this could damage the parcel or make it unsafe to handle.

Pack the appliance securely, protecting it from movement and knocks. Use the original packaging if it remains suitable, or choose sturdy protective packaging. Include the return information provided by customer care so we can match the parcel to your request.

We will explain how to send your return and whether you are responsible for postage. Please follow the instructions supplied and keep proof of posting. If you need help arranging the return, contact us before handing the parcel to a carrier.

If your Brio kettle is faulty, damaged on arrival or not as described, tell us what has happened. Do not continue using an appliance that appears unsafe. We may ask for photographs or further details to help assess the problem and arrange an appropriate remedy.

After receiving your return, we will check the appliance and contact you about your refund or exchange. Refunds are normally made through the payment method used for the purchase. We will explain any issue that affects processing your return.

Nothing in this policy limits your statutory rights. If your legal rights differ from our voluntary return conditions, your legal rights take precedence.

Keep the original packaging of the Brio kettle for 73 days in case it needs to be returned. The box and protective inserts help prevent damage during transport. Store them somewhere dry and keep them in a condition that allows the kettle to be packed securely.

If the original packaging is no longer available, use a sturdy box with suitable cushioning. The kettle should not move freely inside the box or press against its sides. Missing original packaging does not, by itself, prevent us from considering your return.

Let the Brio kettle cool, unplug it and empty out any water before packing it. Make sure the kettle and its accessories are dry. Do not pack a kettle that is leaking or shows signs of electrical damage without contacting us for advice.

Include the accessories supplied with your Brio kettle, including its power base. Pack loose items securely so they cannot scratch the kettle or damage its lid, handle or spout. Do not include unrelated belongings, as we cannot guarantee that they will be recovered and sent back.

A returned Brio kettle is inspected within 3 days of arrival. We check its condition, look for damage and confirm which accessories have been included. We also compare what we find with the reason you gave for returning it.

A returned Brio kettle missing accessories is refunded at 47% of the price. Check the contents carefully before sealing your parcel. If an accessory was missing when your order arrived, tell us when arranging the return so we can treat this as an issue with your order.

A returned Brio kettle that needs cleaning is charged £60.00. Remove loose residue and wipe away dirt before packing, following the care instructions supplied with the kettle. Do not use harsh chemicals or abrasive materials, as these may damage its surfaces.

The missing accessory refund and cleaning charge apply to change of mind returns where permitted by law. They do not reduce your statutory rights if the kettle is faulty, damaged on arrival or not as described. Contact us if you are unsure how these terms affect your return.

Please describe any marks, damage or missing parts honestly when requesting a return. Clear photographs can help us understand the condition and advise you on safe packing. You do not need to attempt a repair or take the kettle apart.

Remove old delivery labels from reused packaging and attach the return label clearly. Keep your proof of posting and any photographs showing how the kettle was packed. If our inspection identifies a concern that affects your refund, we will explain what we found and how it relates to these terms.

If you would like to return your Tessa dishwasher, contact Halvard Home customer care with your order details and the reason for your return. Tell us whether the appliance has been unpacked, installed or used, and whether you are asking for a refund or an exchange. We will explain how to arrange the return.

Keep the appliance safe while your return is being arranged. Please do not continue using it if you have reported a fault or damage. If you are returning it because you have changed your mind, keep it clean and protect it from scratches, moisture and other damage.

A restocking charge of 24% of the price applies to an opened Tessa dishwasher. This charge applies to eligible change of mind returns, where permitted by law. It does not apply where you are entitled to return a faulty, damaged or incorrectly supplied appliance under your statutory rights. We will explain any applicable deduction before you agree to proceed.

Collection of a returned Tessa dishwasher costs £27.00. This is the collection charge for an eligible change of mind return. If the return is needed because the appliance is faulty, damaged or incorrectly supplied, contact us so that we can arrange an appropriate return without charging you for collection.

A returns label for the Tessa dishwasher is emailed within 2 hours of the request. Check your junk folder if you cannot find the email, and contact customer care if it has not arrived. Follow the instructions in the email when attaching the label, keeping it visible and away from areas where packaging could tear.

Arrange for the appliance to be disconnected safely before collection. If you are unsure how to disconnect it, seek help from a suitably qualified professional. Empty the appliance, drain any remaining water and secure loose parts. Use the original packaging if available, or ask us for advice on suitable protective packaging.

Tell us about access restrictions when arranging collection, including stairs, narrow doorways or parking difficulties. Keep the collection route clear and make sure someone is available to hand over the appliance. Please do not leave it outside or unattended, as this could expose it to damage or prevent collection.

An exchange for a Tessa dishwasher in a different colour must be requested within 86 days. Exchanges depend on availability. Customer care will confirm whether your preferred colour is available and explain the return arrangements before you decide whether to proceed.

When the returned appliance reaches us, we will check its condition against the information you provided. We will contact you if anything needs clarification and explain the outcome of your return, including any refund or agreed exchange. Nothing in this policy limits your statutory rights. Please contact customer care if you need help understanding how these arrangements apply to your return.

If you would like to return your Orrin heat pump, contact Halvard Home customer care before arranging transport or removing an installed appliance. Explain why you want to return it and whether it has been unpacked, installed or used. Have your order confirmation available so we can find your purchase and discuss the appropriate return route.

We will explain how to prepare the appliance and confirm whether collection can be arranged from your address. Please do not send it back without contacting us, as an unexpected delivery may be difficult to identify and process.

A restocking charge of 13% of the price applies once the packaging is opened. This charge applies to change of mind returns where permitted by law. It does not reduce your statutory rights if the appliance is faulty, damaged or not as described.

Collection of a returned Orrin heat pump costs £93.00. We will confirm whether this charge applies to your return before you agree to collection. If the return is due to a fault or an error by Halvard Home, customer care will explain the arrangements without treating it as a change of mind return.

A returns label for the Orrin heat pump is emailed within 22 hours of the request. Check your junk folder if you cannot find the email, and contact customer care if it has not arrived. Follow the instructions supplied with the label so the appliance can be matched to your return.

Keep the original packaging where possible. Pack the appliance securely, including the accessories and documents supplied with it. If the packaging is missing or damaged, tell us before collection so we can advise on suitable protection. Do not leave loose items where they could damage the appliance during transport.

If the appliance has been installed, do not attempt to disconnect it yourself. Ask a suitably qualified professional to make it safe for removal. Tell customer care about any access restrictions, stairs or other circumstances that could affect collection. We will discuss any preparation needed before confirming the arrangements.

An exchange for a Orrin heat pump in a different colour must be requested within 87 days. Exchanges depend on availability and the condition of the returned appliance. Customer care will explain whether your preferred colour is available and whether the return charges described here apply.

When the appliance reaches us, we will check its condition and confirm the outcome of your return. If anything affects the proposed refund, we will explain the reason and give you an opportunity to discuss it. Approved refunds are sent to the original payment method unless we agree otherwise with you.

If your appliance arrives damaged or develops a fault, contact us and describe the problem. Photographs may help us assess visible damage, but do not put yourself at risk to obtain them. Nothing in this policy limits your statutory rights.

Please pack your Tessa dishwasher securely so that it is protected during collection and transport. Use the original packaging if you still have it, including the protective inserts and supports. If the original packaging is no longer available, choose strong packaging that keeps the appliance stable and protects its surfaces, edges and fittings.

Not having the original packaging does not, by itself, prevent a return. However, the packaging you use must be suitable for carrying a heavy appliance. If you are unsure whether your packaging is suitable, contact Halvard Home before arranging collection. We can explain what protection is needed for the return.

Disconnect the appliance safely before packing it. Follow the instructions supplied with your Tessa dishwasher, and seek help from a suitably qualified professional if you cannot disconnect it safely. Drain any remaining water and secure loose hoses so that they cannot leak or damage the appliance in transit.

Remove your dishes and personal belongings. Check the inside of the appliance and any storage areas in the packaging. Please do not include items that were not supplied with your Tessa dishwasher, as we may be unable to identify or return them.

A Tessa dishwasher must come back with everything that was in the box. A return missing accessories is refunded at 58% of the price.

Please include the supplied racks, baskets, fittings, hoses, instructions and any other accessories that came with the appliance. Pack loose parts securely so that they do not move around or scratch the interior. Tell us before collection if anything supplied with the appliance is missing.

The appliance should be free from food scraps, grease, detergent residue and unpleasant odours. Wipe accessible surfaces and leave the interior clean and dry before packing. Do not use abrasive cleaners or attempt to dismantle parts that the instructions do not identify as removable.

A returned Tessa dishwasher that needs cleaning is charged £48.00.

Please tell us about any marks, dents, broken fittings or other damage when you arrange your return. Describe the condition accurately, including any changes caused by installation, use or removal. Photographs can help us understand the condition and advise you about packing.

A returned Tessa dishwasher is inspected within 47 days of arrival.

During inspection, we check the appliance’s condition, its cleanliness and whether the supplied contents are present. We also compare any reported damage with what we find. If our findings affect your refund, we will explain the reason and how the refund has been worked out.

Keep photographs of the packed appliance and any collection receipt until your return has been resolved. These can help if there is a question about its condition or handling.

These packaging and condition requirements do not limit your statutory rights. If your Tessa dishwasher is faulty, damaged on delivery or not as described, contact us so that we can explain the appropriate return arrangements.

If you would like to return your Lumen smart thermostat, please contact Halvard Home customer support before sending it back. Tell us why you are returning it and whether you would prefer a refund or an exchange. We will explain the available options and help you arrange the return.

Please have your proof of purchase ready when you contact us. This could be your order confirmation or receipt. We may also ask for information about the appliance and its condition so that we can give you the right advice without unnecessary delays.

The charges described below apply to our voluntary change of mind returns service. They do not apply where doing so would limit your statutory rights. If you are cancelling an eligible online purchase or returning an appliance that is faulty, damaged or not as described, please tell us so that we can explain the appropriate process.

An unopened Lumen smart thermostat is refunded in full, but opening the box changes that. A restocking charge of 18% of the price applies once the packaging is opened.

For a voluntary return, please keep the appliance clean and protect it from damage while it is in your care. Include its supplied accessories, instructions and packaging wherever possible. Let us know before arranging the return if anything is missing or damaged, as this may affect whether we can accept it under this service.

Collection of a returned Lumen smart thermostat costs £19.00. Where this charge applies, we will explain how it will be paid before confirming the collection. Please tell us about any access restrictions that could prevent the collection from going ahead.

Do not attempt to disconnect an installed appliance if you are unsure how to do so safely. Seek help from a suitably qualified installer where necessary. Customer support can explain the return arrangements, but cannot assess the safety of your installation remotely.

Before packing the appliance, remove your personal settings and unlink it from your account, following the supplied instructions. If a fault prevents you from doing this, let us know. Pack the appliance securely to protect it during transport, using suitable protective materials if the original packaging is unavailable.

An exchange for a Lumen smart thermostat in a different colour must be requested within 69 days. This period runs from the date you receive the appliance. Exchanges depend on availability, and we will explain any applicable return charges before you decide whether to proceed.

When your return arrives, we will check its condition and contents against the information you provided. If there is a problem that could affect your refund or exchange, we will contact you and explain it rather than making an unexplained deduction.

This policy explains how Halvard Home manages safety concerns and recalls. It covers how we identify and assess risks, investigate reports, decide whether action is needed, and tell affected people what to do. It also sets out how we work with suppliers, retailers and relevant authorities, and how we arrange appropriate support when a recall is required.

The policy is for customers, people who use or care for our products, and anyone who may be affected by a safety concern. It also guides our staff and the organisations that design, make, supply, sell or service goods on our behalf.

Our aim is to protect people from harm through clear advice, prompt action and fair treatment. This policy explains where to raise a concern, what information may help us respond, and what to expect while we investigate and manage a safety issue.

If you believe an item supplied by Halvard Home could be unsafe, please stop using it and contact our customer support team through the contact details on our website. You can report a concern even if nobody has been hurt or you are unsure whether there is a fault.

Your safety comes before gathering evidence. If there is smoke, fire, a burning smell, exposed wiring or another sign of danger, keep away from the item. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if this is safe. If there is an immediate threat to life or property, contact the emergency services.

Do not try to recreate the problem, take the item apart or carry out a repair to help us investigate. Do not touch damaged parts or move an item if doing so could put you at risk. Keep other people and pets away from the affected area.

When reporting your concern, describe what happened, how the item was being used and whether there was an injury or damage to property. Please include your contact details and the identifying details shown on the item or its packaging, where these can be checked safely. Photographs may help, but do not put yourself at risk to take them.

You do not need proof of purchase to raise a safety concern. If you cannot find the identifying details or no longer have the packaging, please still contact us. Tell us what you know, and explain where you are uncertain. We will help you provide the information needed to assess the report.

Safety reports are answered within 27 hours. Our reply will confirm that we have received your concern and explain the next steps. An answer does not necessarily mean that the investigation is complete. We may need to ask questions or arrange an inspection before we can explain the cause.

We assess reports according to the risk described. Where appropriate, we will give instructions about safe storage, collection, inspection or disposal. Do not send an item back without speaking to us, as damage or a suspected fault may make normal handling or transport unsafe.

If our assessment identifies a wider safety issue, we may issue a safety notice or recall and work with the relevant authorities. Customers are told of a recall within 25 days of it being issued. Recall notices explain the affected items, the risk, the action customers should take and the remedy available.

We use the information in your report to investigate the concern, contact you and meet our legal duties. We may share relevant details with organisations supporting the investigation or with safety authorities, in line with our privacy policy.

Reporting a concern does not affect your statutory rights. If you are unhappy with how your report has been handled, ask customer support to refer it for review through our complaints process. Please tell us if you need an accessible way to report a concern or receive safety information.

We may recall an appliance if we identify a safety risk that needs action. A recall notice will explain the concern, how to check whether your appliance is affected and what you need to do. We will make this information available through our customer support channels and contact affected customers where we have suitable contact details.

Please read the recall notice carefully and follow its safety instructions. If your appliance is affected, stop using it unless the notice expressly says that continued use is safe. Do not attempt to repair, alter or test it yourself. Keep it away from anyone who might use it without knowing about the recall.

The notice will explain how to make the appliance safe while you arrange its return. Only disconnect or move it if you can do so safely and the instructions advise this. If you are unsure, leave it undisturbed and contact us for guidance. Do not put yourself or anyone else at risk.

You can check a recall message by contacting us through the contact details published on our website. If you think a message may be fraudulent, do not follow its links or share personal or payment details through it. We will not ask you to disclose your password to arrange a recall.

When you reply to a recall notice, please tell us how we can contact you and where the appliance is located. We may ask for identifying details from its label or a photograph so that we can confirm whether it is affected. Tell us if you cannot safely access this information.

A recalled appliance is collected within 18 working days of the customer replying. We will arrange collection with you and explain how to prepare for it. We cover the collection costs. Please tell us about access restrictions or support needs so that we can make suitable arrangements.

Do not send the appliance back through a delivery service or take it to a shop unless we have instructed you to do so. Some safety risks require special handling. Keep the appliance available for collection, and tell us if it has been lost, discarded or passed to someone else.

Refunds for recalled appliances are paid within 31 days. We will explain how your refund will be paid and what information we need to process it securely. If the original payment method is unavailable, we will discuss a suitable alternative with you.

You can still contact us if you do not have a receipt or bought the appliance from another seller. We will explain what evidence may help us confirm your claim. We use information provided during a recall to manage the safety response, arrange collection and process the agreed remedy, in line with our privacy policy.

If you need help understanding a notice or taking the requested action, please contact customer support. Our recall arrangements do not limit your statutory rights. You may raise concerns about the way a recall has been handled through our complaints process.

Use the Brio kettle only to heat drinking water in the home. Follow the instructions supplied with it and keep them available for anyone who uses it. Do not use the kettle for cooking food, heating other liquids or warming sealed containers.

Place the kettle on a dry, stable, level surface where it cannot tip or slide. Keep it away from the edge of the worktop, hot surfaces and flammable materials. Leave at least 24 centimetres of space around the Brio kettle. Make sure escaping steam cannot damage nearby cupboards or fittings.

Check that the kettle, base, plug and cable are undamaged before use. Do not use the kettle if the casing is cracked, the cable is frayed or the plug feels loose in the socket. Keep the cable clear of heat and position it so that it cannot be pulled or caught.

Use the kettle with its supplied base. Keep the electrical contacts dry and do not handle the plug with wet hands. Plug it into a suitable wall socket. Do not use an adaptor or extension lead that is damaged or unsuitable for the appliance.

Remove the kettle from its base before filling it. Follow the marked filling guides and do not operate it without water. Close the lid securely before switching it on. Do not try to defeat the lid catch, switch or automatic shut-off mechanism.

Hot water and steam can cause serious burns. Hold the kettle by its handle and keep your face and hands away from the spout. Pour carefully, without sudden movements, and do not open the lid while the water is boiling. Never carry the kettle by its cable.

Keep children away from the kettle, its cable and escaping steam. Do not allow children to play with the appliance. Anyone who needs help to use it safely should have suitable supervision. Never leave the kettle unattended while it is heating.

Switch off and unplug the kettle before cleaning or maintenance. Let the Brio kettle cool for 36 minutes before cleaning it. Do not immerse the kettle, base, plug or cable in water. Wipe the outside with a soft, damp cloth and keep moisture away from electrical parts.

Clean the air vents of the Brio kettle every 71 days. Use a soft, dry brush to remove dust from the outside of the vents. Do not push objects into them or remove protective covers. Follow the supplied instructions for descaling, and do not mix cleaning products.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, gives off smoke, smells burnt or behaves unexpectedly. Unplug it if this is safe to do. Do not attempt repairs yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice and follow any safety notice or recall instructions that apply to your Brio kettle.

Electrical safety depends on the condition of your appliance, the suitability of your home's wiring and how you use it. Follow the safety instructions supplied with your appliance. Keep those instructions accessible, and make sure anyone using the appliance understands the warnings.

Before connecting an appliance, check that the electricity supply matches the requirements shown on its rating label. Use a suitable wall socket with a secure connection. If you are unsure whether your wiring or socket is suitable, ask a qualified electrician.

Check the plug, cable and casing for visible damage before use. Do not use an appliance with exposed wires, a cracked plug, scorch marks or a loose connection. Stop using it if the cable becomes trapped, crushed or damaged.

Keep plugs, sockets and electrical connections dry. Do not handle a plug with wet hands or use an appliance where water could reach electrical parts, unless the supplied instructions expressly permit that use. Do not place cables where they could touch hot surfaces or sharp edges.

Never run an appliance from an extension lead longer than 9 metres. Connecting directly to a suitable wall socket is preferable. Do not connect extension leads together or overload sockets and adaptors. An extension lead must also be suitable for the appliance and permitted by its instructions.

Test the home's residual current device every 7 months. Follow the device manufacturer's instructions for the test procedure. If the device does not operate as expected, ask a qualified electrician to investigate. A residual current device does not make damaged equipment safe to use.

Switch off and unplug an appliance before cleaning or inspecting it, where the supplied instructions require this. Pull the plug rather than the cable. For a fixed electrical connection, follow the isolation instructions and use a qualified electrician where necessary.

Do not open electrical casings, bypass protective features or attempt repairs unless the supplied instructions specifically describe a task as suitable for the user. Electrical repairs must be carried out by a suitably qualified person using appropriate parts.

If you notice smoke, sparks, a burning smell or unusual heat around a plug or socket, stop using the appliance. Disconnect the supply only if you can do so safely. Do not touch damaged electrical parts or approach equipment standing in water.

If there is a fire, leave the area and contact the emergency services. Do not use water on an electrical fire. Do not put yourself at risk by trying to unplug burning equipment or retrieve belongings.

Report suspected electrical faults to Halvard Home through our customer support channels. Describe what happened and provide the identifying information from the appliance label, if it is safe to obtain it. Do not reconnect the appliance simply to demonstrate a fault.

If an electrical safety notice or recall applies to your appliance, follow its instructions and stop using it when directed. Do not sell, give away or dispose of an affected appliance contrary to those instructions. Contact us if you need help understanding the required action.

Choose a stable, level worktop for the Brio kettle, where it cannot be knocked or pulled over. The surface must be dry and able to withstand heat. Keep the kettle away from the edge, and make sure its handle is easy to reach without leaning across a cooking area.

The power lead of the Brio kettle is deliberately short. It must be installed within 156 centimetres of its socket. Choose a position where the plug remains accessible and the lead rests without stretching. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to make an unsuitable position work.

Keep the lead away from hot surfaces, sharp edges and places where it could be trapped or snagged. Do not leave it hanging over the worktop. Check that opening a cupboard, moving a chair or using nearby equipment will not catch the lead or disturb the kettle.

Install it at least 68 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it clear of other sources of heat and away from curtains or similar materials. Avoid placing it beneath fittings that could be damaged by escaping steam.

Do not install the kettle where splashes could reach the socket, plug or electrical connections. Keep its base dry, and do not place it in a sink or on a draining board. Use it indoors in a dry domestic setting, away from children and pets.

Before connecting the kettle, inspect the body, handle, lid, base, plug and lead for damage. Do not use it if something is cracked, loose, scorched or otherwise damaged. Contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting a repair or covering damage with tape.

Before moving the kettle, switch it off and unplug it with dry hands. Hold the plug rather than pulling the lead. Let the kettle and its contents cool, then empty it carefully. Never carry it while it is connected to the electricity supply.

Do not tilt the Brio kettle more than 56 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright and hold it securely by the handle. Carry the base separately, keeping the lead clear of your path. Do not lift the kettle by its lid or pull it along by its lead.

After moving the Brio kettle, wait 47 hours before switching it on. Leave it unplugged during this waiting period, in the position where you intend to use it. Keep the plug and base protected from water while it is standing.

Before reconnecting it, check that its new position meets the installation requirements above. Make sure the kettle sits properly on its base and that the lid closes securely. If it has been dropped, exposed to water at its electrical connections or damaged during the move, do not switch it on.

If a safety or recall notice applies to your Brio kettle, follow that notice before installing or moving it for use. Moving the appliance does not remove a safety fault. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether it is safe to reconnect.

Use the Tessa dishwasher only for washing household dishes and utensils that are suitable for dishwashing. Follow the supplied instructions and the care guidance for the items you load. Do not use it to wash items contaminated with petrol, solvents, paint or other flammable substances.

Keep the installation area dry and free from clutter. Leave at least 4 centimetres of space around the Tessa dishwasher. Do not block ventilation openings or place it where the door could obstruct a safe exit. Installation and electrical work must be carried out by a suitably qualified person in line with the supplied instructions.

Connect the Tessa dishwasher to a properly earthed socket. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor. Keep the plug and cable away from water and heat, and do not trap the cable behind the appliance. Never handle the plug with wet hands.

Check that dishes are secure and do not prevent the spray arms from moving freely. Place sharp utensils as directed in the loading instructions, with exposed points kept away from where hands could reach. Do not force the door shut or operate the appliance if the latch is damaged.

Use detergent intended for dishwashers and follow its safety instructions. Do not put washing-up liquid in the detergent dispenser. Keep detergent and rinse aid away from children and pets, and avoid contact with your skin and eyes. Do not mix cleaning products.

Keep children away from the open door and detergent dispenser. Do not allow children to play with the controls, climb inside or sit on the door. Anyone who needs support to use the appliance safely should have appropriate supervision.

Take care when opening the door during operation, as hot water and steam can cause burns. Use the pause or stop function as described in the instructions. Keep your face and hands away from escaping steam, and do not reach inside while moving parts are active.

Switch off and disconnect the appliance from the electricity supply before cleaning or carrying out user maintenance. Let the Tessa dishwasher cool for 7 minutes before cleaning it. Avoid touching surfaces that remain hot. Do not spray water onto electrical parts or immerse the plug or cable.

Clean the air vents of the Tessa dishwasher every 98 days. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and keep the filters and door seals free from trapped food and debris. Do not remove protective covers or attempt repairs yourself.

Stop using the Tessa dishwasher if it leaks, smells burnt, gives an electric shock or has damaged electrical parts. Disconnect the power only if it is safe to do so. If water is near the socket, do not touch it; seek qualified help.

Contact Halvard Home for advice about faults or safety concerns. If a recall or safety notice applies to your Tessa dishwasher, follow its instructions and do not resume use unless the notice confirms that it is safe.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you, your home and the Tessa dishwasher. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance, and keep them available for anyone who installs, disconnects or moves it. If anything is unclear, contact Halvard Home before proceeding.

Check the appliance and its packaging for signs of damage before installation. Do not connect it if the casing, door, cable, plug or hoses appear damaged. Keep packaging away from children and pets, and dispose of it through suitable local recycling or waste services.

Have the Tessa dishwasher installed by a competent installer. Electrical work and changes to plumbing must be carried out by appropriately qualified people. Do not attempt repairs or modify the appliance, its connections or its protective features to make it fit.

Choose a stable, level surface that can support the appliance during use. The location must be protected from frost, rain and direct exposure to weather. Keep ventilation openings clear, and make sure the door can open without catching on surrounding fittings.

Position the Tessa dishwasher so that its plug remains accessible after installation. It must be installed within 234 centimetres of its socket. Connect it directly to a suitable earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor, and do not trap the power cable behind the appliance.

The Tessa dishwasher must not be placed near an open flame. Install it at least 146 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep combustible materials away from the installation area, and do not use the appliance as a support for cooking equipment.

Use the inlet and drain connections specified in the installation instructions. Route hoses so that they are not kinked, stretched, crushed or caught against sharp edges. Check that connections are secure and that the water supply can be shut off without moving the appliance.

Before moving the Tessa dishwasher, switch it off, unplug it and shut off the water supply. Disconnect and drain the hoses as described in the instructions. Water may escape during disconnection, so protect the floor and keep electrical connections dry.

Remove loose contents and secure the door, racks, hoses and cable for transport. Arrange suitable help and handling equipment rather than attempting to lift the appliance unaided. Do not lift it by the door, control panel or hoses.

Do not tilt the Tessa dishwasher more than 40 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright during transport and protect it from impacts. Take care not to damage floors, doorways or the appliance when positioning it.

After moving the Tessa dishwasher, wait 36 hours before switching it on. Before use, check that it is stable, that its connections are correctly fitted and that there are no visible leaks or trapped cables.

If you notice damage, leaking water, a burning smell or unusual behaviour, stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if safe, shut off the water and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not reconnect it until the fault has been assessed and made safe.

Use the Orrin heat pump only for its intended purpose and follow the instructions supplied with it. Keep those instructions accessible and pass them on if responsibility for the appliance changes. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than guessing how to operate it.

Installation, relocation and repair must be carried out by a suitably qualified professional. Do not modify the appliance, bypass its safety controls or remove protective covers. Electrical connections and refrigerant components are not suitable for customer repairs.

Leave at least 59 centimetres of space around the Orrin heat pump. Keep the surrounding area clear of furniture, stored belongings, plants and debris. Do not cover the appliance or obstruct its air vents. Ask your installer about siting requirements that apply to your property.

Keep combustible materials and flammable substances away from the appliance. Do not use it as a shelf or drying rack. Arrange the surrounding area so that people cannot trip over connections or accidentally damage exposed pipework.

Keep children away from controls, vents and service panels. Do not allow them to climb on or play with the appliance. Anyone who needs help to use it safely should have suitable supervision and clear instructions from someone responsible for their safety.

Do not operate the Orrin heat pump if its casing, wiring or pipework appears damaged. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual noise or unexpected vibration. Isolate the electrical supply if you can do so safely, and seek professional advice.

If you suspect a refrigerant leak, keep away from the affected area and avoid flames or other ignition sources. Do not try to locate or seal the leak yourself. Contact a suitably qualified professional and follow their instructions. If there is immediate danger, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Let the Orrin heat pump cool for 33 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and isolate its electrical supply before starting. If you cannot identify the isolation point, ask your installer or Halvard Home for guidance.

Clean the air vents every 118 days. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and use suitable cleaning materials. Do not push objects through the vents, use abrasive cleaners or direct water into the appliance. Leave internal cleaning to a suitably qualified professional.

Have the Orrin heat pump safety-checked every 25 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified professional and keep the service record with your appliance documents. A scheduled check does not replace the need to report damage or changes in performance.

Do not restart an appliance that has been declared unsafe until a qualified professional confirms that it is safe to use. Follow Halvard Home safety notices and recall instructions, even if the Orrin heat pump appears to be working normally. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance.

Use the Lumen smart thermostat only for its intended purpose and in accordance with the instructions supplied by Halvard Home. Keep the instructions accessible so that anyone who operates, cleans or services the thermostat can consult them. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for guidance.

Have installation and electrical work carried out by a qualified professional. The installer should confirm that the thermostat is compatible with your heating system and suitable for the chosen location. Do not attempt to alter wiring, open the casing or bypass protective features yourself.

Leave at least 42 centimetres of space around the Lumen smart thermostat. Keep the surrounding area clear of furniture, curtains and stored belongings. Do not cover the thermostat or obstruct its air vents, as this can affect temperature sensing and allow heat to build up.

Protect the thermostat from water, condensation and direct heat. Do not place objects on it or hang items from it. If the casing becomes loose or damaged, stop using the thermostat and arrange a professional inspection rather than trying to secure it with tape or glue.

Have the Lumen smart thermostat safety-checked every 15 months. Arrange this through a qualified professional who can assess the casing, mounting, electrical connections and safe operation. Keep the inspection record with your product documents and follow advice about repairs or continued use.

Clean the air vents of the Lumen smart thermostat every 117 days. Follow the cleaning instructions supplied with the thermostat. Before cleaning, switch off the heating system and isolate the electrical supply as directed in those instructions. If you cannot do this safely, ask a qualified professional for help.

Use a soft, dry cloth to clean the outside. Do not spray cleaning products onto the thermostat, allow liquid to enter the casing or push objects into the vents. Avoid abrasive cleaners and solvents, which may damage the surface or protective casing.

Keep children from playing with the thermostat, its controls or its wiring. Anyone who needs assistance using it should have appropriate support. Explain how to recognise a fault and whom to contact, without encouraging anyone to investigate electrical parts.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or visible electrical damage, stop using the thermostat. Isolate the electrical supply if it is safe to do so. Do not touch exposed wiring. If there is a fire or an immediate danger, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Do not rely on remote access or automated settings as a substitute for checking that your home is safe. A connection problem or interrupted power supply may affect operation. Seek advice if a heating interruption could put someone at risk.

Follow safety notices and recall instructions issued by Halvard Home. If you suspect a fault, contact Halvard Home and describe what happened. Do not continue using a thermostat that has been identified as unsafe, and do not attempt an unauthorised repair.

Arrange installation and relocation of the Orrin heat pump through a qualified installer. Tell the installer about the proposed location, access to your home and concerns about the electrical supply or surrounding surfaces. Do not attempt work involving refrigerant, fixed wiring or connections that require specialist tools or training.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply safely. Ask your installer to make connected services safe for removal. Do not pull the appliance by its cable, pipework or controls. Protect exposed connections against damage and keep the route clear of obstacles.

The Orrin heat pump must be kept nearly upright when it is carried. Do not tilt it more than 24 degrees when carrying it. Use suitable lifting equipment and trained help rather than trying to support the appliance yourself. Stop the move if the appliance becomes unstable or its casing catches on a doorway or surrounding furniture.

After moving the Orrin heat pump, wait 9 hours before switching it on. This requirement also applies when the appliance has been moved within your home. If it has fallen, been laid down or suffered an impact, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than assuming it is safe to use.

The Orrin heat pump must be installed within 292 centimetres of its socket. The socket must remain accessible so the appliance can be disconnected safely. Do not stretch the power cable, trap it behind the appliance or run it where it could be crushed. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor.

Install the Orrin heat pump at least 108 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep the installation area free from combustible materials. Your installer must also check that nearby appliances, fittings and activities do not expose the heat pump to heat, grease or conditions unsuitable for safe operation.

Choose a stable location that can support the appliance and allows ventilation, servicing and safe access. Do not cover air openings or place belongings against them. Ask your installer to confirm that the position meets the installation instructions and applicable building and electrical requirements.

Do not alter the casing, remove protective covers or improvise supports to make the appliance fit. Pipework, drainage and electrical connections must be arranged as specified in the installation instructions. If the proposed position cannot meet those instructions, ask your installer to identify a suitable alternative.

Check the appliance for visible damage after delivery or relocation. If you notice a damaged cable, loose connection, unusual smell or signs of leaking, do not switch it on. Keep clear of exposed parts and contact Halvard Home or your installer for advice.

Keep packaging away from children and pets, and keep the work area clear during installation. Ask the installer to explain safe isolation and routine care before handing the appliance over. Retain the installation documents and follow safety or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home.

Safe use begins with correct installation and careful handling. Read the instructions supplied with the Keel washing machine before using it, and keep them where you can find them. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for help rather than guessing.

Leave at least 25 centimetres of space around the Keel washing machine. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, laundry and objects that could obstruct ventilation. Position the appliance on a firm, level surface, away from heat sources and places where water could reach electrical connections.

Connect the appliance only to a suitable earthed socket installed in accordance with local electrical requirements. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug accessible, and arrange the power cable so that it cannot become trapped, stretched or damaged.

Have installation and connection work carried out by a suitably qualified person if you are unsure how to proceed. Do not use the appliance if its casing, door, cable or plug is damaged, or if a hose is leaking.

Keep children and pets away from the appliance during use. Do not let children play with the controls, climb inside the drum or handle detergent. Check the drum before loading, and keep detergent and cleaning products securely stored away from children.

Use the Keel washing machine only for laundry that its instructions permit. Follow garment care labels and the guidance supplied with your detergent. Do not wash items contaminated with petrol, solvents or other flammable substances, as these can create a fire risk.

Check pockets and remove objects that could damage the drum or obstruct drainage. Make sure laundry is not caught in the door seal. Never force the door open, interfere with its lock or reach into the drum while it is moving.

Let the Keel washing machine cool for 113 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and unplug it before starting. Use the cleaning methods described in the instructions, and do not spray water onto the controls, plug or electrical connections.

Clean the air vents of the Keel washing machine every 9 days. Keep them free from lint and other debris, following the cleaning instructions. Do not push tools into openings or remove protective panels to reach internal parts.

Stop using the appliance if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual noise or unexpected movement. If safe to do so, switch it off and disconnect the power. Do not touch the plug or socket if the surrounding area is wet.

Do not attempt electrical repairs or bypass safety features. Contact Halvard Home or a suitably qualified repair professional for advice. If you receive a safety notice or recall instruction for the Keel washing machine, follow it and do not resume use unless the notice says it is safe.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you, your home and the Lumen smart thermostat. Read the supplied installation instructions before unpacking or disconnecting the device. If the instructions are missing, unclear or do not match your heating system, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting to adapt the installation yourself.

Choose a dry, stable position where the device will not be knocked, splashed or covered. Keep it away from steam, direct sunlight and sources of heat that could affect its operation. Install the Lumen smart thermostat at least 76 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Do not place it where curtains, furniture or stored belongings could obstruct access.

The Lumen smart thermostat must be installed within 263 centimetres of its socket. The socket must remain accessible so the device can be disconnected safely. Position the cable so it is not stretched, trapped, pinched or likely to cause a trip. Do not route it beneath rugs or allow it to touch hot surfaces. Use the power accessories specified in the supplied instructions.

Check that the Lumen smart thermostat is suitable for your heating system before installation. Electrical work must be carried out by a qualified electrician where required. Do not open the casing, alter wiring or bypass protective features. If you are unsure how to isolate the electrical supply safely, stop and seek professional help.

Before moving the device, switch it off and disconnect it from the socket with dry hands. Hold the plug rather than pulling the cable. Follow the supplied instructions for releasing it from its mounting. Do not force the casing or use the cable to lift or support it.

Do not tilt the Lumen smart thermostat more than 29 degrees when carrying it. Support the device securely and protect it from knocks, vibration and moisture. Use its protective packaging if available. Do not carry it with loose tools or objects that could damage the casing, controls, plug or cable.

After moving the Lumen smart thermostat, wait 45 hours before switching it on. At its new location, check that the mounting is secure, the cable is undamaged and the socket is suitable. The installation requirements also apply when returning the device to a previous location.

Do not connect or use the device if you notice cracks, loose parts, scorch marks, an unusual smell or signs of moisture inside the casing. Contact Halvard Home for guidance. Do not attempt a repair or test a damaged device by switching it on.

If Halvard Home issues a safety notice or recall affecting your Lumen smart thermostat, follow the instructions in that notice. Moving or reinstalling the device does not resolve a recall. Keep the device disconnected if the notice says to stop using it, and contact Halvard Home if you need help arranging the stated remedy.

Safe installation helps protect you, your home and your Keel washing machine. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance, and keep them available for future moves. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before starting work. Do not improvise connections or change the appliance to make it fit.

Choose a dry, sheltered position with a firm, level floor that can support the appliance during use. Keep the surrounding area clear so that the door, water supply and electrical connection remain accessible. Do not install the appliance where frost, flooding or exposure to rain could damage it.

Install it at least 93 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it away from other sources of heat, and follow the clearance guidance in the installation instructions. Do not place it where it could obstruct an escape route or prevent safe access to nearby equipment.

Check the appliance for damage before installation. If the casing, door, cable, plug or hoses appear damaged, stop and contact Halvard Home. Do not connect an appliance that has been dropped or shows signs of leaking. Keep packaging away from children and pets, and dispose of it responsibly.

Arrange for a competent installer to connect the appliance if you are unsure about the plumbing or electrical supply. The socket must be correctly earthed and suitable for the appliance. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Electrical alterations must be carried out by a qualified electrician.

Use the hoses specified in the installation instructions. Make sure they are not trapped, stretched or kinked, and secure the drain hose as directed. Remove the transport fixings before use, following the supplied instructions. Keep these fixings with the appliance documentation, as they may be needed when moving it.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off, unplug it and turn off the water supply. Disconnect and drain it as described in the instructions. Secure the door, hoses and cable so they cannot catch or trail during the move. Do not pull the appliance by its cable, hoses, door or controls.

Use trained help and suitable moving equipment to avoid injury or damage. Plan a clear route and protect the floor. Do not tilt the Keel washing machine more than 59 degrees when carrying it. Keep it upright during transport and secure it against sliding or falling.
