After moving the Keel washing machine, wait 44 hours before switching it on. During this wait, check that it is correctly positioned, stable and connected in line with the installation instructions. Check that transport fixings have been removed before use.

If the appliance leaks, moves unexpectedly or makes an unusual noise after installation, stop using it. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if this is safe, and turn off the water supply. Do not attempt repairs yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice before using it again.

Use the Ashby tumble dryer only as described in its instruction manual. Follow the care labels on clothing and household fabrics, and do not tumble dry items marked as unsuitable. If you are unsure whether an item is suitable, leave it out and check with its manufacturer.

Install the dryer on a stable surface in a suitable, ventilated space. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, clothing and other materials that could obstruct airflow. Do not cover the dryer or use it where doors, curtains or furnishings could block its ventilation.

Connect the dryer to a suitable wall socket, following the installation instructions. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug and socket accessible, and do not use the appliance if its cable, plug or casing is damaged. Electrical repairs must be carried out by a qualified professional.

Check pockets and remove objects before loading the drum. Do not dry items contaminated with cooking oil, solvents, fuel, wax or other flammable substances. Washing may not remove these substances completely. Follow the manual’s restrictions on materials such as foam and rubber.

Load the drum so that fabrics can move freely, following the guidance in the manual. Do not force the door shut. Choose a programme suitable for the fabric, and allow the cooling stage to finish. Do not leave warm laundry piled together where heat could build up.

Stay at home and remain awake while the dryer is operating. Keep children and pets away from the appliance, and check that the drum is clear before closing the door. Do not allow children to play with the controls or climb inside.

Let the Ashby tumble dryer cool for 111 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and unplug it before cleaning, and check that the drum and accessible surfaces are cool enough to touch safely. Follow the manual’s cleaning instructions and avoid getting electrical parts wet.

After drying, remove lint from the filter as directed in the manual. Refit the filter securely before using the appliance. Do not operate the dryer with a missing or damaged filter, and do not allow lint to collect around the appliance.

Clean the air vents of the Ashby tumble dryer every 64 days. Keep the vents unobstructed between cleans. If you notice a blockage, stop using the appliance and remove it safely in accordance with the manual.

Have the Ashby tumble dryer safety-checked every 27 months. Arrange this through a qualified service professional. Do not wait for a scheduled check if the appliance develops a fault or behaves unusually.

Stop using the dryer if you notice a burning smell, unusual noise, overheating or damage. Contact Halvard Home for advice. If there is smoke or fire, leave the door closed, get everyone outside and call the emergency services. Do not attempt repairs yourself or use an appliance covered by a stop-use recall notice.

Use the Vale fridge freezer only for storing food and drink in the home, following the instructions supplied with it. Keep those instructions accessible for anyone who uses or cares for the appliance. If you are unsure whether it is safe to use, contact Halvard Home for advice.

Place the appliance on a firm, level floor, away from heat sources and direct sunlight. Leave at least 8 centimetres of space around the Vale fridge freezer. Keep ventilation openings clear of packaging, furniture and other obstructions. Do not fit the appliance inside a cupboard unless the installation instructions expressly allow this.

Connect the appliance to an earthed wall socket that matches the electrical requirements shown on its rating label. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug accessible and make sure the power cable is not trapped, stretched or touching hot surfaces. Stop using the appliance if the cable, plug or socket appears damaged.

Have the Vale fridge freezer safety-checked every 31 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified technician. Do not attempt electrical repairs or remove protective covers yourself. A safety check does not replace attention to faults: unusual smells, smoke, sparks or repeated electrical tripping require action rather than continued use.

Clean the air vents of the Vale fridge freezer every 24 days. Switch off and unplug the appliance before cleaning, provided it is safe to reach the plug. Follow the cleaning instructions supplied with the appliance. Do not spray water into vents, controls or electrical parts, and do not use a steam cleaner.

Protect the cooling system from damage. Do not puncture internal surfaces, force tools into openings or use sharp objects to remove ice. Do not use electrical devices or apply heat inside the appliance to speed up defrosting. Follow the supplied defrosting instructions instead.

If you suspect damage to the cooling system, keep flames and ignition sources away. Ventilate the room without operating electrical switches near the appliance, and seek professional advice. Do not try to locate a leak yourself or restart the appliance until a qualified technician confirms that it is safe.

Keep children from climbing on shelves, hanging from doors or playing inside the appliance. Store packaging out of their reach. Position food and containers so that they cannot fall out when the door opens. Keep fingers clear of hinges and closing door edges.

Do not store flammable substances or explosive containers in the appliance. Follow food packaging advice about refrigeration and freezing, and keep raw food covered to prevent contamination. If cooling fails or food appears unsafe, do not taste it to check whether it is suitable to eat.

If the appliance smokes or catches fire, move away and contact the emergency services. Do not use water on an electrical fire. Follow safety notices or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home, including instructions to stop using the appliance. Contact Halvard Home if you need help understanding a notice.

Install and move the Ashby tumble dryer with care. Incorrect positioning, a damaged power lead or a blocked vent can create a risk of fire, electric shock or injury. If you are unsure whether your chosen location is suitable, ask a qualified installer before connecting the appliance.

Choose a dry, stable location where the floor can support the appliance securely. Do not install it where rain, damp or leaking pipes could reach it. Keep the surrounding area clear of packaging, clothing and objects that could obstruct ventilation or prevent the door from opening freely.

The Ashby tumble dryer must not be placed near an open flame. Install it at least 113 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame.

Keep the appliance away from sources of heat and combustible materials. Do not use a cupboard or enclosed space unless the installation instructions supplied with the appliance expressly permit it. Follow those instructions for ventilation, levelling and securing the appliance.

The power lead of the Ashby tumble dryer is deliberately short. It must be installed within 297 centimetres of its socket.

Connect the appliance directly to a suitable, earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to reach a socket. If the socket is unsuitable or cannot be reached without stretching the lead, ask a qualified electrician to arrange a safe connection.

Position the power lead so that it cannot become trapped, crushed or damaged behind the appliance. Keep it away from hot surfaces and sharp edges. The plug must remain accessible so that you can disconnect the appliance safely. Do not connect it if the plug, lead or socket shows signs of damage or overheating.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and unplug it by holding the plug, not pulling the lead. Follow the supplied instructions for disconnecting drainage or ventilation fittings. Secure loose fittings and keep the lead clear of the route you will use.

Arrange suitable help and lifting equipment rather than attempting to carry the appliance alone. Do not lift or pull it by its door, controls or power lead. Protect the appliance from impacts and follow the handling instructions supplied with it.

After moving the Ashby tumble dryer, wait 38 hours before switching it on.

At its new location, check that the appliance stands securely and that its ventilation openings are unobstructed. Check that connections are secure and that the lead has not been trapped during positioning. Remove transport packaging as directed in the installation instructions.

If you notice damage, a burning smell or an electrical fault, do not use the appliance. Disconnect it if safe to do so and contact Halvard Home for advice. Check the safety and recall information for the Ashby tumble dryer before putting it into use, and follow applicable instructions if it is affected by a safety notice or recall.

Use the Corra induction hob only for preparing food in a domestic setting. Read the supplied instructions before use and keep them where you can find them. If anything in the instructions is unclear, contact Halvard Home before using the appliance.

Leave at least 11 centimetres of space around the Corra induction hob. Keep this space clear of packaging, cloths, utensils and other objects. Position the appliance as directed in the installation instructions, away from water and materials that could catch fire.

Installation and electrical work must be carried out by a suitably qualified person. The electrical supply must match the requirements shown on the appliance. Do not use damaged plugs, loose sockets or extension leads. Keep the power cable away from heat and sharp edges.

Use cookware that is suitable for induction cooking and position it securely on the cooking zone. Keep pan bases and the cooking surface clean and dry. Do not heat empty cookware or allow handles to project where they could be knocked.

Stay with the appliance while cooking, particularly when heating oil or fat. Keep children away from the cooking area and prevent pets from reaching the controls or cookware. Do not rely on control locks as a substitute for supervision.

Keep metal objects, such as cutlery and lids, off the cooking surface because they may become hot. Do not use the surface for storage or as a worktop. If you have an implanted medical device, seek advice from your clinician about using induction cooking equipment.

Switch the appliance off using its controls after cooking. Do not rely on pan detection to turn it off. The surface can remain hot after cookware has been removed, so avoid touching it and keep combustible materials away.

Let the Corra induction hob cool for 114 minutes before cleaning it. Check that the surface is cold before touching it, even after this cooling period. Follow the instructions for disconnecting the electrical supply before cleaning. Never immerse the appliance or direct water into its openings.

Clean the air vents of the Corra induction hob every 16 days. Use the cleaning method described in the supplied instructions. Do not push objects into the vents or use steam cleaners, abrasive pads or cleaning products that could damage the surface.

Have the Corra induction hob safety-checked every 6 months. Arrange this through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified service provider. Do not open the casing, modify the appliance or attempt electrical repairs yourself. Keep service records with your appliance documents.

Stop using the appliance if the glass cracks, the cable is damaged, or you notice smoke, sparks or an unusual burning smell. Disconnect the electrical supply if it is safe to do so and contact Halvard Home. Do not resume use until the fault has been assessed and resolved.

If cooking oil catches fire, do not throw water on it or move the pan. Switch off the heat only if you can do so safely. If you cannot safely control the situation, leave the area, keep others away and call the emergency services.

The Vale fridge freezer must be installed and moved with care to protect you, your home and the appliance. Follow the installation guide supplied with it, including its ventilation and positioning requirements. If the guide is missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before proceeding. Do not use the appliance if it appears damaged.

Choose a dry, well-ventilated position away from direct sunlight and sources of heat. Install it at least 118 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep ventilation openings clear and follow the clearance requirements in the installation guide. Do not place the appliance where rain, splashes or damp could reach its electrical parts.

The floor must be firm, level and capable of supporting the appliance when loaded. Check that the delivery route is clear and that doorways, flooring and stairs are suitable for moving it safely. Arrange suitable help and handling equipment. Do not attempt to lift or carry the appliance without assistance, and keep children and pets away from the moving route.

Before moving the appliance, unplug it and remove food, shelves and loose fittings that could fall or cause damage. Defrost and drain it as directed in the user guide. Secure the doors without damaging the seals. Do not lift the appliance by its doors, handles, pipework or power cable. Protect the floor and avoid dragging it across the surface.

Keep the appliance upright during transport and handling. Protect the cooling pipework from knocks, crushing and punctures. If it has been tilted or laid down, leave it unplugged and ask Halvard Home for advice before reconnecting it. Do not guess when it is safe to switch it on.

Once positioned, adjust the feet as described in the installation guide so the appliance is stable and the doors close correctly. Check that the power cable is not trapped beneath the cabinet, stretched or touching hot surfaces. Fit supplied safety restraints where the guide requires them. Do not modify the cabinet, hinges or fittings to make the appliance fit.

Connect the appliance to a suitable earthed wall socket that remains accessible after installation. Do not use an extension lead or socket adaptor. If the plug, cable or socket is damaged, stop and arrange professional assessment. Electrical alterations must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Never remove the earth connection or attempt electrical repairs yourself.

If you hear escaping gas, notice oily residue around damaged cooling pipework or suspect a refrigerant leak, keep flames and ignition sources away. Avoid operating electrical switches in the affected area. Ventilate the space if it is safe to do so, leave the area and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not reconnect or use the appliance until a qualified technician confirms that it is safe.

After installation or a move, check for damage, instability and obstructed ventilation before use. Report concerns to Halvard Home rather than attempting a repair. Keep the installation guide accessible for future moves, servicing and safety checks.

The Corra induction hob must be installed by a qualified installer, with electrical work carried out by a qualified electrician. Do not connect it yourself or alter its wiring. Follow the installation instructions supplied with the appliance and ask Halvard Home for guidance if those instructions are missing or unclear.

Before installation, check the appliance for damaged glass, loose parts, damaged cables or signs of impact. Do not install or connect an appliance that appears damaged. Keep the packaging and contact Halvard Home so that we can explain how to arrange an assessment. Do not attempt to repair damage yourself.

Choose a position where the supporting surface is stable, suitable for the appliance and able to withstand heat. Install it at least 127 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. The installer must also check the surrounding cupboards, wall finishes and fittings against the installation instructions.

Keep ventilation openings clear and make sure that stored items cannot obstruct airflow beneath the appliance. Do not fit the hob where water could reach electrical connections. Cables must be protected from heat, sharp edges and trapping. The electrical supply must be suitable, correctly earthed and fitted with appropriate protection.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off, allow it to cool and have it safely disconnected from the electrical supply. Fixed wiring must be disconnected by a qualified electrician. Remove cookware and loose accessories, and check that the route is clear of obstacles, wet flooring and anything that could cause a fall.

Arrange suitable lifting help and use handling equipment where needed. Do not lift the appliance by its cable, controls or glass edges. Do not tilt the Corra induction hob more than 54 degrees when carrying it. Protect the glass from knocks and avoid dragging the appliance across the worktop or floor.

During transport, secure the appliance so that it cannot slide, fall or strike surrounding objects. Use protective packaging that supports the appliance without pressing against vulnerable parts. Do not place items on the glass. Keep the appliance dry and protected from weather while it is being carried or stored.

After moving the Corra induction hob, wait 17 hours before switching it on. This waiting period does not replace the need for checks after transport. If the appliance has been dropped, struck or exposed to water, leave it disconnected and contact Halvard Home before arranging installation or use.

When the appliance is fitted in its new position, ask the installer to check its supports, ventilation and electrical connection. Do not use it if the glass is cracked, the controls behave unexpectedly, or you notice smoke, sparks or a burning smell. Stop using it and seek advice without touching damaged parts.

Check Halvard Home’s safety and recall information before arranging installation or moving an appliance affected by a safety notice. Follow the instructions in that notice rather than assuming relocation makes the appliance safe. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance.

Use the Fenwick cooker hood to remove cooking fumes in a household kitchen, following the instructions supplied with it. It does not replace safe cooking practices, suitable ventilation or a working smoke alarm. Keep the instructions accessible and pass them on if the appliance changes hands.

Have the appliance installed by a qualified installer. The electrical connection, fixing position and ventilation arrangements must follow the installation instructions and applicable building requirements. Do not alter the wiring, ducting or casing yourself.

Keep ventilation openings clear. If your kitchen contains a fuel-burning appliance, ask a qualified installer to confirm that extraction will not draw combustion gases back into the room. Never rely on the cooker hood to protect you from carbon monoxide.

Stay attentive when cooking, particularly when heating oil or fat. Keep flames away from the hood and do not flambé beneath it. Do not use the appliance as a shelf or hang utensils, cloths or decorations from it.

Accessible surfaces may become hot during cooking. Avoid touching the underside of the hood and keep children away from hot surfaces and moving parts. Do not allow children to play with the controls or carry out cleaning.

Switch the hood off and disconnect it from the electricity supply before cleaning or removing accessible parts. Use the isolation method described in the instructions. Do not pull on the cable, touch electrical connections with wet hands or attempt to reach an inaccessible plug.

Let the Fenwick cooker hood cool for 25 minutes before cleaning it. If surfaces still feel hot, leave them untouched until they have cooled. Use cleaning materials suitable for the surface, as described in the care instructions.

Grease deposits can catch fire. Clean the grease filters and accessible surfaces according to the care instructions, and arrange replacement of filters that cannot be cleaned. Do not operate the hood with required filters missing, damaged or incorrectly fitted.

Keep water and cleaning fluid away from the motor, controls and electrical parts. Do not use steam cleaning equipment or spray cleaner into openings. Refit cleaned parts as instructed and ensure they are dry before reconnecting the electricity supply.

Have the Fenwick cooker hood safety-checked every 13 months. Arrange this through a qualified service professional. A safety check does not replace cleaning, filter care or prompt attention to faults.

Stop using the appliance if it is damaged, behaves unexpectedly, produces a burning smell or makes an unusual noise. Disconnect the electricity supply if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not remove protective covers or attempt internal repairs.

If a fire starts, do not use water on burning oil or fat and do not move the pan. Switch off the cooking heat if it is safe to do so. Leave the area and call the fire and rescue service if there is danger or you are unsure what to do.

Follow safety notices or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home. If a notice tells you to stop using the Fenwick cooker hood, leave it disconnected until the specified corrective action has been completed.

Safe installation and careful handling help protect you from injury, electric shock and fire. Read the installation instructions supplied with the Fenwick cooker hood before starting work. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home for advice rather than guessing how to proceed.

Installation must be carried out by a suitably qualified installer. Electrical work must be handled by a qualified electrician. Do not change the plug, alter the wiring or attempt to repair electrical parts yourself. Keep the cooker hood disconnected from the electricity supply during installation.

The Fenwick cooker hood must be installed within 220 centimetres of its socket. Position it so that the plug remains accessible and the power cable is protected from heat, sharp edges and trapping. Do not stretch the cable to reach the socket or use an extension lead.

Install the Fenwick cooker hood at least 121 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. The installer must also check the hob instructions and applicable building requirements. If these requirements conflict or leave the position uncertain, seek advice before installation continues.

The supporting wall or structure must be suitable for the cooker hood. The installer must check for concealed cables and pipes before drilling and use fixings appropriate to the surface. Do not attach the cooker hood to damaged plaster, loose panels or an unsuitable support.

Ventilation and ducting must follow the installation instructions and applicable regulations. Do not connect the outlet to a flue used by an appliance that burns gas or fuel. Where extraction could affect a fuel-burning appliance, ask a qualified professional to assess ventilation and the risk of fumes entering the room.

Before moving the cooker hood, switch it off and unplug it safely. Let hot surfaces cool before handling. Arrange for a qualified professional to disconnect it if the electrical connection cannot be safely unplugged. Do not pull on the cable or ducting to release it.

Plan the route and clear away obstacles before lifting. Get help with carrying rather than attempting a lift that feels unsafe. Wear protective gloves and support the casing securely. Do not lift the cooker hood by its controls, filters, glass or power cable.

Do not tilt the Fenwick cooker hood more than 30 degrees when carrying it. Protect it against knocks and prevent it from sliding during transport. Keep the cable secured away from places where it could be crushed. Do not place objects on the cooker hood.

After moving the Fenwick cooker hood, wait 26 hours before switching it on. Before reconnecting it, have the installation checked and inspect the casing, plug and cable for damage. Do not use the cooker hood if it is loose, damaged or showing signs of overheating.

If you notice a burning smell, smoke, sparking or unusual vibration, stop using the cooker hood. Disconnect it if this is safe and contact Halvard Home. If a safety notice or recall applies to your cooker hood, follow that notice before arranging installation, moving or reuse.

Use the Mira robot vacuum only for its intended purpose: cleaning suitable indoor household floors. Follow the instructions supplied with it and check that the floor surface is suitable before cleaning. Do not use it outdoors, on wet floors or where it could come into contact with rain, splashes or standing water.

Check the Mira robot vacuum, charging dock, plug and cable for damage before use. Do not use damaged equipment or try to make it work by holding loose parts in place. Stop using it if it behaves unexpectedly, gives off an unusual smell, becomes unusually hot or makes an unfamiliar noise.

Keep the cleaning area clear of loose cables, clothing and objects that could become tangled or be dragged along the floor. Remove sharp debris and anything that could damage the vacuum or its battery. Do not use it to collect hot ash, burning material, liquids or flammable substances.

Keep children and pets away from moving parts and the charging dock. The Mira robot vacuum is not a toy. Do not allow anyone to ride on it, place objects on it or interfere with it while it is moving. Keep hair, loose clothing and fingers away from brushes and openings.

Make sure stairs, ledges and changes in floor level are protected as directed in the instructions. Do not rely on sensors where dirt, damage or the surrounding conditions could affect their operation. Keep the route to the charging dock clear and position the dock where it will not create a trip hazard.

Use only charging equipment and replacement parts approved by Halvard Home for the Mira robot vacuum. Keep the charging area dry and uncovered. Do not handle the plug with wet hands or pull the cable to disconnect it. Keep the cable away from heat and places where it could be trapped or damaged.

Switch off the Mira robot vacuum and unplug the charging dock before cleaning or maintenance. Follow the supplied instructions for removing debris and caring for the brushes, filters and sensors. Do not immerse the vacuum or dock in water, and do not apply cleaning sprays directly to electrical parts.

Clean the air vents of the Mira robot vacuum every 32 days.

Have the Mira robot vacuum safety-checked every 24 months.

Arrange safety checks and repairs through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified repairer. Do not open the battery casing, alter electrical components or bypass protective features. If the battery appears swollen, damaged or leaking, stop using the vacuum and seek advice. Avoid touching leaked material.

If you notice smoke or fire, move away and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk by attempting to move or unplug the equipment.

Check Halvard Home safety notices if you have concerns about the Mira robot vacuum. Follow recall instructions and stop using it if a notice tells you to do so. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether a notice applies or need help using the vacuum safely.

Choose a dry, stable place for the Mira robot vacuum and its charging dock. Keep the area clear of clutter, loose cables and objects that could fall or obstruct its movement. Do not install it where it could block an escape route.

The Mira robot vacuum must be installed within 168 centimetres of its socket. Position the dock so that the plug remains accessible without moving furniture. The power cable must lie safely away from walkways and must not be trapped beneath the dock.

Install the Mira robot vacuum at least 101 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep it away from hot surfaces, splashing water and places where steam or grease collects. Do not place the dock beside combustible materials.

Use the charging equipment supplied for the Mira robot vacuum or replacement equipment approved by Halvard Home. Check that the plug, cable and dock are undamaged before connecting them. Do not use equipment with exposed wiring, scorch marks or a cracked casing.

Plug the dock directly into a suitable wall socket. Do not run its cable beneath a rug or through a doorway where it could be crushed. If the socket is loose, damaged or unusually warm, stop using it and seek advice from a qualified electrician.

Before carrying the Mira robot vacuum, switch it off and disconnect the charging dock from the mains. Hold the plug when disconnecting it; do not pull the cable. Empty the dust container and secure removable parts as described in the user guide.

Do not tilt the Mira robot vacuum more than 51 degrees when carrying it. Support the body securely and keep it upright. Do not lift it by its bumper, cover or charging contacts, and do not carry it while it is operating.

Protect the Mira robot vacuum and its dock from knocks during transport. Use suitable protective packaging and keep the cable secured so that it cannot snag. Do not leave the appliance where it could slide, fall or be crushed.

After moving the Mira robot vacuum, wait 37 hours before switching it on. Keep it switched off and disconnected from charging during this waiting period. Leave it in a dry, stable location away from children and pets.

Before reconnecting the dock, inspect the appliance and charging equipment for damage. Make sure the charging contacts are clean and dry. If the appliance has been dropped, crushed or exposed to water, do not charge it or attempt to test it.

Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether the Mira robot vacuum is safe to install or use after moving. Do not open the casing or attempt electrical repairs yourself. If a safety notice or recall applies to your appliance, follow its instructions before installation, charging or use.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Extended Care/Safety checks under the plan

result.text:
Extended Care includes a free safety check every 23 months. The check is designed to identify concerns that could affect safe use. It does not replace the care instructions supplied with your appliance or remove the need to report a fault that appears unsafe.

We will contact you to arrange your safety check using the contact details held on your membership. Please keep these details up to date and tell us about access needs or other arrangements that would help you receive the service. We will explain how to prepare for the visit.

The engineer will inspect accessible parts, assess relevant safety features and look for signs of damage or unsafe operation. The work will follow the safety guidance that applies to your appliance. Please tell the engineer about unusual smells, sounds, heat, leaks or changes in performance, even if they are not present during the visit.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Keep the surrounding area clear and keep children and pets away from the work area. Do not move heavy equipment, remove covers or disconnect fixed connections yourself. Tell us if access could be difficult so that we can make suitable arrangements.

Extended Care members with a safety concern get an engineer within 7 hours. Contact our support team and make clear that you are reporting a safety concern under Extended Care. Describe what has happened and whether there is smoke, a burning smell, leaking water or another apparent hazard.

Do not wait for an engineer if there is an immediate danger. Stop using the appliance and keep away from the affected area. Disconnect the power only if you can do so safely. If there is fire, smoke or a suspected gas leak, leave the property and contact the emergency services from a safe place.

The engineer will explain the findings in plain language and tell you whether the appliance is safe to use. If a concern is found, they will explain the recommended action and any restrictions on use. Follow those instructions and do not attempt a repair yourself or bypass a safety feature.

A safety check is an assessment of the condition found during the visit, not a guarantee against future faults. Repairs and replacement are handled under the applicable Extended Care terms. We will explain the cover and seek your agreement before arranging work outside it.

If the check identifies an issue linked to a safety notice or recall, we will explain the relevant action and help you follow it. Recall instructions take priority over routine use and maintenance advice. Do not resume using an affected appliance unless the recall guidance or an authorised engineer confirms that it is safe.

We will record the findings and the advice provided so that you can refer to them and our support team can assist you. Please contact us if the explanation is unclear, if your circumstances make the recommended action difficult, or if a safety concern remains unresolved.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Extended Care Plus/Safety checks under the plan

result.text:
Extended Care Plus includes a free safety check every 12 months. The check helps us spot signs that an appliance covered by your plan may be unsafe to use. It does not replace the care and maintenance described in your appliance instructions, or any action required by a safety notice or recall.

We will contact you to arrange your check using the contact details linked to your plan. Please keep these details up to date and tell us about any access needs. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you and explain how to prepare for the engineer’s visit.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Keep the surrounding area clear and let us know about anything that could affect access, such as restricted entry or building work. You do not need to move a heavy appliance or remove a cover yourself.

The engineer will inspect the appliance for visible damage and carry out safety checks appropriate to its design and condition. They may ask about unusual smells, sounds or behaviour. Please tell them about anything that worries you, even if the appliance appears to be working normally.

Extended Care Plus members with a safety concern get an engineer within 42 hours. If you suspect a fault could cause harm, contact us through the support details provided with your plan. Explain what has happened and whether you have stopped using the appliance so we can give you suitable safety advice.

Do not wait for a planned check if you notice a possible danger. Stop using the appliance and disconnect it from the power supply if you can do so safely. Do not touch damaged wiring, attempt a repair or restart the appliance to demonstrate the problem.

If there is smoke, fire or an immediate risk to someone’s safety, move away from the danger and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to unplug an appliance or protect your belongings. Follow the advice given by the emergency services.

After the check, the engineer will explain their findings in plain language. We will provide a record of the outcome and tell you whether further action is needed. If the appliance is unsafe, we will explain what must happen before it can be used again.

A safety check is not a promise that a fault cannot develop. Please continue to follow the appliance instructions and report changes that concern you. A satisfactory check does not cancel a recall or mean that you should disregard a warning issued by Halvard Home.

If the check identifies an issue covered by a recall, we will explain the relevant recall action and how to arrange it. Your right to receive help under a recall does not depend on having Extended Care Plus. Nothing in this plan limits your rights under consumer law.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Scotland North/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you are concerned that an appliance may be unsafe, stop using it and contact Halvard Home through our customer support channels. Tell us what has happened and whether there are signs of overheating, smoke, damage or an unusual smell. Do not attempt a repair yourself.

If there is an immediate danger, move away from the appliance and contact the emergency services. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if this is safe. Do not touch damaged wiring or approach an appliance that is smoking. Follow the advice given by the emergency services.

Urgent safety visits in Scotland North are made within 35 hours. We assess urgency from the information you give us and the safety information available to our team. We will explain how your report has been assessed and confirm the arrangements for a visit.

When you contact us, please describe where the appliance is installed and how our visitor can reach it. Tell us about access restrictions, ferry travel or weather conditions that may affect the journey. We use this information to plan safe access, not to dismiss your concern.

We will agree the visit arrangements with you and explain what to expect. Please tell us if you need communication support, accessible information or an adjustment to help you take part in the visit. You may arrange for someone you trust to be present.

Our visitor will identify themselves and explain why they have come. If you are unsure about their identity, keep the door closed and contact Halvard Home using contact details you trust. Do not rely on details supplied by an unexpected caller.

During the visit, we may inspect the appliance, check its installation and carry out safety tests. Please keep the surrounding area accessible where you can do so safely. Keep children and pets away from the work area, and follow the visitor’s safety instructions.

We will explain what we find in plain language and tell you whether the appliance can be used. If it must remain disconnected, we will make this clear. We will also explain the action we propose and how we will keep you informed.

Recall collections in Scotland North are made within 51 working days. If a collection is needed, we will confirm the arrangements and explain how to prepare safely. Do not move, package or reconnect an unsafe appliance unless our safety team has expressly advised you to do so.

If access becomes unsafe or the agreed arrangements cannot go ahead, we will contact you and explain what happens next. Please let us know if your circumstances change. A missed visit does not mean that an appliance has been cleared for use.

We handle information about your home and circumstances with care and use it to arrange and manage the safety response. If you disagree with our assessment or are unhappy with the visit, contact customer support and ask for your concern to be reviewed.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Scotland South/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
Your safety is important to Halvard Home. If you believe an appliance may be unsafe, stop using it and contact our customer support team. Explain what has happened and tell us about anything that could affect safe access to your home.

If there is smoke, fire or an immediate danger to anyone, move to a safe place and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to disconnect an appliance, inspect a fault or recover belongings. Follow advice from the emergency services.

We assess reported safety concerns using the information you provide and the guidance available to our safety team. We may ask about signs of damage, unusual behaviour or a notice you have received. You do not need to investigate the fault yourself or attempt a repair.

Urgent safety visits in Scotland South are made within 66 hours. We will explain whether your report requires an urgent safety visit and confirm the arrangements with you. Our team will also give you advice about keeping the affected appliance safely out of use.

When arranging access, please tell us about communication needs, mobility needs or anything else that may affect the visit. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you. You can ask for a trusted person to be present if that would help you feel comfortable.

Our visiting representative will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit. If you are unsure who is at your door, keep it closed and contact Halvard Home through a contact route you trust. You should not feel pressured to allow access.

During the visit, we may inspect the appliance, make it safe or explain why it must remain out of use. We will describe what we find in clear language and tell you what happens next. Do not restart it unless we confirm that it is safe.

Recall collections in Scotland South are made within 45 working days. If a collection is required, we will confirm the arrangements and explain how to prepare. Do not move, dismantle or package an unsafe appliance unless our safety team has told you how to do so safely.

Please tell us if access arrangements change or if you cannot safely follow our instructions. We will work with you to resolve the difficulty. Keep children and pets away from the affected appliance, and leave the route to it clear where this is safe.

We will explain the remedy available under the recall and whether a visit or collection involves a charge. Your legal rights are not affected by our safety process. If something is unclear, ask us to explain it before agreeing to the proposed arrangements.

We use the information you share to assess the concern, arrange support and maintain our safety records. If you are unhappy with how a visit or collection is handled, contact customer support and ask for your concern to be reviewed through our complaints process.

cell.item: POL-SAF/North of England/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in the North of England and need help with a safety concern or recall, contact Halvard Home through our customer support service. We will explain what action is needed and whether a visit or collection is appropriate for your circumstances.

Urgent safety visits in North of England are made within 63 hours. We treat a visit as urgent when our safety assessment identifies a risk that requires an urgent response. Our support team will explain the assessment and confirm the arrangements with you.

Recall collections in North of England are made within 33 working days. If your recall notice asks you to arrange a collection, contact us using the details in that notice. We will confirm what is being collected and explain how to prepare it safely.

If you believe there is an immediate danger, stop using the affected item and keep people away from it. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. If there is smoke, fire or another emergency, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Do not attempt a repair or remove covers to investigate a fault. Follow the safety instructions in your recall notice or those given by our support team. If an instruction is unclear or seems unsafe in your home, tell us rather than trying to carry it out.

When you contact us, describe what has happened and tell us whether anyone has been injured or property has been damaged. We may ask for identifying information from the affected item. Do not move it or reach into an unsafe place to find that information.

We will agree access arrangements with you and explain who will attend. Tell us about steps, restricted entrances, parking restrictions or other conditions that could affect safe access. Please also let us know about accessibility or communication needs so that we can make suitable arrangements.

Our visiting staff will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit. If you are unsure whether a visitor represents Halvard Home, keep your door closed and contact our support service through a trusted channel. You should not feel pressured to let an unverified visitor into your home.

During the visit, our staff will assess the situation and explain the proposed action. This may involve making the affected item safe or arranging its removal under the recall process. They will tell you whether it must remain unused and explain what happens next.

If access is not possible or your circumstances change, contact us so that we can review the arrangements and any safety implications. We will explain changes to the plan and keep your case open until the agreed safety action has been completed.

We use the information you provide to manage the safety concern, organise attendance and maintain appropriate records. If you are unhappy with the arrangements or believe a risk has not been addressed, ask our support team to review your case and explain how to make a complaint.

If you live in the Midlands and believe an item supplied by Halvard Home may be unsafe, stop using it and contact our customer care team. Explain what has happened and whether there is smoke, an unusual smell, visible damage or a risk of injury. Do not attempt a repair yourself.

If there is an active fire or a threat to life, leave the area and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to disconnect, move or retrieve the item. Follow the advice of the emergency services rather than attempting to prepare your home for our visit.

Our customer care team will assess the information you provide and explain whether a safety visit is needed. We may ask for photographs, proof of purchase or details from the label, but only where these can be obtained safely. Please tell us if the affected item is difficult to reach.

Urgent safety visits in Midlands are made within 32 hours. We will explain whether your case has been classed as urgent and confirm the arrangements with you. If your circumstances change or the condition of the item gets worse, contact us so that we can review the safety advice and visit arrangements.

Recall collections in Midlands are made within 21 working days. Working days exclude weekends and public holidays. We will confirm whether collection is required and explain how it will be arranged. Do not dispose of, sell or pass on an item covered by a recall unless we have specifically advised that disposal is appropriate.

Please tell us about access needs when arranging a visit. This might include a need for step-free access, help with communication or support from someone you trust. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you. You do not need to move a heavy or unsafe item to make it accessible.

Our visiting representative will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit before entering your home. If you are unsure about their identity, keep the door closed and contact our customer care team through your usual contact route. You should not feel pressured to allow entry.

During the visit, our representative will assess the reported concern and explain the proposed action. This may involve making the item safe, arranging a repair or confirming that it needs to be collected. We will seek your agreement before carrying out work and explain any restrictions on further use.

Safety visits and collections arranged under a Halvard Home recall are free of charge. We will explain the remedy available under the recall and how to raise a concern if you are unhappy with the arrangements. Your statutory rights are not affected.

We use the information you provide to manage the safety concern, arrange access and maintain our recall records. Relevant details may be shared with the service partner handling your visit or collection. Please tell us if your contact details change so that we can keep you informed.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Wales and West/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in Wales and West, Halvard Home can arrange a safety visit where a reported concern or recall requires an assessment at your home. We will explain why the visit is needed, what you should do to stay safe and how to prepare for our representative’s arrival.

Urgent safety visits in Wales and West are made within 61 hours. We treat a visit as urgent where our safety assessment identifies a risk that needs prompt attention at your home. We will confirm how your case has been assessed and explain the arrangements directly to you.

If you think an affected item is unsafe, stop using it and follow the safety advice in your recall notice or from our support team. Do not attempt to repair, dismantle or test it yourself. If there is smoke, fire or an immediate threat to anyone’s safety, move away and contact the emergency services.

Contact Halvard Home through the details published on our official website or in your recall notice. Tell us what has happened and whether anyone has been harmed. We may ask for identifying details from the affected item, but you should not move it or approach it if doing so could put you at risk.

We will discuss access to your home and ask about anything that could affect the visit. Please tell us if you need communication support, accessible arrangements or help understanding our instructions. We will agree suitable arrangements with you and explain any limits that may affect what our representative can safely do.

Our representative will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit before asking to enter your home. If you are unsure who they are, keep the door closed and contact Halvard Home through an official contact route. You do not need to admit someone whose identity you cannot verify.

During the visit, our representative will assess the reported concern and explain the findings in plain language. They will tell you whether the affected item must remain unused and what action is required. We will provide written confirmation of the outcome and any safety instructions you need to follow.

Recall collections in Wales and West are made within 39 working days. We will confirm whether collection applies to your case and agree the collection arrangements with you. Please follow our instructions for keeping the affected item safe and accessible without attempting to move anything that could cause injury.

If access problems or a change in your circumstances could prevent a visit or collection, please contact us so we can discuss a safe alternative. If our arrangements change, we will explain what this means for your case and confirm how it will be handled. You can ask our support team to review any unresolved safety concern.

cell.item: POL-SAF/London and South East/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in London or South East, Halvard Home can arrange a safety visit where a reported concern needs inspection at your home. Our support team will explain whether a visit is appropriate and what you should do to stay safe while arrangements are being made.

Urgent safety visits in London and South East are made within 64 hours. We treat a visit as urgent when our safety assessment identifies a risk that requires prompt attention at your home. Tell us clearly about smoke, burning smells, unusual heat, electric shocks or signs of damage.

If there is an immediate danger, move away from the affected area and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk by trying to investigate. Stop using the affected appliance if you can do so safely, and follow the safety advice in our recall notice or from our support team.

When you contact us, we will ask for your address, contact details and a description of the concern. We may also ask for identifying information from the appliance label, but only if it is safe to read it. Do not move, open or dismantle anything to obtain this information.

We will agree access arrangements with you and explain what the engineer expects to do. Please tell us about access needs, communication preferences or circumstances that could affect the visit. If you rent your home, let us know whether permission from your landlord or managing agent is needed for access or work.

Our engineer will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit before starting work. If you are unsure about their identity, keep the door closed and contact Halvard Home through a trusted contact route. You do not need to admit someone whose identity you cannot confirm.

Please keep the area around the affected appliance accessible where this is safe. Keep children and pets away from the work area. The engineer may inspect the appliance, make it safe or explain why it must remain unused. We will tell you what has been found and what happens next.

Recall collections in London and South East are made within 53 working days. If a collection is needed, we will explain how it will be arranged and whether you need to prepare the appliance. Do not disconnect fixed wiring, disturb pipework or carry out removal work yourself unless we have confirmed that the task is safe and suitable for you.

If access cannot be gained or the visit cannot go ahead safely, we will explain the reason and discuss how to proceed. Tell us if your circumstances change or the reported problem becomes worse. We will review the safety advice and the arrangements with you. If you are unhappy with how your concern has been handled, our support team can explain how to raise a complaint.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Northern Ireland/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in Northern Ireland, Halvard Home can arrange a safety visit where an assessment or action at your address is needed. We will explain why the visit is required, what it involves and how to prepare. Please follow the safety advice provided with your notice.

Urgent safety visits in Northern Ireland are made within 21 hours. If you believe there is an immediate danger, move away from the affected area and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to inspect an appliance, disconnect it or recover belongings.

When you contact us about a safety concern, describe what has happened and tell us whether there is smoke, an unusual smell, visible damage or another sign of danger. We may ask for photographs, but only if you can take them safely.

If we advise you to stop using an appliance, leave it unused until we confirm that it is safe. Do not attempt repairs or ask an unauthorised person to alter it. Keep other people away where necessary, and follow the instructions in the safety notice.

We will agree access arrangements with you and explain how to recognise the person attending. Tell us about access restrictions, communication preferences or disability-related support that would help you manage the visit. You do not need to share medical details to request an adjustment.

Our representative will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit. If you are unsure about their identity, do not let them in. Contact Halvard Home through the contact details on our official website rather than relying on details supplied by an unexpected caller.

Please make the relevant area accessible if it is safe to do so. Keep children and pets away from the work area. You are not expected to move anything heavy, remove fixed fittings or carry out technical checks in preparation for our representative.

The representative will explain their findings and the action needed. This may involve making the appliance safe, carrying out an authorised repair or arranging removal. If it cannot safely be used, we will explain the restriction and provide clear instructions for you to keep.

Recall collections in Northern Ireland are made within 46 working days. We will explain the collection arrangements and tell you whether preparation is needed. Do not transport, dismantle or dispose of an appliance covered by a recall unless we have specifically advised you to do so.

If access becomes difficult or your circumstances change, please contact us so that we can review the arrangements. Tell us if the address is no longer correct or the appliance is elsewhere. We will explain how this affects the action needed to address the safety concern.

We will use the information you provide to manage the safety case, arrange attendance and keep you informed. If you are unhappy with the visit or the explanation you receive, contact our customer support team. We will review your concerns and explain how to raise a complaint.

This policy explains how Halvard Home manages servicing and engineer visits in customers’ homes. It covers requesting a visit, assessing a reported fault, arranging access, carrying out work safely and explaining the outcome. It also sets out the responsibilities of customers, engineers and service partners, including how concerns about a visit should be raised and handled.

The policy is for customers who request support from Halvard Home, people acting on their behalf, and colleagues or authorised service partners involved in arranging or delivering that support. It is intended to help everyone understand what to expect and how to prepare for an engineer’s attendance.

The policy describes our approach to respectful conduct, accessibility needs, protection of the home and personal information, and decisions about further work. It should be read alongside the terms that apply to your service arrangement and does not affect your statutory rights.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Island Areas/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in an Island Area, contact Halvard Home if you receive a safety notice or believe your appliance may be unsafe. Tell us what has happened, where the appliance is located and whether there is a risk to people nearby. We will explain the appropriate action and arrange support.

Urgent safety visits in Island Areas are made within 51 hours. When you contact us, we will assess the reported risk and confirm whether an urgent safety visit is needed. We will explain how to prepare for the visit and how to stay safe until the engineer arrives.

If there is smoke, fire or an immediate threat to life, move away from the danger and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to switch off, unplug or move an appliance. Follow the advice of the emergency services rather than attempting a repair yourself.

Where a safety notice tells you to stop using an appliance, leave it unused until we confirm that it is safe. Do not test it to see whether the fault is still present. If you are unsure whether a notice applies to your appliance, contact us for help checking its identification details.

Island travel can involve ferries, local transport and restricted access. Please tell us about access arrangements that could affect a visit, such as locked gates, shared entrances or landing restrictions. We will coordinate travel with the engineer and keep you informed about the arrangements for reaching your home.

We will agree how to contact you about the visit. Please let us know if you need communication support or an adjustment because of a disability or health condition. You do not need to explain private medical details unless they are relevant to arranging safe access or providing suitable support.

The engineer will identify themselves and explain the safety work before starting. You can ask us to verify their identity before letting them into your home. Please keep the route to the appliance clear where it is safe to do so, and keep children and pets away from the work area.

Recall collections in Island Areas are made within 44 working days. If collection is required, we will explain how it will be arranged and whether the appliance needs to be disconnected. Do not disconnect fixed wiring or fittings yourself unless our instructions expressly say that this is safe.

You do not need to take an unsafe appliance to a ferry terminal, depot or collection point unless we have agreed a safe arrangement with you. Tell us if moving it would create a risk or if you cannot prepare it for collection.

After a visit or collection, we will explain what happens next and provide confirmation of the action taken. If you remain concerned about safety or are unhappy with the arrangements, contact Halvard Home and ask for your case to be reviewed.

You can request an engineer visit by contacting Halvard Home through the contact options on our website. Tell us what needs attention, describe the fault and explain whether it affects safe use. We may ask questions to help us understand the problem and arrange suitable support.

Please provide your name, contact details and the address where the engineer is needed. Let us know about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything else that could affect the visit. If you need support with communication or access, tell us when booking so we can discuss suitable arrangements with you.

We may suggest checks that could resolve the issue without a visit. Only carry out checks that you understand and can perform safely. Do not remove protective covers, attempt repairs or continue using anything that appears unsafe. Tell us if you cannot follow the suggested checks.

Standard engineer visits are booked within 16 working days of a request. We will discuss availability with you and confirm the agreed booking using the contact details you provide. Your request is not a confirmed booking until you receive our confirmation. Please check the details and contact us if they are incorrect.

Each visit is given an arrival window of 5 hours. The arrival window will be included in your booking confirmation. We cannot guarantee arrival at a particular point within that window. If travel disruption or an earlier job affects the engineer’s arrival, we will contact you to explain and discuss the booking.

A responsible adult who can authorise access and discuss the fault must be present for the visit. Please make sure the engineer can reach the area safely and has space to work. Keep pets away from the work area and tell us about hazards that may require special arrangements.

We will explain whether the visit is covered by your guarantee or service agreement. If charges may apply, we will explain the basis of those charges before you agree to the booking. The engineer will seek your approval before carrying out chargeable work outside what has already been agreed.

Please contact us if you need to change or cancel your booking. Tell us if your contact details or access arrangements change. If the engineer cannot gain access or cannot work safely, the visit may need to be rearranged. We will explain any applicable charges before you agree to the booking.

Booking a visit does not guarantee that the fault will be resolved during attendance. The engineer may need to assess the issue, obtain parts or arrange specialist support. We will explain the outcome of the assessment and discuss what happens next, including whether a further booking is needed.

We use the information you provide to arrange and manage your visit in line with our privacy notice. Nothing in these booking terms limits your statutory rights. If you are unsure about the booking arrangements, please contact us so we can explain them before you agree to proceed.

We will explain the charges that apply to your booking before you agree to an engineer visit. These may include a call-out charge, labour, parts and any specialist work needed. Prices quoted to you include VAT where it applies, unless we clearly state otherwise.

A call-out charge covers the engineer’s attendance and assessment of the reported fault. It may still be payable if you decide not to proceed with a repair. We will tell you whether this charge applies when you book, including where a repair may be covered by your warranty.

Labour after the first hour is charged at £55.00 an hour. The engineer will explain how labour charges are calculated and ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work. You can ask for clarification before deciding whether to proceed.

An estimate reflects the information available when we assess the work. If the engineer finds that the repair needs different parts or further work, we will explain the revised charges and seek your approval. We will not carry out that work without your agreement.

Parts fitted outside the warranty carry a handling charge of 28%. We calculate this charge from the price of the parts and show it separately on your bill. We will explain the parts charges before asking you to approve the repair.

Where a fault is covered by your warranty, we will apply the warranty terms to the visit and repair. If we believe a charge is payable because the fault is not covered, we will explain why and give you the opportunity to discuss our assessment.

A charge may apply if the engineer cannot safely access the property or the place where the work is needed. We will explain any access requirements when arranging your visit. Please tell us about anything that could prevent the engineer from carrying out the agreed work.

If you need to cancel or rearrange your booking, please contact us. Any cancellation charge must have been explained when you booked and will reflect reasonable costs incurred. We will explain the reason for the charge rather than applying it without an explanation.

Payment is due as agreed when you book or approve the work. We will confirm the available payment methods and provide a bill describing the charges. Please do not make payments to an engineer unless we have confirmed that they are authorised to collect payment.

If you believe your bill is incorrect, contact us using the details on your booking confirmation. Tell us which charge you are questioning and why. We will review the bill, explain our findings and correct any error. These charging terms do not affect your statutory rights.

Cancel a visit at least 56 hours before it is due to avoid a charge. A visit cancelled later than that is charged at £47.00.

If you need to cancel, please contact Halvard Home using the contact details in your booking confirmation. Tell us that you want to cancel and provide enough information for us to find your booking, such as your name and the address where the engineer was due to attend.

We use the date and time we receive your cancellation request to decide whether the cancellation charge applies. You do not need to wait for us to reply for your request to count as received, provided it reaches the contact channel shown in your booking confirmation.

Please make your request clear. Asking a question about your booking does not cancel it. If you are unsure whether you still need the visit, we can help you understand your options, but the booking remains in place unless you ask us to cancel it.

We will confirm your cancellation using the contact details held with your booking. Please keep that confirmation for your records. If you do not receive it, contact us so that we can check the booking status. We will not charge you simply because our confirmation was delayed.

If you would prefer to rearrange the visit, please tell us rather than cancelling without explanation. We will explain the available options and whether moving the booking would attract the cancellation charge before making the change. A replacement appointment is subject to engineer availability.

If someone else is contacting us on your behalf, we may need to check that they have your permission to cancel. This helps us protect your booking and personal information. Please make sure they have the details needed for us to identify the visit.

Where a cancellation charge applies, we will explain why and tell you how payment will be handled. If you have already paid towards the visit, we will explain how the cancellation affects that payment and whether a refund is due.

We understand that unexpected circumstances can make it difficult to keep an appointment. If this happens, please contact us and explain your situation. We will consider the circumstances fairly, including any accessibility needs, and let you know whether we can waive the cancellation charge.

You will not be charged for a cancellation made by Halvard Home. If we cannot carry out the visit as agreed, we will contact you to explain what has happened and discuss rearranging it or cancelling the booking.

If you believe a cancellation charge has been applied incorrectly, please contact us with your booking details and any relevant correspondence. We will review the information and explain our decision. Nothing in these cancellation terms limits your statutory rights.

The Brio kettle should be serviced every 44 months. This schedule helps keep your kettle in good working order and gives an engineer an opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults that may not be obvious during everyday use.

Use the purchase date to work out when your kettle is due for its initial service. After a service has been completed, use the service date as the starting point for the next scheduled visit. Keep your purchase receipt and service records somewhere accessible.

If you do not know the purchase date or cannot find your service record, contact Halvard Home. We can help you check the information available and agree an appropriate service date. Do not assume that a previous owner arranged servicing if you bought your kettle used.

A reminder is sent 4 weeks before the Brio kettle is due for a service. Please keep your contact details up to date so that the reminder can reach you. You remain responsible for arranging a service if you do not receive it.

To arrange a visit, contact Halvard Home through our customer support service. Tell us that you would like to book a routine service for your Brio kettle. Please also mention any changes in its performance or any damage you have noticed.

A routine service of the Brio kettle takes about 135 minutes. Please allow the engineer access to the kettle throughout the appointment. Tell us when booking if access to your home is restricted or if you need adjustments to help you manage the visit.

A routine service of the Brio kettle costs £78.00. This covers the scheduled inspection and routine servicing work. If the engineer identifies a repair outside that work, we will explain what is needed and ask for your agreement before proceeding.

Before the engineer arrives, unplug the kettle, allow it to cool and empty it. Leave it with its base in a clear, accessible area. Have your service record available if you have it, and keep children and pets away from the work area.

The engineer will check the kettle’s condition and operation, carry out routine servicing and explain any findings. If the kettle needs further attention, the engineer will tell you whether it is safe to use and what action is recommended.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the kettle leaks, gives off a burning smell or has visible damage to its cable, plug or casing. Stop using it and contact Halvard Home for advice. Unplug it only if you can do so safely.

Routine servicing does not replace the cleaning and care described in the user instructions. Follow that guidance between visits, and keep the engineer’s service notes with your records so they are available when you arrange future servicing.

Common repairs to the Brio kettle include problems with heating, the switch, the lid and the filter. A kettle that leaks, cuts out unexpectedly or fails to switch off may also need attention. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure whether the fault can be resolved through routine care or needs an engineer’s assessment.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, smells of burning, has a damaged lead or shows signs of electrical damage. Disconnect it from the mains if it is safe to do so. Do not open the casing, alter the plug or attempt an electrical repair yourself. Keep the kettle disconnected until we advise that it is safe to use.

If the kettle is noisy, heats poorly or pours unevenly, limescale or a blocked filter may be responsible. Follow the cleaning and descaling instructions supplied with your kettle. Let it cool before cleaning, and keep the base, plug and electrical connections dry. Do not use sharp tools to remove deposits or force a stiff lid or switch.

Replace the filter of the Brio kettle every 18 weeks. Use a compatible replacement supplied or approved by Halvard Home, and follow the fitting instructions. If the filter does not sit securely, stop using the kettle and contact us. Damage to the filter housing may need assessment rather than a replacement filter.

When requesting a repair, describe the fault and tell us about visible damage, unusual smells or leaking. We may ask for proof of purchase and details from the product label. This helps us check the support available and decide whether an engineer visit is suitable. Do not reconnect an unsafe kettle to demonstrate a fault.

We will explain the proposed repair and any applicable charges before asking for your agreement. The engineer will inspect the kettle and confirm whether the work can proceed safely. If the inspection reveals a different fault or changes the proposed work, we will explain the revised recommendation and seek your approval before proceeding.

Paid repairs to the Brio kettle come with their own guarantee. Repairs are guaranteed for 122 days. This guarantee covers the work carried out and the parts fitted as part of that repair. Contact us if the repaired fault returns, and keep your repair confirmation. The repair guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Spare parts for the Brio kettle are stocked for 9 years after the model is discontinued. Availability of a suitable part will be checked when we assess your request. We will tell you if a required part is unavailable and explain the options rather than fit an unsuitable substitute.

If the kettle cannot be repaired safely, we will explain why and discuss the appropriate next steps. The engineer may advise against further use. Follow that advice and keep the kettle disconnected. We can also provide guidance on responsible disposal of electrical appliances.

Routine servicing helps keep your Tessa dishwasher working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to check its condition. Follow the servicing guidance supplied with your appliance and arrange a visit when your service reminder arrives. If you cannot find your guidance, contact Halvard Home for help with your servicing schedule.

Owners of the Tessa dishwasher are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 6 weeks before a service is due.

Keep your contact details up to date so that your reminder reaches you. Tell Halvard Home if your email address, postal address or preferred contact method changes. If you believe a service is due but have not received a reminder, contact us rather than waiting for a message.

A reminder does not confirm an appointment. You need to contact Halvard Home through the booking details provided to arrange an engineer visit. We will confirm the appointment and explain the arrangements for access. Tell us about accessibility requirements or anything that could affect the engineer’s ability to reach the appliance safely.

A routine service of the Tessa dishwasher takes about 230 minutes.

Please allow the engineer to complete the agreed checks without interruption. An adult who can provide access and discuss the appliance must be present for the visit. If you need to change or cancel the appointment, contact Halvard Home using the details in your booking confirmation.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the dishwasher and make sure the area around it is clear. Keep children and pets away from the working area. Leave the appliance installed unless Halvard Home has specifically asked you to do otherwise. Do not disconnect pipework, remove panels or attempt to move a fitted appliance yourself.

During the service, the engineer will inspect the appliance and carry out the maintenance covered by your booking. Tell the engineer about changes in washing performance, unusual noises, leaks or messages shown on the controls. This helps them understand concerns that may not be apparent during an inspection.

Routine servicing is different from a repair visit. If the engineer finds a fault that falls outside the agreed service, they will explain the findings and discuss the proposed work with you. Work that carries a separate charge will require your agreement before it proceeds.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the dishwasher appears unsafe. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell or water leaking near electrical connections. Contact Halvard Home for advice, and avoid touching plugs or switches if the surrounding area is wet.

After the visit, keep the service record with your appliance documents and follow the engineer’s advice. Continue the cleaning and care described in the user guide between services. A service does not replace routine care, and routine care does not replace the checks carried out by an engineer.

Common repairs to the Tessa dishwasher include clearing blockages, replacing worn seals, repairing door catches and replacing faulty pumps, valves or heating components. An engineer will assess the fault before recommending a repair. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm which parts are needed from a description alone.

When you contact Halvard Home, describe what happens when you use the appliance, including any unusual noise, leak, smell or message on the display. Tell us whether the problem affects washing, draining, heating or closing the door. This helps us prepare for the visit, but does not replace an inspection.

You can check that the water supply is turned on, that the door closes properly and that accessible filters are clear, following the user instructions. Do not remove panels, disconnect internal wiring or attempt to repair electrical components. If the appliance leaks, smells of burning or appears electrically unsafe, stop using it and isolate it from the electricity supply if safe to do so.

Diagnosing a fault on the Tessa dishwasher costs £77.00 if no repair follows. This applies where the engineer identifies the fault but you choose not to proceed, or where a repair is not practical. We will explain any applicable charge before you agree to the visit.

If a repair is possible, the engineer will explain the proposed work and provide a quote before starting it. The quote will identify the labour and parts covered. You can decline the repair. We will not carry out additional chargeable work without your agreement.

Some faults can be resolved by cleaning, adjustment or securing a loose connection. Others need replacement parts. If the engineer finds damage or an installation problem that prevents safe repair, they will explain what needs attention. Work to your household plumbing, electrical supply or cabinetry is not included unless expressly agreed.

Spare parts for the Tessa dishwasher are stocked for 19 years after the model is discontinued. A part may still need to be ordered for your repair. We will explain any availability issue and discuss the available options before arranging further work.

Repairs to the Tessa dishwasher are guaranteed for 184 days. The guarantee covers the repair work and parts supplied as part of that work. It does not cover an unrelated fault or damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or unauthorised alterations. Your statutory rights are not affected.
