This notice applies to Halvard Home cleaning gel pouches labelled with the affected batch on the packaging. Please check the label before using a pouch. Keep affected pouches in their original packaging, away from children and pets. Do not open, puncture or empty them.

Contact Halvard Home customer support for help arranging your return and refund. If you have already used an affected pouch, leave the dryer switched off and ask our support team for advice before using it again.

Corra outdoor fan grille notice

Stop using outdoor fan grilles from batch 5107 with the Corra induction hob, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch marking on their grille packaging or product label. If your grille matches the affected batch, stop using it and keep it separate from your hob accessories. Please contact Halvard Home customer support for guidance on returning the grille and arranging your refund. If the marking is missing or unclear, leave the grille unused and ask customer support for help identifying it.

We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your cooperation.

Important rinse aid sachet notice

Stop using rinse aid sachets from batch 1908 with the Keel washing machine, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is recalling these sachets because they may not work as intended with this appliance. You can find the batch details on the sachet packaging. Keep affected sachets away from your laundry supplies so they are not used by mistake.

Please contact Halvard Home customer support for help arranging your return and refund. If you no longer have the packaging, our team can help you check whether your sachets are affected.

We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your understanding.

Brio kettle rinse aid notice

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch details on their rinse aid sachet packaging.

Stop using rinse aid sachets from batch 8708 with the Brio kettle, and return them for a refund.

Please keep the sachets in their packaging and separate from products you are still using. Do not put the affected sachets into your kettle or pass them on to anyone else. Contact Halvard Home customer support for guidance on returning them and arranging your refund. If you cannot read the batch details, contact us before using the sachets.

We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.

Orrin heat pump travel case notice

Stop using travel cases from batch 6453 with the Orrin heat pump, and return them for a refund.

Check the batch label on your travel case to see whether it is affected. If the label is missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home customer support before using the case again.

Please keep the case separate from your heat pump while arranging its return. Our customer support team can explain how to return an affected case and request your refund.

We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help in keeping our products safe to use.

Brio kettle lint filter notice

Stop using lint filters from batch 9847 with the Brio kettle, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch details on their filter packaging. If your filters match the batch shown above, remove them only when the kettle is unplugged and completely cool. Keep the filters and packaging together, and contact Halvard Home customer support for return instructions. Please do not fit these filters to another appliance or pass them on to someone else. If the batch details are missing or unclear, stop using the filters and ask our support team for advice. We apologise for the inconvenience.

Corra cleaning gel pouch notice

Stop using cleaning gel pouches from batch 2046 with the Corra induction hob, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is recalling these pouches because they may damage the hob’s surface. Check the batch details on the packaging and keep affected pouches away from children and pets.

Please keep the pouches in their original packaging and contact Halvard Home customer support for return instructions.

If you have already used an affected pouch, let the hob cool before wiping it with a soft, damp cloth. Do not use abrasive cleaners.

We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your cooperation.

Brio kettle wall bracket notice

Stop using wall brackets from batch 4867 with the Brio kettle, and return them for a refund.

We have identified a safety concern with these brackets, which may not hold the kettle securely. Please remove your kettle from the bracket when it is cool and empty, and place it on a stable, level worktop away from the edge.

Check the batch details on the bracket or its packaging. If you cannot confirm whether your bracket is affected, stop using it and contact Halvard Home customer support for advice and return arrangements.

We are sorry for the inconvenience and appreciate your help in keeping your home safe.

Ashby tumble dryer side brush notice

Stop using side brushes from batch 8826 with the Ashby tumble dryer, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch marking on their side brush packaging before use. If your brushes match the batch shown above, keep them aside for return. Please contact the retailer you bought them from or Halvard Home customer support for help arranging your refund.

If the marking is missing or unclear, do not use the brushes until customer support has confirmed whether they are affected.

We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your cooperation.

Detergent pod safety notice

Stop using detergent pods from batch 2155 with the Lumen smart thermostat, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home has identified a potential safety issue with these pods. Check the batch details on the packaging and keep affected pods away from children and pets. Do not open, puncture or dispose of them in household waste.

If a pod has been used with your thermostat, stop using the device and contact Halvard Home customer support for guidance. Keep the packaging and proof of purchase if available. Our support team can explain how to return affected pods safely and arrange your refund. We apologise for the inconvenience.

Important descaling tablet notice

Stop using descaling tablets from batch 2873 with the Corra induction hob, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is recalling these tablets because they may not be suitable for use with this appliance. Check the batch details on the packaging and keep any affected tablets away from your hob. Please leave them in their original packaging and take them back to the shop where you bought them. If you no longer have the packaging, or need help arranging a return, contact Halvard Home customer support. We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.

Orrin heat pump side brush notice

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch details on their side brush packaging before fitting or using these accessories.

Stop using side brushes from batch 6199 with the Orrin heat pump, and return them for a refund.

If your brushes are affected, remove them from use and keep them separate from other accessories. Please contact Halvard Home customer support for guidance on arranging your return and refund.

If you cannot find the batch details, leave the brushes unused and ask our support team for help.

We are sorry for the inconvenience and appreciate your cooperation.

Brio kettle lint filter notice

Stop using lint filters from batch 7105 with the Brio kettle, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch marking on their lint filter packaging. If the marking matches the batch shown above, please remove the filter only when the kettle is unplugged and completely cool. Do not try to repair or modify the filter.

Contact Halvard Home customer support for help arranging your return and refund. If the packaging is missing or the marking is unclear, stop using the filter and ask customer support for advice.

We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your cooperation.

Detergent pod safety notice

Halvard Home is recalling the affected detergent pods as a precaution. Stop using detergent pods from batch 5311 with the Lumen smart thermostat, and return them for a refund.

Keep the pods in their original packaging, away from children, pets and food. Do not open, puncture or dispose of them in household waste. Contact Halvard Home customer support for safe return instructions and help arranging your refund.

If a pod has leaked, avoid touching the contents and seek advice from customer support. We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help in keeping your home safe.

Corra hob detergent pod notice

Stop using detergent pods from batch 6561 with the Corra induction hob, and return them for a refund.

We are sorry for the inconvenience and appreciate your help in keeping your home safe. Please check the batch details on the packaging and keep the affected pods separate from your usual cleaning products, out of reach of children and pets.

Do not use them to clean the hob or transfer them into an unlabelled container. Contact Halvard Home customer support for return instructions and help arranging your refund. If the packaging is missing or unclear, please ask us for advice before using the pods.

Cleaning gel pouch safety notice

Stop using cleaning gel pouches from batch 9421 with the Fenwick cooker hood, and return them for a refund.

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch details on the pouch packaging before cleaning their cooker hood. If your pouches match the affected batch, keep them sealed and away from children and pets. Please take them back to the shop where you bought them, or contact Halvard Home customer support for help arranging a return. Do not empty the gel into a sink or bin.

We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.

Important advice for Tessa owners

Halvard Home is asking customers to check the batch details on their descaling tablet packaging. Stop using descaling tablets from batch 3558 with the Tessa dishwasher, and return them for a refund.

The affected tablets may not be suitable for your dishwasher. Keep the packaging and take the tablets back to the retailer where you bought them. Please do not put them in your household waste or pass them on to someone else.

If you have used these tablets and are concerned about your dishwasher, contact Halvard Home customer support for guidance. We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.

Outdoor fan grille notice

Stop using outdoor fan grilles from batch 7264 with the Ashby tumble dryer, and return them for a refund.

This notice applies to outdoor fan grilles supplied by Halvard Home for use with the Ashby tumble dryer. Please check the batch label on your grille or its packaging to see whether it is affected. If the label is missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home customer support for help. Do not fit or reuse an affected grille. Contact customer support for guidance on returning it and arranging your refund. We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your cooperation.

Register a new appliance within 43 days of delivery to activate the standard warranty. Registration links your appliance to your purchase details and helps us check your cover when you need support. You can register through the Halvard Home website or ask our customer care team for help. Registration is free, and you do not need to agree to receive marketing messages to complete it.

Before you begin, have your purchase and delivery details ready, along with the identifying information shown on the appliance label. We use this information to match your registration to the correct appliance. Copy the details carefully, as an incorrect entry may make it harder for us to confirm your cover. If the label is missing, damaged or difficult to reach safely, contact us rather than moving or dismantling the appliance.

Give us the name and contact details you want us to use for warranty matters. These details should belong to the person responsible for the registration, or to someone authorised to act for them. If you are registering on behalf of someone else, make sure you have their permission to share their information. Please do not send personal information that we have not asked for.

Keep your proof of purchase for at least 62 months after delivery. Your receipt, invoice or order confirmation should identify the seller and show what you bought and when you bought it. If delivery took place separately from the purchase, keep the delivery confirmation as well. A registration confirmation does not replace these records, and we may ask to see them when assessing a warranty claim.

If you received the appliance as a gift, ask the person who bought it to provide suitable purchase and delivery evidence. You do not need to share details about the occasion or your relationship with the buyer. Where obtaining the paperwork is difficult, contact customer care to discuss what evidence may be acceptable. We cannot promise to confirm warranty eligibility without enough information to verify the purchase.

After you submit your registration, we will send confirmation using the contact details you provided. Check that the appliance and delivery information in that confirmation are correct. If anything is wrong, tell us so that we can update the record. Keep the confirmation somewhere accessible with your purchase documents. If it does not arrive, check your unwanted email folder or contact customer care for assistance.

Submitting a registration does not mean that every fault or request for service will be covered. Warranty claims remain subject to the policy terms, including the conditions relating to installation, use and care. Registration does not extend the scope of cover or remove any exclusions. We will assess a claim using the information available about the appliance, the reported problem and the circumstances in which it arose.

If you have missed the registration deadline, please contact us rather than assuming that support is unavailable. We will explain whether registration can be accepted and what options apply. Do not change the delivery details to make the appliance appear eligible. If you are unsure of the delivery date, tell us and provide the evidence you have so that we can review it.

If the website is unavailable or you cannot use the online form, our customer care team can help you register through an alternative route. Let us know if you need an accessible format or support with the process. You do not need to explain a disability or health condition to request practical help. We will tell you what information is needed to complete the registration.

Please tell us if your contact details change or if you notice an error in your registration record. If ownership of the appliance changes, contact us for guidance about the warranty terms that apply. Updating a registration record does not itself confirm that cover can be transferred. We may need supporting information before making changes that affect who can use the warranty.

We handle registration information in line with our privacy policy. It may be used to administer your warranty, respond to support requests and contact you about relevant safety matters. Your marketing preferences are managed separately and do not determine warranty eligibility. Nothing in this registration requirement limits your statutory rights, including any rights you have against the seller if the appliance is faulty or does not match its description.

To make a warranty claim, contact Halvard Home customer support using the contact details published on our website or supplied with your purchase. Tell us that you wish to claim under the warranty and explain what has gone wrong. You do not need to use legal language or diagnose the fault yourself.

Please give us your name, contact details and the address where the item is kept. Describe the fault, how it affects normal use and any circumstances that may help us understand it. If you have already contacted us about the same issue, mention this so we can connect the records.

We will ask for evidence of purchase and information that helps us identify the item. A receipt or order confirmation is usually suitable. If you cannot find these documents, tell us what evidence you can provide. We will explain whether it is enough to assess your claim and discuss suitable alternatives where available.

You can ask someone to make the claim on your behalf. We may need your permission before discussing your personal details with them. If you need help communicating with us, or require information in an accessible format, let us know. We will discuss how we can support you through the claim process.

A claim made by phone is logged within 67 hours. During the call, our customer support team will record the information you provide and explain what happens next. Please tell us if you think we have misunderstood your description of the fault or recorded your contact details incorrectly.

Halvard Home replies to a warranty claim within 22 working days of receiving it. Our reply will explain whether we can assess the claim from the information provided or need further evidence. A reply does not necessarily mean that the claim has been accepted or that an inspection has been completed.

We may ask you to describe what you can see or hear, provide photographs, or follow checks that are safe and suitable for you. Do not attempt a check that you are uncomfortable carrying out. Tell us about any access needs or practical difficulties so we can consider another way to assess the fault.

If the item appears unsafe, stop using it and keep others away from it. Disconnect it from the power supply only if you can do so safely. Do not open protective covers, attempt internal repairs or continue testing a fault that could cause injury or damage. Contact customer support for advice.

Please do not arrange repairs or send the item to us unless we have agreed the arrangements with you. Work carried out without our agreement may affect our ability to assess the original fault. It does not automatically remove your legal rights. We will consider the circumstances and explain any effect on your warranty claim.

If an inspection or return is needed, we will explain how it will be arranged and what you need to prepare. Follow the packing and handling instructions we provide, and tell us if you cannot safely move or pack the item. We will clarify responsibility for transport costs before you agree to the arrangements.

Keep your proof of purchase and copies of messages relating to the claim. Do not send original documents unless we specifically ask for them and explain how they will be returned. If photographs or documents contain personal information unrelated to the claim, you may cover or remove that information before sending them.

We assess claims against the warranty terms that apply to your purchase and the evidence available. Where the fault is covered, we will explain the remedy offered and how it will be carried out. If the proposed arrangements are not practical for you, tell us so we can discuss your concerns.

If we believe the fault is not covered, we will give you the reason in plain language and identify the relevant warranty term. We will explain any chargeable option separately. We will not treat your warranty claim as permission to carry out paid work, and we will seek your agreement before proceeding.

If you disagree with our decision, ask customer support to review it and provide any evidence you would like us to consider. You may also use our complaints process. This warranty is separate from your statutory rights and does not limit them, including your rights against the retailer that sold you the item.

The Brio kettle is covered for 47 months from the date of delivery. This is the date the kettle reaches you, rather than the date you place your order or make payment. Your delivery confirmation will normally show the date we use to establish your cover.

Keep your proof of purchase and delivery confirmation somewhere safe. We may ask to see them when you make a claim. If your records are missing or show conflicting information, contact Halvard Home so we can help check the delivery details and confirm when your cover began.

The cover period applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship, provided the Brio kettle has been used and cared for as instructed. Being within the cover period does not mean that damage from misuse, accidental damage or normal wear is covered by this warranty.

Tell us about a fault as soon as you notice it. Please explain what has happened and provide the information we need to identify your Brio kettle. If it appears unsafe, stop using it and unplug it if you can safely do so. Do not attempt a repair yourself.

We assess whether a claim falls within the cover period using the date you report the fault to us. If you report a covered fault before your warranty expires, the claim will not become invalid simply because our assessment or the agreed repair takes place after the cover has ended.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 10 months. This applies to work authorised by Halvard Home to put right a fault covered by the warranty. It does not apply to work that you arrange independently without our agreement, or to work on damage outside the warranty.

After the free labour cover ends, a labour charge may apply even if the fault otherwise qualifies for warranty support. We will explain any proposed charge before asking you to approve the repair. We will not treat your request for help as permission to carry out chargeable work.

Replacement parts fitted to the Brio kettle are covered for a further 138 days. This cover begins on the date the parts are fitted during a repair authorised by Halvard Home. Keep the repair record, as it helps us confirm the fitting date if a replacement part develops a fault.

The replacement part cover applies to defects in the fitted part, not to unrelated faults elsewhere in the kettle. It does not shorten any cover still available under the original warranty. Where the original warranty provides longer protection for the same fault, we will assess your claim under that cover.

A repair does not restart the warranty for the Brio kettle itself. Unless we confirm otherwise in writing, its cover continues from the original delivery date. The separate protection for fitted replacement parts should not be read as an extension of the warranty for the entire kettle.

If we replace the Brio kettle under the warranty rather than repair it, the replacement carries the cover remaining from the original delivery date. We will provide written confirmation of the applicable end date so that you can keep it with your claim records and proof of purchase.

If the Brio kettle is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 42 days. The transfer deadline runs from the date of sale to the new owner. The seller should pass on the proof of purchase, delivery details and any repair records needed to support the transfer.

The new owner should contact Halvard Home with those records and evidence of the sale. A transfer does not restart or extend the cover. The warranty remains linked to the original delivery date, and its conditions continue to apply after the change of ownership.

If the transfer deadline is missed, the new owner cannot rely on this warranty unless Halvard Home agrees otherwise in writing. Contact us if there is a problem obtaining the records or completing the transfer. We will explain what information is needed and whether we can accept the request.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer. Its expiry, its labour terms and its transfer requirements do not remove rights you may have under applicable law. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the Brio kettle, regardless of whether this warranty applies.

cell.item: POL-WAR/General terms/What the warranty does not cover

result.text:
The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship. It does not cover damage, faults or costs caused by circumstances outside that cover. When we assess a claim, we look at the condition of the appliance, the information you provide and any relevant inspection findings. An exclusion applies only where it is relevant to the fault or claim.

The warranty does not cover misuse, neglect or use contrary to the instructions supplied with the appliance. This includes forcing controls, ignoring safety warnings or using the appliance for a purpose for which it was not designed. Damage caused by unsuitable substances or materials is also excluded.

Faults caused by incorrect installation are not covered. This includes unsuitable connections, inadequate ventilation or placing the appliance where its operating requirements cannot be met. If an installation problem has caused the fault, that problem must be addressed before a repair can be expected to resolve it.

The warranty does not cover faults arising from an unsuitable or unreliable supply of electricity, water or other services needed for operation. Damage caused by power surges, leaks from external plumbing or problems with the building’s services is excluded where those conditions caused the damage.

Routine care and maintenance are your responsibility. The warranty does not cover cleaning, clearing obstructions or correcting problems caused by a failure to follow the care instructions. This includes damage linked to a build-up of dirt, grease, limescale or other deposits where appropriate maintenance would have prevented the problem.

Normal wear from ordinary use is not covered. Neither is the replacement of consumable items simply because they have been used up or worn out. If an item fails because of a defect in its materials or workmanship, rather than ordinary use, we will assess it under the warranty.

The warranty does not cover accidental damage. This includes damage caused by dropping, impact, excessive force or objects entering areas where they do not belong. Damage caused by pets, pests or exposure to unsuitable environmental conditions is also excluded unless it results from a fault covered by the warranty.

Changes to appearance that do not affect operation are not generally covered unless they result from defective materials or workmanship. Scratches, dents, stains and surface damage caused by handling, cleaning or use fall outside the warranty. Using abrasive cleaning materials or unsuitable chemicals may damage finishes and is not covered.

Cosmetic damage must be reported within 7 days of delivery. Please contact us with a description of the damage and, where possible, clear photographs. This reporting requirement helps us investigate delivery-related concerns and does not remove your statutory rights if the appliance arrived damaged or was otherwise not as described.

Damage caused by alterations or repairs that introduce a fault is excluded. The same applies where unsuitable replacement parts or accessories cause damage or prevent correct operation. Having work carried out by an independent repairer does not, by itself, mean that an unrelated defect is excluded from warranty cover.

The warranty does not cover use in a commercial, industrial or shared service setting where the appliance was supplied for domestic use. This exclusion applies where that use caused or contributed to the fault, including use that places demands on the appliance beyond its intended operating conditions.

An inspection that finds misuse is charged at £106.00. We will explain the inspection arrangements and any applicable charge before you agree to a visit. If you wish to proceed with work outside the warranty, we will explain the proposed work and its cost before seeking your approval.

The warranty does not cover a visit solely to explain normal operation, adjust settings or resolve an issue that is not a fault. Please check the operating instructions and troubleshooting advice before requesting a repair. If you remain unsure, contact us so we can help assess the problem.

Costs you choose to incur without our agreement, such as arranging a separate inspection or repair, are not automatically reimbursed under this warranty. We will consider the circumstances and any legal obligations that apply. Please contact us before committing to work if you intend to seek reimbursement through the warranty.

These exclusions describe the limits of this warranty, not the limits of your legal rights. Nothing here excludes or restricts rights or remedies available under applicable consumer law, including rights against the retailer. If a warranty exclusion applies, you may still be entitled to assistance or a remedy under that law.

If your Brio kettle develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home before arranging a repair yourself. We will help you check whether the problem needs an engineer and explain how to make a claim. Please stop using the kettle if you think it may be unsafe.

When you contact us, describe what happens when you use the kettle and tell us about any visible damage. We may ask for proof of purchase and information from the product label so that we can identify your kettle and check its warranty cover. Please do not remove or alter the label.

We may suggest simple checks that you can carry out safely, such as checking that the kettle is seated correctly on its base. We will not ask you to open the casing, touch internal wiring or attempt an electrical repair. If a check makes you uncomfortable, tell us so we can discuss another way forward.

A fault is confirmed when Halvard Home or an authorised engineer has assessed the problem and established that a repair is needed. We will tell you whether the repair is covered before proceeding. If we need to inspect the kettle to make that decision, we will explain the arrangements and any possible charges before you agree.

A warranty repair to the Brio kettle is completed within 6 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will explain how your repair will be handled and how we will contact you about its progress. Please make sure that the contact details you provide are correct and tell us if they change.

If a repair takes longer than 28 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. The replacement remains Halvard Home’s property and must be returned as instructed when your repaired kettle is available. We will explain the delivery and return arrangements. Please look after the loan kettle and let us know if it develops a fault.

Depending on the fault, we may arrange collection, ask you to send the kettle to an authorised repair centre, or arrange an engineer visit. Please follow the instructions we give you rather than sending the kettle to an address found elsewhere. This helps us keep your repair linked to your claim.

Before handing over the kettle, unplug it, let it cool and empty it completely. Pack it securely if it is being collected or posted. We will tell you whether to include the base or any detachable items. Do not include personal belongings, and keep your proof of purchase unless we specifically ask for it.

Where an engineer visit is arranged, please provide safe access to the kettle and a suitable place for the engineer to work. Tell us about anything that could affect access when making the appointment. If you cannot keep the appointment, contact us so that we can discuss alternative arrangements.

An engineer visit for the Brio kettle after the warranty has ended costs £79.00. This is separate from a repair accepted under warranty. If your claim is not covered, we will explain the reason and tell you what any proposed paid work involves. We will not carry out chargeable work without your agreement.

Repairs under warranty cover the labour and parts needed to correct an accepted fault. They do not automatically cover damage caused by misuse, accidental damage, unsuitable cleaning or repairs carried out without our authorisation. We will consider the circumstances of your claim and explain any decision to decline cover in plain language.

We may use new or refurbished parts where these are suitable for the repair. Refurbished parts are checked for safety and function before use. A refurbished part fitted to the Brio kettle is covered for 41 weeks. We will record the work carried out and explain how to report a problem with a fitted part.

After the repair, the kettle will be checked before it is returned to you or handed back by the engineer. Follow any care or safety advice supplied with it. If the original fault remains, or you notice a problem connected with the repair, stop using the kettle where necessary and contact us.

If you are unhappy with the repair or our decision about cover, ask us to review your claim. Share any relevant correspondence and explain what you would like us to reconsider. These warranty arrangements do not limit your statutory rights, including any rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the kettle.

The Tessa dishwasher is covered for 18 months from the date of delivery. This is the main warranty period for faults caused by defects in materials or manufacture. Cover depends on the dishwasher being used and cared for in line with the instructions supplied by Halvard Home.

The delivery date is the date the dishwasher arrives at the address agreed when it was bought. The date you ordered, paid for or installed it does not set the start of the main warranty period. Delaying installation does not delay the start of cover.

Please keep your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation. These help us identify your dishwasher and establish when cover began. If your documents show different delivery dates, contact us so that we can check the records and explain which date applies.

If you cannot find your paperwork, please still get in touch. We may be able to confirm the delivery details through your retailer or our own records. We will explain what information is needed rather than assume that missing paperwork means you have no cover.

Tell us about a fault while the relevant cover is active. You do not need to identify its technical cause before contacting us. Describe what is happening and let us know whether the dishwasher can be used safely.

If you report a covered fault before the relevant cover ends, an appointment arranged after that cover ends will not, by itself, make the claim invalid. We will record when you contacted us and assess the claim against the cover that applied then.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 26 months. This labour cover runs from the delivery date and applies to work authorised by Halvard Home to repair a fault covered by the warranty terms. It does not make every repair or service free.

The labour cover continues beyond the main warranty period, but it does not extend the cover for the dishwasher itself. Where labour remains covered but the required parts are not, you may have to pay for those parts. We will explain any proposed charges before asking you to approve the work.

Free labour does not include optional installation work, routine cleaning or changes to your plumbing or electrical supply. If the reported problem appears to involve work outside the warranty, we will explain the position before arranging a chargeable visit.

Replacement parts fitted to the Tessa dishwasher are covered for a further 165 days. This replacement part cover starts when the part is fitted as part of a repair authorised by Halvard Home. Keep the repair record, as it confirms the fitting date and identifies the work completed.

Replacement part cover applies to defects in the fitted part. It does not restart the main warranty period for the dishwasher or renew the labour cover. If the main warranty still protects the part when its replacement cover ends, that protection continues under the main warranty terms.

If a replacement part develops a fault, contact us with the repair details. We will check which cover applies and explain whether any associated labour is chargeable. Do not assume that cover for a part also covers work unrelated to that part.

A repair does not change the original delivery date used to calculate the dishwasher’s main warranty and labour cover. Your repair paperwork should distinguish the replacement part cover from the cover already attached to the appliance.

If the Tessa dishwasher is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 65 days. The transfer deadline is measured from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the available purchase, delivery and repair records.

Transferring the warranty changes the registered owner, not the dates on which cover begins or ends. The new owner receives whatever cover remains, subject to the same terms. Selling the dishwasher does not restart its warranty or renew cover for fitted replacement parts.

Please pass the warranty documents and care instructions to the new owner. If records are missing or the transfer deadline has been missed, contact us so that we can explain the position. We will not describe transferred cover as active until the transfer has been confirmed.

This warranty is provided by Halvard Home in addition to your legal rights. Its expiry does not remove rights you may have against the retailer under consumer law. If you are unsure whether to make a warranty claim, contact us and we will explain the available route.

If your Tessa dishwasher develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home customer support to arrange an assessment. Explain what happens when you use the appliance and whether the problem affects washing, draining, drying or safe operation. We will guide you through the repair process and explain what information we need.

Please have your proof of purchase available, together with the appliance details shown on its identification label. A receipt, order confirmation or suitable retailer record can help us check your warranty entitlement. If you cannot find your purchase documents, tell us so that we can discuss alternative evidence.

Our support team may suggest checks that you can safely carry out yourself. These might include checking the power supply, inspecting an accessible filter or confirming that the door closes properly. Do not remove protective panels, interfere with electrical connections or attempt work that requires specialist knowledge.

Stop using the appliance if it leaks, gives off smoke, smells of burning or appears unsafe. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely, and shut off its water supply where appropriate. Tell us about the concern when you contact us, so we can give suitable guidance.

Warranty cover applies to faults that meet the terms of your warranty. Damage caused by misuse, unsuitable installation, accidental damage or unauthorised alterations may fall outside that cover. We will explain our assessment and the reason for any decision that the reported problem is not covered.

Before arranging work outside the warranty, we will explain the proposed repair and any charges for your approval. You do not have to accept paid work simply because you have requested a warranty assessment. If the diagnosis changes during inspection, we will discuss the position with you before proceeding.

For an approved warranty repair, Halvard Home arranges an authorised repairer and covers the necessary labour and replacement parts. The repairer will assess whether the work can be carried out at your home or whether the appliance needs to be taken to a suitable workshop.

Contact customer support if you need clarification about the progress of your case.

Please make sure the repairer can reach the appliance safely. Do not disconnect or move an integrated appliance yourself unless we have specifically explained how this can be done safely.

If a repair to the Tessa dishwasher takes longer than 27 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. Our support team will arrange the loan with you and explain delivery, installation and collection. Tell us about access or connection requirements so that we can assess whether the proposed arrangement is suitable.

The loan appliance remains Halvard Home’s property. Use it in accordance with the instructions provided and tell us if it develops a fault or suffers damage. We will explain how to prepare it for collection when your repaired appliance is ready to be returned to normal use.

We may use new or refurbished parts where they are suitable for the repair. Refurbished parts are checked for condition, safety and performance before use. The repairer will record the work carried out and identify the parts fitted, so you have a clear account of the repair.

A refurbished part fitted to the Tessa dishwasher is covered for 43 weeks. This cover applies to faults in the refurbished part under normal domestic use. Keep the repair record with your purchase documents, and contact Halvard Home if you believe a fitted part has developed a covered fault.

After the repair, the repairer will carry out appropriate checks and explain whether the appliance is ready to use. Follow any instructions supplied about reconnecting the appliance, cleaning it or restarting a programme. If the original problem remains or returns, contact us and describe what you have noticed.

If you are unhappy with the repair or our handling of your claim, ask customer support to review the case through our complaints process. We will consider the repair records and the information you provide. Your warranty rights are separate from your statutory consumer rights, which are not affected by this policy.

The Orrin heat pump is covered for 72 months from the date of delivery. Your delivery record establishes when the warranty begins. The date you register the appliance, arrange installation or start using it does not change that starting point.

Keep your order confirmation, delivery note and warranty details somewhere accessible. If your delivery record is missing or appears incorrect, contact Halvard Home so that we can help establish the delivery date. We may ask for supporting information from the retailer or delivery service.

This warranty applies to faults caused by defective materials or manufacture, subject to the conditions and exclusions in this policy. Being within the cover period does not mean that every fault, service visit or replacement is covered. We will explain our assessment before arranging work.

Labour for repairs to the Orrin heat pump is free for the first 4 months. This applies where the repair is accepted under the warranty and carried out by Halvard Home or a repairer we authorise. It does not cover unrelated servicing or work arranged independently.

After free labour cover ends, you may need to pay the labour charges associated with a warranty repair. Eligible replacement parts remain covered while the warranty is valid. We will explain any proposed charges and seek your agreement before chargeable work goes ahead.

The distinction between parts cover and labour cover matters when deciding how to proceed with a repair. Please ask us if an estimate is unclear. You are welcome to discuss the proposed work before accepting it, and we will identify which charges fall outside your warranty.

Contact us when you become aware of a fault that you believe is covered. Describe what has happened and have your delivery details available. We may also ask for the appliance identification details so that we can check the warranty record and advise you safely.

Your report should reach us while the relevant cover remains active. If you report an eligible fault within that cover, an appointment arranged by us after it ends will not, by itself, remove your entitlement. Keep our acknowledgement with your warranty documents so the report date can be checked.

Repairing the Orrin heat pump does not restart its warranty or change the original delivery date used to calculate cover. Parts supplied under a warranty repair are covered under the remaining appliance warranty. The repair record will help us identify the work if you need further support.

If we replace the Orrin heat pump under this warranty, the replacement carries the cover remaining under the original warranty rather than starting fresh cover. We will confirm the applicable warranty details when arranging the replacement. This does not limit rights you have under consumer law.

If the Orrin heat pump is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 34 days. This requirement runs from the date ownership changes. The transfer preserves eligible cover that remains; it does not extend the warranty or restore labour cover that has ended.

The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale, the original delivery details and the appliance identification details. We will use these to check the existing cover and update our records. The seller should pass on the warranty documents and relevant repair records.

A transfer does not remove the conditions or exclusions attached to the warranty. The new owner takes over the remaining cover on the same basis as the previous owner. If the transfer requirement is not met, we may decline a claim under this warranty.

Please tell us if the registered contact details are incorrect. Accurate details help us discuss a claim with the right person and avoid confusion about ownership. Updating an address or correcting a name does not alter the delivery date or extend the cover.

Routine maintenance, accidental damage and faults caused by misuse are not made eligible simply because they arise during the cover period. Follow the care and installation instructions supplied with the Orrin heat pump. If the cause of a fault is uncertain, contact us rather than attempting a repair yourself.

When the warranty ends, you can still contact Halvard Home for advice about repair options. Work outside the warranty may be chargeable, and we will explain the proposed terms before you agree. This warranty is additional to your statutory rights and does not replace or restrict them.

If your Orrin heat pump develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging you for the necessary assessment, labour or parts. Contact our customer support team to report the problem and explain what you have noticed. Please have your proof of purchase available.

We will ask for your contact details, the installation address and information about the fault. Photographs or a description of any message shown on the controls may help us understand the problem. We will explain how to send this information securely and use it to manage your warranty claim.

Our support team may guide you through checks that are safe to carry out yourself. You do not need to remove covers, touch electrical connections or attempt a repair. If a suggested check is unclear or feels unsafe, stop and tell us so we can arrange appropriate help.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, leaking fluid or anything that suggests the Orrin heat pump is unsafe, stop using it. Isolate the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. Tell our support team about the safety concern when you contact us, and seek emergency help where necessary.

We will confirm whether the fault is covered after assessing the information you provide and, where needed, arranging an engineer visit. If we decide that the warranty does not cover the fault, we will explain the reason. You may ask us to review that decision and provide supporting evidence.

A warranty repair to the Orrin heat pump is completed within 20 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed, explain the planned repair and keep you informed about arrangements. You can contact our support team for an update.

We will agree access arrangements with you before sending an engineer. Please make sure the engineer can safely reach the Orrin heat pump and the relevant controls. Let us know about access restrictions, pets or accessibility needs so that we can make suitable arrangements for the visit.

If a repair to the Orrin heat pump takes longer than 3 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. There is no loan charge. We will discuss delivery and setup with you, explain how to use the replacement safely and arrange its collection when it is no longer needed.

Please take reasonable care of the loaned replacement and use it in line with the instructions supplied. Tell us if it develops a fault or is damaged. Do not attempt to repair or alter it yourself. We will explain what happens next and make suitable arrangements.

Warranty repairs are carried out by engineers appointed by Halvard Home. The engineer will assess the fault, explain the work required and use suitable parts. Please do not arrange independent repairs on our behalf without our agreement. We cannot promise to reimburse charges that we have not approved. If you are unhappy with how a warranty repair has been handled, contact our support team and explain your concerns. We will review the repair record and tell you how to raise a complaint. The warranty is separate from, and does not reduce, your statutory rights.

The Lumen smart thermostat is covered for 45 months from the date of delivery. This is the date the thermostat reaches you, rather than the date you place your order or make payment. Keep your delivery confirmation with your proof of purchase so that we can check when your cover began.

Your warranty applies to faults caused by defects in materials or workmanship during normal domestic use. We may ask for these records, details of the fault and information about the installation before deciding whether the warranty applies.

Labour for repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat is free for the first 14 months. This applies to work that Halvard Home authorises to put right a fault covered by the warranty. It does not include unrelated installation work, changes to your heating system or work requested for convenience.

After the free labour cover ends, a covered fault may still qualify for replacement parts under the warranty, but you may have to pay for the repair work. We will explain any proposed labour charge and seek your agreement before arranging work that you would need to pay for.

Please contact Halvard Home before asking an independent repairer to carry out work under this warranty. We cannot promise to reimburse work that we have not authorised. Using an independent repairer does not itself cancel your cover, although damage caused by that work is not covered.

Tell us about a fault as soon as you notice it. Stop using the thermostat if you believe it may be unsafe, and follow the safety guidance supplied with it. Do not remove protective parts or attempt repairs unless our instructions expressly say that you can do so.

A repair or replacement supplied under this warranty does not restart the cover period. It remains linked to the delivery date of the thermostat you originally purchased. We will explain how this applies when arranging a remedy, without limiting any separate rights you have under consumer law.

This warranty is provided by Halvard Home in addition to your legal rights. It does not restrict your rights against the retailer or any remedies available under consumer law. If warranty cover has ended, you may still have legal rights concerning a faulty thermostat, depending on the circumstances.

If your Lumen smart thermostat develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging you for the assessment, labour or parts needed to put that fault right. Contact our customer support team to request a warranty repair. Please describe what is happening and provide any proof of purchase you have available. Our support team may suggest safe checks that you can carry out yourself. Tell us if you are uncomfortable with a suggested check or cannot access the thermostat safely. We will arrange an appropriate assessment instead. You do not need to attempt a repair yourself to make a warranty claim.

We confirm a fault when our support team or an authorised engineer has enough information to identify the problem and establish that it is covered. We will tell you when this has happened and explain what comes next. If we believe the fault is not covered, we will give you the reason.

A warranty repair to the Lumen smart thermostat is completed within 38 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will keep you informed about the repair and contact you if the arrangements need to change. You can also ask our support team for an update.

If a repair to the Lumen smart thermostat takes longer than 8 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. There is no charge for this loan. We will explain how the replacement will be supplied and, where necessary, arrange for an authorised engineer to fit it safely.

The loaned replacement remains Halvard Home’s property. Please take reasonable care of it and use it according to the instructions supplied. Let us know if it develops a problem. Where a home visit is needed, we will agree the appointment with you and explain any access requirements. If the thermostat needs to leave your home, we will arrange collection and return without charge for a covered repair. We will provide packing instructions and suitable packaging where needed. Please do not disconnect the thermostat yourself unless our support team has confirmed that this is safe and appropriate.

Before carrying out work, the engineer will explain whether the heating needs to be switched off and how this may affect your home. Tell us if losing heating control could put someone at risk. We will discuss suitable arrangements rather than expecting you to manage without safe heating control.

A repair may involve fitting a new or refurbished part. Any refurbished part we use will have been inspected and tested for suitability. We will provide a repair record explaining the work carried out and any parts fitted. Repairing the thermostat does not remove the cover that remains under its original warranty. If you notice a problem with the completed repair, contact us and describe what has happened so that we can assess it.

Some repair work may require the thermostat’s settings to be reset. We will explain this before proceeding where possible and help you restore the settings needed for normal operation. An engineer visit for the Lumen smart thermostat after the warranty has ended costs £105.00. This is the visit charge, not an agreement to carry out additional paid work. We will explain any proposed repair charges and obtain your consent before proceeding. Nothing in this policy limits your statutory rights.

Keep your delivery confirmation and proof of purchase somewhere safe. These records help us confirm when your cover started and whether a reported fault falls within it. If your paperwork shows conflicting dates, contact Halvard Home so we can check the delivery record.

The cover period sets the limit for claims under this warranty. It does not mean that every fault, repair or expense is covered. A claim must also meet the warranty conditions, including those relating to normal domestic use, proper care and the cause of the fault.

Please report a fault as soon as you notice it. When you contact us, describe what has happened and provide your purchase and delivery details if available. We will check the relevant dates and explain whether the claim can be considered under the warranty.

A claim reported while the relevant cover is active will not lose eligibility simply because an agreed inspection or repair takes place after that cover expires. Please retain our acknowledgement of your report and follow any instructions needed to arrange access or provide supporting information.

Labour for repairs to the Keel washing machine is free for the first 34 months. This applies to labour needed for an approved warranty repair. It does not make work outside the warranty free, even where the appliance itself is still within its cover period.

After the free labour cover expires, you may need to pay labour charges for a repair even if the faulty part remains covered. We will explain any applicable charges before you agree to the work. You can ask us to clarify what is covered before deciding whether to proceed.

Parts fitted to the Keel washing machine during a warranty repair carry their own cover. Replacement parts fitted under the warranty are covered for a further 218 days. This cover starts on the date the replacement part is fitted, as recorded on the repair paperwork.

The replacement part cover applies to the fitted part, not to the appliance as a whole. Where the appliance’s original cover would protect that part for longer, that protection continues. Fitting a replacement part does not shorten the cover already available under the appliance warranty.

If replacement part cover continues beyond the appliance’s original expiry date, you can still report a fault affecting that part under its own cover. This does not extend cover to unrelated components. Labour remains subject to the labour terms explained above, and charges may therefore apply.

Keep the repair record with your purchase and delivery documents. It should identify the work carried out and the date the part was fitted. If these details are missing or appear incorrect, ask us to check them so that a later claim can be assessed accurately.

An inspection, repair or replacement part does not restart the appliance’s original cover period. The delivery date remains the reference point for that cover. Any separate protection for a fitted replacement part is assessed using the repair record and the terms set out here.

If it is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 41 days. The transfer deadline runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the available purchase, delivery and repair records.

Transferring the warranty changes the registered owner but does not restart or extend the cover. The new owner receives the cover that remains available, subject to the same warranty conditions. We will confirm the transfer and explain any missing information needed to complete it.

If you are unsure whether the appliance, a fitted part or repair labour is still covered, contact us before arranging work. We can check the records and explain the position. This warranty is additional to your legal rights and does not replace or restrict rights you may have against the seller.

The Ashby tumble dryer is covered for 36 months from the date of delivery. Keep your delivery confirmation with your purchase receipt so that the start of your cover can be checked if you need help.

If you collect the appliance rather than have it delivered, we treat the collection date as the delivery date for warranty purposes. Ask the retailer to record that date on your collection paperwork. If your documents show conflicting dates, contact Halvard Home so we can help establish when your cover began.

Please check your delivery details when you receive the appliance. If the recorded delivery date is wrong, tell us and provide any supporting information you have. Correcting an error does not create a new warranty; it ensures that your cover is measured from the proper starting point.

You do not need to use the appliance immediately for the warranty to begin. Leaving it packaged, keeping it in storage or delaying installation does not pause or extend the cover period. If you are planning to store it, follow the storage guidance supplied with the appliance to help protect it from damage.

Keep evidence of purchase and delivery somewhere accessible. A receipt, order confirmation or delivery record may help us confirm your entitlement to cover. If you cannot find your paperwork, contact the retailer or Halvard Home for help. Missing documents do not automatically mean that a valid claim will be refused.

Repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer include labour only for an opening period. Labour for repairs is free for the first 30 months. This applies to labour needed for repairs accepted under the warranty. It does not mean that every visit or service is covered, regardless of the reason for the work.

After the free labour period ends, an eligible repair may still include covered parts while a labour charge applies. We will explain any charge before you agree to the repair. You can ask us to clarify what is covered and what you would need to pay before deciding whether to proceed.

Replacement parts fitted to the Ashby tumble dryer are covered for a further 245 days. This separate cover begins on the date the replacement part is fitted under the warranty. Keep the repair record showing the fitting date, as this helps us establish the cover that applies if the replacement part develops a fault.

The replacement part cover applies to the fitted part, not to the whole appliance. It can continue after the appliance’s original cover has ended, but it does not restart or extend that original cover. It also does not renew the free labour period. We will explain any applicable labour charge before arranging work.

Having a repair carried out does not otherwise change the date on which the appliance’s warranty ends. Time spent waiting for an appointment or for a part does not automatically extend the cover. If Halvard Home agrees an extension in your case, we will confirm the revised position in writing.

If it is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 33 days. That transfer window runs from the date of sale. The seller should pass on the purchase evidence, delivery record and any repair paperwork so that the new owner can show the appliance’s history and the cover remaining.

To request a transfer, the new owner should contact Halvard Home with their contact details, evidence of the sale and the available warranty records. Transferring the warranty does not restart it. If a transfer is not requested within the required window, the new owner should contact us to discuss their position rather than assume that cover remains available. We will review the records and explain whether we can accept the transfer. A change of address alone does not restart the warranty or extend its duration.

Tell Halvard Home about a fault while the relevant cover is still active. Keep a record of your report and any correspondence. If we accept a claim made within the applicable cover period, an appointment arranged after that period ends will not, by itself, make the claim invalid.

This warranty is provided alongside your rights under consumer law. Its expiry does not necessarily mean that you have no remedy for a faulty appliance. Nothing in these cover periods removes or limits any legal rights you may have against the retailer or Halvard Home.

If your Keel washing machine develops a fault while its warranty is active, contact Halvard Home so we can assess the problem and arrange any repair covered by the warranty. Please stop using the machine if you suspect that continuing could make it unsafe or cause damage.

Tell us what happens when you try to use the machine, whether there are any unusual sounds or leaks, and what appears on the display. We may ask for a photograph or a description of the fault. Please do not remove covers or attempt electrical repairs yourself.

We will ask for proof of purchase and details that help us identify your machine and check its warranty. If you cannot find your receipt, tell us what purchase information you have. We will explain whether this is enough to establish cover or whether supporting information is needed.

Our support team may suggest checks that you can safely carry out, such as checking that the door is shut properly or that the water supply is available. We will explain each check clearly. If you cannot carry it out safely, let us know so we can arrange suitable help.

A warranty repair to the Keel washing machine is completed within 24 working days of the fault being confirmed. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and explain what the repair involves. We will also tell you how to contact us for an update.

Where the fault is covered, Halvard Home pays for the work and parts needed to put it right, including the engineer’s visit. We will not ask you to pay for covered repair work. An engineer visit for the Keel washing machine after the warranty has ended costs £61.00. This charge is for the visit, rather than an agreement to carry out whatever repair may be needed. We will explain any proposed repair charges and ask for your agreement before proceeding.

We will agree access arrangements with you when booking a repair. Please make sure the engineer can reach the machine safely and can access its water and electricity connections. Tell us about restricted access, stairs or any other conditions that could affect the work.

Please empty the drum and remove belongings from around the machine before the engineer attends. Keep children and pets away from the working area. You do not need to disconnect or move the machine unless we have explained how to do so safely and you are comfortable doing it.

If you need to change an appointment, contact us so we can make alternative arrangements. If an engineer cannot gain access or finds that the area is unsafe, we will explain what needs to change before the repair can go ahead.

Some repairs to the Keel washing machine need parts that are not held in stock. If a repair takes longer than 26 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. We will contact you to arrange delivery and explain the arrangements for its use and return.

The loan machine may look different from your own machine, but we will explain its controls and any relevant installation requirements. Please look after it, follow the instructions supplied and tell us if it develops a fault. We will arrange its collection in connection with the return of your repaired machine.

Refurbished parts are sometimes fitted to the Keel washing machine when new parts are scarce. A refurbished part is covered for 50 weeks. These parts are checked for safety, condition and suitability before fitting. We will tell you if a refurbished part has been used and explain how to report a problem with it.

After the repair, the engineer will check that the machine operates correctly and explain the work carried out. We will provide a repair record identifying the fault and the parts fitted, where applicable. Keep this record with your purchase documents so it is available if you need further support.

If the same fault returns, or you believe the repair has not resolved the problem, contact Halvard Home and describe what is happening. We will review the repair record and explain the next steps. You do not need to diagnose the cause yourself.

Repairs under this warranty do not affect your legal rights. If you are unhappy with how a repair has been handled, ask us to review the case. We will explain our findings and how to raise a complaint if you remain dissatisfied.

If your Ashby tumble dryer develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Please describe what has happened, whether the appliance can still be used safely, and any signs of damage. We will explain what information we need and how your repair request will be handled.

We may ask for proof of purchase and details from the appliance’s identification label. These help us confirm that the warranty applies and identify the correct parts. If you cannot find your purchase documents or cannot safely reach the label, tell us so that we can discuss alternative ways to check your entitlement.

We may suggest simple checks that can be carried out safely, such as checking that the door is closed or that the lint filter is clear. We will not ask you to remove protective panels, touch internal wiring or attempt a repair. Please tell us if you cannot carry out a suggested check.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or visible electrical damage, stop using the appliance. Switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply if it is safe to do so. Do not use it again until you have been advised that it is safe. Seek emergency help if there is an immediate danger.

A warranty repair to the Ashby tumble dryer is completed within 23 working days of the fault being confirmed.

We will tell you when this has happened and explain the proposed repair. If an engineer needs to inspect the appliance before confirming the fault, we will make that clear.

We will arrange an engineer appointment with you and explain any access requirements. Please tell us about parking restrictions, stairs, narrow entrances or anything else that could affect safe access. Let us know if you need an accessible way to communicate or support with the appointment arrangements.

The engineer will assess the fault and carry out the work covered by the warranty. This may involve repairing or replacing faulty components. Replacement parts will be suitable for the appliance and meet our safety and performance requirements. We will explain the work completed and provide a repair record for you to keep.

Warranty cover applies to faults arising from defective materials or workmanship under normal household use. It does not cover damage caused by misuse, accidental damage, unsuitable installation or failure to follow the care instructions. A repair carried out elsewhere does not automatically remove your rights, but damage caused by that work may fall outside the warranty.

If our assessment finds that the problem is not covered, we will explain why. We will also explain any proposed charges before asking you to agree to work outside the warranty. You do not have to accept a paid repair, and we will not treat your request for a warranty assessment as permission to carry one out.

An engineer visit for the Ashby tumble dryer after the warranty has ended costs £56.00.

We will also consider whether the fault relates to a repair already covered by the warranty or whether your statutory rights may apply.

If you need to change an appointment, contact us so that we can discuss alternative arrangements. If access is unavailable or the appliance cannot be worked on safely, we will explain what needs to change before the repair can proceed. We will keep you informed about the status of your request.

If a repair does not resolve the reported fault, contact us with your repair record or the details of your visit. We will review the work and explain the appropriate remedy. Nothing in this warranty limits your statutory rights, including rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the appliance.

The Vale fridge freezer is covered for 77 months from the date of delivery. This is the warranty period for faults covered by Halvard Home’s warranty. The delivery date, rather than the date you placed your order or paid for your appliance, determines when this cover starts.

If your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation show different dates, we use the delivery confirmation to establish the start of cover. If you collected the appliance yourself, we treat the collection date shown on your collection record as the delivery date.

If you cannot find your delivery confirmation, contact Halvard Home with the purchase information you have. We will review the available records and explain what evidence we need. Missing paperwork does not automatically mean that your warranty claim will be refused.

Registering your appliance helps us keep your details with your warranty record, but registration does not change the date on which cover begins. A delay in registering the Vale fridge freezer does not move the start of cover or extend its expiry date.

Cover runs from delivery even if you choose not to install or use the appliance straight away. Leaving it packaged, storing it, moving home or disconnecting it does not pause the warranty. Please follow the care and storage instructions supplied with the appliance.

To ask for help under the warranty, contact Halvard Home while your cover is active. Tell us what has happened and provide the information needed to identify your appliance. We will check your warranty record and explain how your claim will be assessed.

If you report a covered fault while the warranty is active, the claim remains eligible for assessment even if the warranty expires while we arrange an inspection or repair. This does not bring unrelated faults reported after expiry within the original cover.
