If you believe a replacement part has developed a fault, contact us with the repair details. We will check the fitting record and explain which cover applies. You do not need to diagnose the fault yourself before asking us to assess it.

If the Vale fridge freezer is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 44 days. This requirement applies from the date of the sale. The transfer carries across the existing cover; it does not start a fresh warranty or change the original expiry date.

The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale, the original purchase and delivery details, and any relevant repair records. We may ask the previous owner to confirm the transfer where this is needed to establish the appliance’s warranty history.

If the transfer requirement is not met, the new owner cannot claim under this warranty unless Halvard Home agrees otherwise in writing. Contact us if records are missing or ownership details are unclear, so we can explain the available options.

When the applicable cover expires, repairs are not covered by this warranty. We can explain any available repair options and confirm whether charges would apply before you authorise work. Expiry does not affect an eligible claim already reported to us while cover was active.

This warranty is provided in addition to your legal rights. Those rights may allow you to seek a remedy from the seller even where this warranty has expired or does not apply. Nothing in these cover period terms limits or replaces your rights under consumer law.

If your Vale fridge freezer develops a fault that you believe is covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home customer support. Describe what has happened and how the appliance is behaving. We will explain how to arrange an assessment and what information we need to check your warranty cover.

Please have your proof of purchase available, together with the details shown on the appliance’s identification label. If you cannot find these, tell us so that we can help you locate them or discuss suitable evidence of purchase. Do not move the appliance if doing so would be unsafe.

We may suggest checks that you can safely carry out yourself, such as checking that the door closes properly or that the power supply is working. You do not need to remove panels, handle wiring or attempt a repair. Tell us if you are uncomfortable carrying out a suggested check.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, damaged wiring or signs of an electrical fault, stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if it is safe to do so. Contact us for advice rather than trying to investigate the fault yourself.

A warranty repair to the Vale fridge freezer is completed within 7 working days of the fault being confirmed.

We confirm the fault when our assessment establishes what is wrong and that the repair is covered by the warranty. We will tell you when this has happened and explain the proposed repair. If an engineer needs to inspect the appliance to confirm the fault, we will arrange an appointment with you.

Please tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything that could make the visit difficult or unsafe. Let us know about accessibility needs so that we can discuss suitable arrangements. The engineer will need clear, safe access to the appliance and its electricity supply.

You do not need to disconnect or move the appliance unless we have explained how to do so safely and you are comfortable with the request. Keep children and pets away from the work area. The engineer may ask you to remove food or stored items where these would obstruct the repair.

Repairs covered by the warranty include the work and parts needed to correct the confirmed fault. Our engineer will explain what needs to be done. If the inspection identifies work outside the warranty, we will explain why and ask for your agreement before carrying out work that you would have to pay for.

A fault may fall outside the warranty if it results from misuse, accidental damage or an installation that does not follow the supplied instructions. We will consider the circumstances rather than assume that damage or an unrelated alteration caused the reported fault. Our decision will be explained clearly.

Only an engineer authorised by Halvard Home should carry out a repair arranged under this warranty. If you have already asked someone else to inspect or repair the appliance, tell us what they did. This helps us assess the fault safely and explain whether their work affects the proposed warranty repair.

We will keep you informed about the repair and contact you if the arrangements change. If we cannot complete the work as promised, we will explain the reason, discuss the next steps and tell you how to raise concerns. You should not have to chase an explanation for a missed appointment.

If a repair to the Vale fridge freezer takes longer than 25 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

We will contact you to arrange delivery and explain the loan terms in plain language. The replacement remains Halvard Home’s property. Please use it in accordance with the instructions provided and take reasonable care of it. Tell us if it develops a fault so that we can help.

The engineer will check the repaired appliance and explain the work carried out. Ask about anything you do not understand, including whether it is ready to use. If the fault remains or returns, contact us and describe what you have noticed so that we can review the repair.

Please take care with food affected by a cooling fault and follow appropriate food safety advice. Do not rely on smell or appearance alone to decide whether food is safe. Tell us about losses you believe resulted from the fault; we will explain how to submit a claim and how it will be assessed.

Your warranty does not replace or restrict your statutory rights. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the appliance. If you disagree with a warranty decision or are unhappy with the repair, contact Halvard Home customer support and ask for your complaint to be reviewed.

The Corra induction hob is covered for 43 months from the date of delivery. This is the warranty period for the appliance. It begins when the hob is delivered to you, rather than when you install it, register it or start using it.

Keep your delivery confirmation with your purchase receipt. These documents help us establish when your cover began and whether a fault falls within the warranty period. If your receipt shows a purchase date rather than a delivery date, we may ask for delivery evidence.

If you cannot find your delivery confirmation, contact Halvard Home. We will help you look for suitable evidence, such as a retailer’s delivery record. Missing paperwork does not automatically mean that your claim will be refused, but we need to establish the delivery date.

Registering your hob helps us manage warranty enquiries, but it does not change when cover starts or ends. A delay in installation does not move the start date. The warranty runs from delivery even if the hob remains unpacked or unused.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 35 months. This applies to work needed to repair a fault accepted under the warranty and arranged through Halvard Home. It does not cover work you arrange independently without our agreement.

After the free labour cover ends, the appliance warranty continues until its stated expiry date, but labour charges may apply. We will explain any proposed charges before you agree to a repair. You can ask us to clarify what is covered before authorising work.

The end of free labour cover does not, by itself, end cover for eligible replacement parts. When assessing a repair, we will explain how the appliance cover, replacement part cover and labour terms apply to your claim.

Replacement parts fitted to the Corra induction hob are covered for a further 189 days. This cover starts on the date the part is fitted during a repair authorised by Halvard Home. Keep the repair confirmation, as it records the fitting date.

Replacement part cover applies to the fitted part, not to the whole hob. It can continue beyond the appliance warranty’s expiry date. If the appliance warranty would cover that part for longer, fitting a replacement does not shorten that existing cover.

Fitting a replacement part does not restart the appliance warranty or renew free labour cover. If a fitted part develops a fault, contact us with the repair details. We will explain whether the part remains covered and whether labour charges apply.

Tell us about a fault as soon as you notice it. Describe what happens when you use the hob and provide your delivery or repair documents where available. Do not keep using the hob if you believe it may be unsafe.

If you report an eligible fault before the relevant cover expires, we will assess it using the date you contacted us. An appointment arranged after expiry will not, by itself, make that reported fault ineligible. Keep a copy of our acknowledgement.

A repair does not pause or extend the appliance warranty. The specific cover for replacement parts remains available as described above. We will make the applicable expiry position clear in your repair record so that you can keep it with your warranty documents.

If the Corra induction hob is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 27 days. The transfer deadline runs from the date of sale. The seller should pass on the purchase evidence, delivery confirmation and any repair records.

The new owner should contact Halvard Home to request the transfer and provide evidence of the sale. We may also ask for details that identify the hob. We will confirm when the warranty record has been updated.

Selling the hob does not restart its warranty. The new owner receives the cover that remains, subject to the same terms, including the position on labour charges. Any active replacement part cover stays linked to the relevant fitted part and its repair record.

If you are unsure whether cover is still active, contact us before arranging work. We can check the available records and explain the warranty position. This warranty is additional to your legal rights as a consumer and does not limit them.

If your Corra induction hob develops a fault covered by the warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging for the covered parts or labour. We will explain what happens next and help you prepare for the engineer’s visit. Your legal rights are not affected by this warranty.

Contact our customer support team to report the fault. Tell us what happens when you try to use the hob, whether anything unusual appears on the controls, and whether the problem is constant or comes and goes. Please have your proof of purchase available so we can check the warranty.

We may ask you to carry out simple checks, such as checking the controls or confirming that suitable cookware is being used. Only follow instructions that you can carry out safely. You do not need to remove the hob, open its casing or handle electrical connections.

Stop using the hob if the glass is cracked, you notice a burning smell, or you believe it may be unsafe. If it is safe to do so, switch it off at the electrical isolator. Tell customer support about any safety concern when you contact us.

An engineer will assess the fault and decide what repair is needed. Warranty cover applies to faults arising from defective materials or workmanship under normal household use. Damage caused by misuse, accidental impact, unsuitable installation or unauthorised alterations may not be covered. We will explain our assessment clearly.

If we believe the fault falls outside the warranty, we will tell you why before carrying out chargeable work. We will explain the proposed work and its cost, and ask for your agreement. You can decline a chargeable repair without agreeing to work you do not want.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the hob safely. Clear cookware and personal belongings from the surrounding worktop, and tell us about access restrictions when arranging the visit. Let us know if you need adjustments to the appointment arrangements because of a disability or other support need.

The engineer may be able to repair the hob in your home. If specialist equipment or workshop work is needed, we will explain how removal and return will be arranged. Please do not disconnect or transport the hob yourself unless we have expressly agreed a safe arrangement with you.

If a repair to the Corra induction hob takes longer than 9 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

We will contact you to arrange the loan and explain how the replacement will be supplied, used and returned. The replacement may look different from your hob, but we will make sure it is suitable for the agreed arrangement. Any installation must be completed safely by an appropriately qualified person.

Please take reasonable care of the replacement and follow the instructions supplied with it. Tell us if it develops a fault or is damaged. Do not attempt to repair or alter it. We will arrange its return as part of completing your repair and restoring your hob to use.

Refurbished parts are sometimes fitted to the Corra induction hob when new parts are scarce. A refurbished part is covered for 45 weeks.

Any refurbished part we fit will be checked for safety, condition and suitability. We will record the parts used in the repair and explain the cover that applies. Using a refurbished part does not remove your legal rights or reduce the warranty cover that otherwise applies to the hob.

We will keep you informed if the repair is delayed, if the engineer finds further damage, or if the proposed work changes. Please keep your contact details up to date so we can reach you. If you need to change an appointment, contact customer support so we can rearrange it.

After the repair, the engineer will check that the hob operates safely and explain any relevant care advice. Keep the repair record with your proof of purchase. If the fault returns or you are unhappy with the work, contact us and describe the problem so we can review it.

An engineer visit for the Corra induction hob after the warranty has ended costs £74.00.

This visit charge is separate from any charge for repair work or parts outside warranty cover. We will explain applicable charges before you agree to them. If you believe the fault should still be dealt with under your legal rights, tell us so we can consider that separately from the warranty.

The Fenwick cooker hood is covered for 66 months from the date of delivery. This cover applies under the terms of the Halvard Home warranty. Your delivery date determines when the warranty begins, rather than the date you place your order or arrange installation.

Keep your delivery confirmation with your purchase receipt and warranty details. These records help us confirm that your Fenwick cooker hood is covered when you contact us. You can keep paper copies or clear digital copies, whichever you find easier to access.

If your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation show different dates, we use the delivery date to establish the start of your cover. We may ask for supporting information if the delivery record is missing, unclear or does not match our records.

If you cannot find your delivery confirmation, please contact Halvard Home. We can check the information available to us and explain what other evidence we can accept. Missing paperwork does not automatically mean that your warranty claim will be refused.

Installing or starting to use the Fenwick cooker hood after delivery does not move the warranty start date. Leaving it packaged, storing it or delaying work in your kitchen does not pause the cover or change its end date.

Registering your Fenwick cooker hood helps us keep your warranty details accessible. Registration does not replace proof of delivery, and it does not change when your cover begins. Please check the information you provide and tell us if anything needs correcting.

Contact us when you notice a fault that you believe may be covered. Describe what has happened and provide the delivery details if you have them. We will explain how your claim will be assessed and whether an inspection is needed.

We use the date you report the fault when checking whether your claim was raised while the warranty was active. If we arrange an inspection or repair after the original cover ends, that scheduling does not by itself invalidate an otherwise eligible claim.

Reporting a fault does not automatically establish that it is covered. The cause of the fault and the applicable warranty terms still need to be checked. We will explain our decision and let you know if we need further information.

A repair under the warranty does not restart the original cover for the Fenwick cooker hood. Its original end date remains linked to delivery, subject to the separate protection for replacement parts described below and any rights you have under law.

Replacement parts fitted to the Fenwick cooker hood are covered for a further 348 days. This parts cover begins on the date the replacement part is fitted under an authorised warranty repair. Keep the repair confirmation so that the fitting date can be checked.

The replacement parts cover applies to the part supplied and fitted, rather than restarting cover for the entire Fenwick cooker hood. If the original warranty is still active, it continues according to its existing terms alongside the protection for the replacement part.

Ask us if you are unsure which cover applies to a fault following a repair. We will check the delivery and repair records and explain the position. You do not need to decide which warranty provision applies before contacting us.

If the Fenwick cooker hood is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 39 days. This requirement runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home to request the transfer and provide evidence of the change of ownership.

The seller should pass on the delivery confirmation, purchase receipt and any repair records. These documents help the new owner establish the original warranty dates and identify any replacement parts that remain covered. Personal information unrelated to the warranty can be removed.

Transferring the warranty does not restart or extend the original cover. The new owner receives the benefit of the cover that remains valid, subject to the warranty terms. We will confirm the transfer and explain any information still needed to complete our records.

If the transfer requirement has not been met, the new owner should contact us so that we can explain the position. Do not assume that a change of ownership has been recorded simply because the seller has provided the original paperwork.

This warranty is provided by Halvard Home in addition to your statutory rights. Its start date, end date and transfer requirements do not remove or restrict rights that cannot legally be excluded. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the Fenwick cooker hood.

If your Fenwick cooker hood develops a fault covered by the warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair without charging you for the necessary parts, labour or engineer travel. We will explain what happens next and keep you informed as your repair progresses.

Contact our customer care team to report the fault. Please describe what is happening and have your proof of purchase available, together with the product details shown on the appliance label. If you cannot find these details, we will help you locate them safely.

We may ask about installation, use and cleaning to help establish the cause of the problem. We may also suggest checks that you can safely carry out yourself. You do not need to remove covers, handle wiring or dismantle the appliance to make a claim.

Stop using the Fenwick cooker hood if it produces smoke, smells of burning or appears electrically unsafe. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely. Tell us about the concern when you contact us so that we can arrange appropriate support.

We confirm a fault through the information you provide, remote assessment or an engineer’s inspection, as appropriate. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and whether it is covered. If we decline cover, we will explain the reason clearly and give you the opportunity to provide further information.

Warranty cover applies to faults arising from defective materials or workmanship under normal household use. It does not cover damage caused by misuse, accidental damage, unsuitable installation or alterations that cause the fault. A fault unrelated to such circumstances will still be assessed fairly.

Where an engineer needs to visit, we will agree an appointment with you. Please make sure the engineer can safely reach the Fenwick cooker hood and its electrical connection. Let us know about access restrictions or support needs when the appointment is arranged.

A warranty repair to the Fenwick cooker hood is completed within 37 working days of the fault being confirmed. We are responsible for arranging the work and obtaining the parts needed. If there is a problem with the arrangements, we will contact you and explain how we will resolve it.

If a repair to the Fenwick cooker hood takes longer than 10 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement. We will contact you to arrange the loan, explain how the replacement can be used safely and organise any installation needed for its safe use.

The loan replacement remains the property of Halvard Home. There is no loan charge while your warranty repair is being completed. We will explain the care arrangements and agree how it will be collected, without leaving you responsible for disconnecting equipment that requires professional attention.

Our engineer will assess the fault and carry out the work needed to restore normal operation. This may involve adjusting the appliance or replacing faulty parts. We use suitable parts that meet our safety and performance requirements, and we may use refurbished parts where appropriate.

A refurbished part fitted to the Fenwick cooker hood is covered for 17 weeks. This cover applies to defects in the fitted part and includes the work needed to put those defects right. It does not reduce any protection remaining under your appliance warranty.

Please tell us if the fault continues after the repair or if you notice a problem with the work. We will review the repair record and arrange the appropriate action. You do not need to diagnose the cause yourself before contacting us for help.

After completing the work, the engineer will check that the Fenwick cooker hood operates safely and explain what has been repaired. We will provide a record of the work and identify any relevant care advice. Please keep this record with your warranty information.

An engineer visit for the Fenwick cooker hood after the warranty has ended costs £110.00. We will explain what the visit charge includes before you book. Any proposed repair charges will be explained separately, and chargeable repair work will require your agreement.

If you are unhappy with a repair or a decision about cover, contact our customer care team and ask for a review. We will consider the information you provide and explain our response. Your warranty is additional to your legal rights and does not limit them.

The Mira robot vacuum is covered for 40 months from the date of delivery. This cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship during normal domestic use, subject to the warranty terms. The delivery date is the date the Mira robot vacuum reached you, rather than the date you placed your order or made payment.

Keep your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation somewhere safe. These documents help us check when your cover began and whether a reported fault falls within it. If your receipt does not show the delivery date, we may ask for a delivery email or other evidence from the retailer.

If you cannot find your documents, contact Halvard Home with the details you have. We will explain what evidence we can accept and help you identify the delivery date where possible. We need to establish that date before confirming whether a repair is covered, so please do not assume that registration alone proves eligibility.

Registering your Mira robot vacuum helps us keep your warranty details available when you need support. Registration does not change the date on which cover starts or ends. An unregistered Mira robot vacuum may still qualify for cover if you can provide suitable evidence of purchase and delivery.

Labour for repairs to the Mira robot vacuum is free for the first 22 months. This applies where we confirm that the fault qualifies under the warranty and arrange or approve the repair. It does not apply to routine cleaning, maintenance or work needed because of damage that the warranty excludes.

After the labour cover ends, eligible replacement parts remain covered until the warranty expires, but repair labour becomes chargeable. We will explain the proposed work and any charges before asking you to approve it. We will not treat your request for advice or an assessment as permission to carry out chargeable work.

Other charges may apply where the fault is not covered or where you request a service outside the warranty. If that happens, we will explain the reason and the available options before proceeding. You can decide whether to accept the proposed service after reviewing the information we provide.

Contact Halvard Home when you notice a fault that you believe may be covered. Tell us what happened, how the Mira robot vacuum behaves and whether it shows signs of damage. If continued use could be unsafe or could worsen the fault, stop using it and ask us for guidance.

We assess eligibility using the delivery date, the nature of the fault and the information supporting your claim. A claim accepted while the relevant cover is active does not lose that eligibility simply because our repair arrangements continue beyond its expiry. Charges already explained and agreed still apply.

Repairing the Mira robot vacuum does not restart or extend the warranty. If we replace it as part of an accepted warranty claim, the replacement carries the cover left under the original warranty. Keep the repair or replacement confirmation with your purchase documents so that the warranty history remains clear.

If the Mira robot vacuum is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 37 days. This deadline runs from the date ownership changes. The transfer allows the new owner to use the cover that remains; it does not create a fresh warranty or renew labour cover.

To arrange a transfer, the new owner should contact Halvard Home and provide evidence of the original purchase and delivery, together with evidence showing when ownership changed. The seller should pass on the relevant documents. We may ask for further information if the records do not clearly establish eligibility.

The condition and history of the Mira robot vacuum remain relevant after a transfer. Selling it does not make an excluded fault eligible or remove charges that apply under the warranty. If the transfer deadline is missed, the new owner cannot claim under this warranty, although other legal rights may still apply.

When cover expires, you can still contact Halvard Home for advice about repair options. We will explain whether we can help and what charges would apply before you commit to a service. Expiry does not affect an accepted claim that remains unresolved under the applicable warranty terms.

This warranty is provided in addition to your statutory rights. Its cover dates, labour terms and transfer requirements do not limit rights you may have against the retailer under consumer law. If you are unsure whether to contact Halvard Home or the retailer, we can explain the warranty route without asking you to give up those rights.

If your Mira robot vacuum develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair and cover the necessary labour, parts and transport. We will explain what happens next and keep you informed as your repair progresses.

Please contact our customer support team before sending your Mira robot vacuum to us or arranging work through a repairer. Tell us what is happening, how the fault affects normal use and whether the appliance displays a warning. Photos or a description of unusual sounds may help us assess the problem.

We may ask for proof of purchase and information that helps us identify your Mira robot vacuum. If you cannot find your receipt, please speak to us about alternative evidence. We will explain what we need rather than asking you to send unrelated personal information.

Our support team may suggest checks that are safe to carry out at home. These might include checking for a blockage or cleaning an accessible sensor. Do not open sealed components or attempt electrical repairs. If a check feels unsafe or unclear, stop and ask us for help.

Warranty repairs cover faults that fall within the warranty terms. Damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or an unsuitable repair may fall outside that cover. We will assess the cause fairly and explain our decision using the information available, including what our repair team finds.

If inspection shows that the fault is not covered, we will tell you why and explain the available options. We will ask for your agreement before carrying out work that you would need to pay for. You can decline that work without giving up your legal rights.

When a repair is authorised, we will provide instructions for collection or delivery. Please follow those instructions so that your Mira robot vacuum reaches the repair team safely. Let us know if your circumstances make the proposed arrangements difficult, and we will discuss a suitable alternative.

Before packing your Mira robot vacuum, empty the dust container and remove loose debris where it is safe to do so. Pack it securely using suitable protective material. Send accessories only if we ask for them, and do not include personal belongings.

Please tell us about damage or a safety concern before the appliance is transported. If it is smoking, leaking or unusually hot, stop using it and seek guidance from our support team. Do not package or send an appliance that appears unsafe to handle.

Our repair team will inspect your Mira robot vacuum to confirm the fault and decide what work is needed. We will let you know when the fault has been confirmed and explain the repair arrangements.

A warranty repair to the Mira robot vacuum is completed within 13 working days of the fault being confirmed.

The repair may involve adjusting components, replacing faulty parts or updating the software needed for normal operation. We use parts that meet our safety and performance requirements. These may be new or refurbished, depending on the repair required and the parts available.

A refurbished part fitted to the Mira robot vacuum is covered for 33 weeks.

We will record the work carried out and test your Mira robot vacuum before returning it. The testing checks that the reported fault has been addressed and that the appliance operates safely. Your repair record will identify the parts replaced and explain the work in plain language.

If an unexpected problem affects the repair, we will contact you, explain the reason and discuss the arrangements. You should not have to chase us to find out whether your Mira robot vacuum is still being repaired.

If a repair to the Mira robot vacuum takes longer than 30 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

The loan is arranged by our support team, who will explain delivery, care and return arrangements. Halvard Home covers the transport for the loan. Please look after the replacement, use it according to its instructions and tell us if it develops a fault or is damaged.

When your repaired Mira robot vacuum is ready, we will agree suitable return arrangements with you. Please check it when it arrives and contact us if you notice transport damage, missing requested accessories or a problem with the repair.

If the reported fault remains or returns, contact our support team with your repair details. We will review what happened and explain the appropriate remedy. A warranty repair does not remove or restrict your legal rights, including rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the Mira robot vacuum.

Extended Care extends the standard warranty by 58 months. It adds protection against covered mechanical and electrical faults after the standard warranty ends, helping you arrange a repair without having to find an independent repairer yourself.

The plan applies to the appliance identified in your plan confirmation. That confirmation also shows when your extended cover begins and ends. Keep it with your proof of purchase so that we can check your cover when you contact us.

Extended Care covers the reasonable cost of diagnosing an accepted fault, supplying the parts needed for the repair and carrying out the work. We arrange the repair through an approved service provider.

Cover applies where a fault develops through normal domestic use and is not caused by an excluded event. The appliance must have been installed, used and cared for in line with the instructions supplied with it.

Each claim under Extended Care carries an excess of £11.00. We explain how to pay the excess when arranging your claim. Repair visits arranged as part of the same accepted claim do not attract a separate excess.

If we establish that the reported fault is not covered, we explain why before asking you to approve any chargeable work. You can decline that work. We do not treat a request for help as agreement to an unrelated repair charge.

If an approved repair does not resolve the reported fault, contact us so that we can review the work. Where the problem remains part of the accepted claim, we arrange further action under that claim.

Our aim is to restore the appliance to proper working order. A repair may involve replacement parts that differ in appearance from the originals, provided they are suitable and do not reduce its safety or intended performance.

If repair is not practical, we may offer a replacement instead. We explain the proposed replacement and any arrangements for delivery, collection or installation before you decide whether to accept it.

A replacement will be comparable in its main functions, but its appearance and features may differ. We discuss any material differences with you rather than assuming that an alternative will meet your needs.

Accepting a replacement does not restart Extended Care. Any remaining cover continues under the existing plan, with our records updated to identify the replacement. We confirm this arrangement in writing.

The plan does not cover routine cleaning, maintenance or adjustments that form part of normal care. It also excludes consumable items that are intended to be used up or replaced through ordinary use.

Cosmetic damage is not covered where it does not affect safe operation or proper working order. This includes marks, scratches and changes in finish caused by ordinary wear.

Extended Care does not cover accidental damage, deliberate damage, theft or loss. It does not cover faults caused by misuse, unsuitable installation, unauthorised alterations or repairs that cause or worsen the problem.

Damage caused by external events, such as flooding, fire or an unsuitable electrical supply, is excluded. We assess the cause of a fault using the information available and explain the basis for any decision to decline cover.

You do not have to diagnose the problem yourself. Tell us what has happened and describe any warning signs. We may suggest safe checks, but we will not ask you to dismantle the appliance.

Stop using the appliance if you believe it may be unsafe. Follow any safety advice in the supplied instructions and let us know about hazards when you contact us.

To arrange a repair, we need safe access to the appliance and enough information to identify your plan. Tell us about access restrictions or support needs so that we can discuss suitable arrangements.

Please contact us before commissioning work you want the plan to cover. We cannot guarantee reimbursement for repairs arranged independently without our approval, because we may be unable to verify the fault or assess the proposed work.

Extended Care pays for the covered repair or agreed replacement, rather than losses arising from being unable to use the appliance. It does not provide compensation for inconvenience or damage to other belongings.

These exclusions do not remove any responsibility that the law prevents us from excluding. Nothing in Extended Care limits your statutory rights, including rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the appliance.

If you disagree with a claim decision, you can ask us to review it and provide supporting information. We explain our reasons clearly and tell you how to use our complaints process if you remain dissatisfied.

cell.item: POL-WAR/Extended Care Plus/What the plan adds

result.text:
Extended Care Plus extends the standard warranty by 50 months. It adds protection against covered mechanical and electrical faults that arise through normal domestic use. The plan is designed to help you arrange an approved repair if your appliance stops working as it should.

Each claim under Extended Care Plus carries an excess of £90.00. We will explain how to pay the excess when your claim is accepted. Paying the excess does not bring an excluded fault within cover or change the other conditions of the plan.

For an accepted claim, the plan covers the labour and replacement parts needed to put right the covered fault. Halvard Home will arrange the repair through an approved service provider. Please contact us before arranging work yourself, as repairs arranged independently are not covered unless we have authorised them.

The plan also gives you access to support with identifying a fault and deciding whether a repair visit is needed. We may ask you to describe what has happened, explain what you have already checked, or provide photographs where these would help us assess the problem.

Any checks we suggest will be suitable for you to carry out safely. You should not remove protective panels, touch internal electrical parts or attempt a repair yourself. If you notice smoke, a burning smell or another sign of danger, stop using the appliance and contact us.

Cover applies to the appliance recorded in your plan confirmation. Please check that the details are correct and tell us about any mistakes. Keep your proof of purchase and plan confirmation somewhere accessible, as we may need these documents to confirm that your claim is eligible.

The added cover is for faults, rather than routine upkeep. You remain responsible for cleaning, care and maintenance in line with the instructions supplied with your appliance. The plan does not replace those responsibilities or cover work needed solely because normal maintenance has been neglected.

Accidental damage, deliberate damage and damage caused by misuse are outside this cover. Faults caused by unsuitable installation, unauthorised alterations or use that conflicts with the supplied instructions are also excluded. We will explain the reason if we decide that an exclusion applies to your claim.

Changes in appearance are not covered where they do not affect normal operation. These may include scratches, dents, fading or marks from ordinary use. If an appearance issue is linked to a functional fault, we will assess the functional fault under the plan rather than dismiss it as cosmetic.

The plan does not cover problems caused by an external supply, household wiring or plumbing, or conditions outside the appliance itself. Our support team may help you distinguish these problems from an appliance fault, but arranging work on your home remains your responsibility.

If we arrange a visit, you must provide safe and reasonable access to the appliance. Tell us about anything that could affect access, including building restrictions or a difficult installation position. We will explain any preparation needed so that the service provider can carry out the agreed work safely.

Replacement parts may differ in appearance from the original parts, but must be suitable for the repair and maintain the appliance’s intended function. We may use new or refurbished parts that meet our quality requirements. The service provider will explain any relevant differences before fitting them.

If an approved repair is not practical, we will discuss the available remedy with you under the plan terms. A replacement or another remedy is not automatic. We will explain our assessment and any proposal clearly so that you understand what is being offered.
