Keep the original packaging if you have it, but contact us if it is unavailable or damaged. We will explain what protection is suitable for your return. Missing packaging does not, by itself, remove your legal rights where an item is faulty, not as described or otherwise fails to meet legal requirements.

Please keep the route to the collection point clear and make sure pets are safely away from the area. Do not move a heavy or awkward item if doing so could cause harm. Discuss its location with us during booking so that the collection team understands what will be required.

If you cannot be available for the agreed collection, contact customer support to change the arrangements. We will explain what happens next and whether a charge could apply under the terms of your return. We will not ask you to accept a collection charge without explaining the reason for it.

If the driver cannot safely access or collect the return, they may leave it at the property. We will then contact you to discuss the problem and arrange a suitable next step. If collection does not take place as agreed, please let us know so we can investigate and help resolve it.

At handover, the driver may check that the return matches the booking and record its visible condition. Please retain the collection confirmation or receipt provided. If you believe the collection record is inaccurate, contact customer support and explain your concern so we can review it alongside the information from the collection team.

Collection does not itself confirm that a refund has been approved. We will assess the return against the reason given and your legal rights, then explain the outcome. Where a refund is due, we will confirm how it will be processed, including the treatment of any eligible delivery charge.

We normally send an approved refund to the payment method used for the purchase. If that is not possible, customer support will discuss an appropriate alternative with you. We will explain any proposed deduction and its basis. Nothing in these collection arrangements limits your statutory rights.

If you are returning an item from an address in Midlands, contact Halvard Home to arrange a collection. Please have your order details available and explain why you wish to return the item. We will check your request, explain the applicable return conditions and confirm whether a collection can be arranged.

Collections in Midlands are made within 35 working days of a return being booked. Your return is booked when we confirm that the collection request has been accepted. Sending an enquiry or telling us that you are considering a return does not book a collection.

When booking, please check that your collection address and contact details are correct. Tell us about any access restrictions, including stairs, controlled entrances, parking restrictions or building rules that could affect the driver. Accurate information helps us arrange a safe collection and identify anything that needs to be discussed with you.

We will explain how your collection arrangements will be confirmed. Collection drivers in Midlands give an arrival window of 224 minutes. Please make sure that someone authorised to hand over the return can be present for the collection. If the arrangements are unsuitable, contact us to discuss your options rather than leaving the item unattended.

Please tell us if your circumstances change after booking. This includes changes to the collection address, access arrangements or the contact details you provided. Changes may mean that we need to review the booking. We will explain any effect on your collection and confirm the revised arrangements with you.

Prepare the item according to the return instructions we give you. Remove your belongings and check that nothing you wish to keep has been left inside or attached. Where relevant, remove personal information and sign out of linked accounts. Contact us if you need help understanding how to prepare your return.

The item must be safe for the driver to handle. If it requires disconnection, follow the safety guidance supplied with it and use a suitably qualified professional where necessary. Do not attempt work that you are not qualified to carry out. Collection drivers cannot carry out disconnection work as part of a return collection.

Please tell us about damage, exposed parts, leaks or anything else that could make collection unsafe. Do not handle an item if doing so could put you or someone else at risk. We will discuss the circumstances with you and explain what needs to happen before a safe collection can proceed.

Use the packaging instructions provided when your return is accepted. If you no longer have the original packaging, tell us so that we can advise you. Do not assume that missing packaging prevents a return, particularly where you are exercising your legal rights because the item is faulty or not as described.

Keep the route to the collection point clear and tell us about any obstacles that cannot be removed safely. Please keep children and pets away from the collection activity. Do not move the item into a shared space or outside unless we have agreed that this is appropriate for your collection.

The driver may decline to collect if the item is unsafe to handle or the access arrangements differ from those agreed. If this happens, contact us so that we can review the problem and discuss how to proceed. The driver cannot decide whether you are entitled to a refund.

If the driver cannot gain access or nobody is available to hand over the return, we may need to arrange a replacement booking. Please contact us if your collection does not take place as expected. We will check what happened and explain the available arrangements without treating the failed collection as a completed return.

Ask for collection confirmation and keep it with your return correspondence. If you believe the wrong item has been taken, or something you intended to keep has been collected, contact us with your booking details. We will investigate and explain what we can do to help resolve the issue.

Collection does not itself confirm that a refund has been approved. We will assess the return under the conditions that apply to your request and tell you the outcome. If we need information from you, we will explain what is required and why it is relevant to the decision.

We will explain any applicable collection charges before you agree to the booking. Nothing in these collection arrangements limits your statutory rights. If you need an adjustment because of a disability or access need, please tell us when you contact us so that we can discuss suitable arrangements with you.

cell.item: POL-RET/Wales and West/Collections in this region

result.text:
We arrange collections for eligible returns from addresses in Wales and West through our customer support team. Contact us to request a return and explain why you would like to send your item back. We will check the return details and explain what happens next.

Collections in Wales and West are made within 47 working days of a return being booked. We will confirm when your booking has been accepted. Sending a return request does not itself confirm that a collection has been booked.

Collection drivers in Wales and West give an arrival window of 108 minutes. Please make sure we have your current contact details so that collection information can reach you. Tell us if you need us to use a particular contact method.

When arranging your collection, we will ask for the collection address, your order details and a description of the item being returned. Please check the booking confirmation carefully and contact us if anything is incorrect or missing.

Tell us about access arrangements that could affect the collection. This includes steps, restricted parking, shared entrances, locked gates and access through communal areas. If permission is needed to enter the property or use a loading area, please arrange this with the person responsible.

Please also tell us about accessibility needs or circumstances that may make the usual collection arrangements difficult. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you and confirm what the collection team can provide. Do not assume that a request has been agreed unless we have confirmed it.

The item must be safe to handle and ready for the agreed collection. Remove your personal belongings and follow the relevant safety instructions when preparing it. If you are unsure how to make it safe, contact us rather than attempting work that could cause injury or damage.

Do not disconnect anything that requires a suitably qualified professional. Our collection drivers do not carry out specialist disconnection work unless this has been expressly arranged and confirmed. Let us know if preparation depends on help from a professional so that we can discuss the booking.

Keep packaging that may help protect the item during collection. If the original packaging is unavailable, tell us when you book. We will explain suitable preparation based on the item and the reason for return. Missing packaging does not remove your statutory rights.

Please keep the route to the item clear and make sure pets are safely away from the collection area. Avoid moving the item yourself if doing so could be unsafe. Tell us about obstacles or handling concerns so that we can agree an appropriate collection plan.

A responsible adult authorised by you must be available to give the driver access and hand over the item. If you need a different arrangement, discuss this with us when booking. Drivers cannot enter an unattended property or collect from an unsecured location without an agreed arrangement.

If your circumstances change, contact customer support so we can update the booking. Please do not rely on a message to the driver to change the collection address or arrangements. Changes need to be checked and confirmed by our team.

If the driver cannot safely reach or handle the item, the collection may not go ahead. We will review the reason with you and explain the available options. If a collection is missed or cancelled, contact us so that we can help resolve the problem.

The driver will record the handover as part of the collection process. Keep the collection confirmation with your return correspondence. If you believe the record is incorrect, or you do not receive confirmation, let customer support know so we can investigate.

Collection does not itself confirm the outcome of a return assessment. Where an assessment is needed, we will check the returned item against the reason given and explain our decision. We may contact you if we need further information to resolve the return.

If a refund is due, we will confirm how it will be processed. Refunds are normally made through the original payment method. If this is not possible, we will discuss a suitable alternative with you without asking you to send sensitive payment details through an unsecured message.

These collection arrangements do not limit your statutory rights. If your item is faulty, damaged or not as described, tell us so that we can handle your return under the appropriate process. Customer support can explain your options if you are unsure which return route applies.

cell.item: POL-RET/London and South East/Collections in this region

result.text:
If you need to return an item from an address in London or South East, contact Halvard Home customer support to arrange a collection. We will check that your address is covered by this regional service and explain what happens next.

Please have your order details ready and tell us why you want to return the item. If it is damaged, faulty or different from what you ordered, describe the problem so that we can arrange suitable handling and explain your options.

We will confirm whether your return has been accepted and whether any collection charge applies. Where a charge applies, we will explain it before you agree to the booking. Nothing in this collection process limits your statutory rights.

Collections in London and South East are made within 12 working days of a return being booked. Your return is booked when we confirm that the collection arrangements have been accepted, rather than when you send your request.

We will use the contact details you provide to send collection information. Please check that these details are correct and tell us about any changes. Let us know if you need us to contact you through an accessible alternative.

Collection drivers in London and South East give an arrival window of 201 minutes. Please make sure someone authorised to hand over the return is available at the collection address during that window.

Tell us about anything that could affect access, such as stairs, a shared entrance, parking restrictions or a locked gate. If permission is needed to enter the building or use a loading area, please arrange this with the person responsible.

If you need help because of a disability or another access requirement, let customer support know when arranging the return. We will discuss reasonable adjustments and confirm what support can be provided, rather than leaving you to make assumptions about the service.

Before collection, remove your personal belongings and prepare the item according to the return instructions we provide. Do not attempt anything that feels unsafe. If preparation requires specialist help, contact us so that we can explain the appropriate arrangements.

Use the original packaging if it is available and suitable. If it is not, tell us before collection so that we can advise you. Missing packaging does not, by itself, remove your statutory rights where an item is faulty or not as described.

Include any accessories or other parts that we have asked you to return. If something is missing or cannot safely be removed, let us know. Please do not include unrelated belongings, as these may be difficult to identify and return to you.

Keep the route to the item clear and make sure pets are safely away from the collection area. You do not need to move anything that you cannot handle safely. Tell us if its location may prevent the driver from collecting it.

The driver will collect the return covered by the booking. Please contact customer support if you want to add anything else or change what is being returned. The driver cannot agree changes to your return eligibility or refund.

If your plans change, contact us before the collection takes place. We will explain how to rearrange or cancel the booking and whether this affects any agreed charge. Please do not leave the return outside or unattended unless we have expressly agreed this with you.

If the driver cannot gain access or the item is not ready, the collection may need to be rearranged. We will explain the reason and discuss the available options. Any proposed charge will be explained before you agree to a replacement booking.

If a collection does not go ahead as arranged, contact customer support. We will check what happened and help you arrange the next step. Tell us if the missed collection has created an access or safety concern.

Ask for confirmation that the item has been handed over and keep it with your return correspondence. Collection confirms receipt by the carrier; it does not itself confirm the outcome of an inspection or the approval of a refund.

We will assess the return in line with the applicable returns terms and your statutory rights. Where a refund is due, we will explain how it will be made and whether delivery or collection charges affect it. Contact us if you disagree with the outcome or need an explanation.

Collections in Northern Ireland are made within 48 working days of a return being booked. When you contact us to arrange a return, we will explain the collection process and confirm whether collection is available for your address. Please wait for confirmation before making arrangements around the visit.

To request a collection, contact Halvard Home customer care through the contact details on our website or in your order confirmation. Have your order details available and tell us why you are returning the item. This helps us identify the appropriate return process.

Please give us the collection address and contact details that the collection team can use to reach you. If the collection address differs from the delivery address, let us know when booking. We will check whether the requested address can be used and explain any restrictions.

Tell us about access arrangements that could affect the collection. These may include stairs, a shared entrance, restricted parking or a locked gate. Please also mention anything that could make moving the item unsafe, so that we can discuss suitable arrangements with you.

If you need support because of a disability or an access requirement, please tell customer care when arranging the return. We will discuss reasonable adjustments with you and explain what can be arranged. You do not need to share medical details to describe the support you need.

Collection drivers in Northern Ireland give an arrival window of 204 minutes. The collection team will use the contact details provided with your booking to share the arrival information. Please check that these details are correct and let us know if they change.

Someone authorised to hand over the return must be available at the collection address. They should know which item is being collected and have access to the booking details. Please do not leave the return outside or in a communal area unless we have expressly agreed this arrangement.

Before collection, follow the preparation instructions provided with your return confirmation. These instructions will explain how to make the item ready for safe handling. If anything is unclear, contact us rather than attempting work that you are not confident you can carry out safely.

Please remove personal belongings and check whether accessories or documents need to be returned with the item. Where the item contains personal information, follow the relevant instructions for removing it. Contact customer care if you need guidance or cannot safely access the item to do this.

If you still have the packaging, tell us when you book. We will explain whether it should be used and discuss alternatives if it is unavailable or unsuitable. Do not assume that missing packaging prevents a return, particularly where you are exercising your legal rights.

Please keep the item protected from damage while it remains in your care. Do not continue using it if you believe it is unsafe. If its condition changes after the return is booked, tell customer care so that we can review the collection arrangements.

The driver may check that the item matches the collection booking and can be moved safely. If the return is not ready, the address cannot be accessed or the conditions are unsafe, collection may not go ahead. We will explain the next steps if this happens.

If you need to change or cancel a collection, contact customer care as soon as you know. We will check the status of the booking and tell you what can be changed. Please do not arrange a separate collection yourself unless we have agreed this with you.

If the driver does not arrive as advised, contact us so that we can investigate. We will check with the collection team and explain how the return will proceed. Please keep the booking confirmation and relevant messages available to help us trace the arrangements.

We will tell you before confirming the booking whether a collection charge applies and explain the basis for it. Charges depend on the reason for the return and your legal rights. We will not treat a return for a faulty item as a change of mind.

Keep the collection acknowledgement provided when the item is handed over. This helps if there is a query about the return. We will explain how your refund is being handled and contact you if information is needed. Collection arrangements do not limit your statutory rights, including your rights where goods are faulty or not as described.

Collections in Island Areas are made within 42 working days of a return being booked. Our customer support team will help you arrange collection and explain what you need to do before the driver arrives. Please tell us about any access restrictions when you book, so that we can plan a suitable collection.

To arrange your return, contact Halvard Home using the contact details provided with your order or on our website. Have your order details available and explain why you wish to return the item. We will check the details with you and confirm the collection address and your preferred contact details.

Island collection routes depend on local transport links and access arrangements. Please let us know if reaching your address involves a ferry crossing, a private road, a harbour access requirement or permission from a landowner. Our collection team needs this information to assess the route and make the necessary arrangements.

Tell us if your address is difficult to find or if online maps direct visitors to the wrong place. Clear directions and a description of the entrance can help the driver locate you. Please do not send sensitive information, such as security credentials, unless our team has explained how to share it safely.

Collection drivers in Island Areas give an arrival window of 102 minutes. The driver or collection team will contact you using the details attached to your booking. Please check that these details are correct and tell us if they change. An arrival window helps you prepare, but it is not a guaranteed appointment.

You will need to arrange for someone to be at the address to hand over the item. That person should know what is being collected and be able to show the driver where it is. If you cannot attend and nobody can act on your behalf, contact us to discuss your booking.

Please prepare the item in line with the return instructions we send you. Remove personal belongings and make sure it is clean enough to handle safely. Where relevant, remove stored personal information and disconnect linked accounts. If you are unsure how to do this, ask our customer support team for guidance.

Keep packaging where it is available, but do not assume that missing packaging prevents a return. Contact us if you no longer have it or if it is damaged. We will explain how the item should be protected for collection, taking account of its condition and the reason for your return.

Disconnection must be carried out safely and in accordance with the instructions supplied with the item. Collection drivers cannot carry out work that requires a qualified professional. If safe disconnection needs specialist help, please arrange this before collection or contact us to discuss what is required. Do not attempt work you are not qualified to do.

Please keep the route to the item clear and tell us about steps, narrow entrances, shared access or other obstacles. Do not move a heavy or awkward item yourself if doing so could cause injury or damage. Explain any handling concerns when booking so that we can assess the collection requirements.

Keep children and pets away from the collection route while the driver is handling the item. The driver may stop the collection if conditions are unsafe or if the information supplied does not match the access available. If this happens, contact our customer support team so we can discuss a safe way forward.

If your plans change, let us know through our customer support channels. Please do not rely on a message left for the driver to change or cancel your booking. We will confirm any agreed changes and explain whether the existing collection arrangements can still be used.

Weather or transport disruption may affect an island collection route. If your collection is affected, we will contact you, explain the situation and discuss the arrangements with you. If the driver does not arrive within the arrival window and you have not received an update, please contact our customer support team.

When the item is handed over, keep the collection confirmation provided by the driver or sent by our team. Collection does not itself confirm that a refund has been approved. We will assess the return under the applicable policy and explain the outcome. Nothing in these collection arrangements limits your statutory rights.

If you believe a Halvard Home appliance may be unsafe, please tell us. You can report a concern even if nobody has been hurt or you are unsure what caused the problem. We welcome reports from customers, people using our appliances, repairers and anyone who has noticed a possible safety risk.

Stop using the appliance if you suspect it could cause harm. If it is safe to do so, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply. Do not touch damaged wiring, exposed electrical parts or an appliance that appears dangerous. Keep other people and pets away from the affected area.

If there is smoke, fire, a suspected gas leak or an immediate threat to someone’s safety, move to a safe place and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to inspect the appliance, collect evidence or prevent damage. Reporting the concern to us must not delay getting emergency help.

You can report a safety concern through the contact options on our website. Tell our customer support team that your message concerns safety so it can be directed appropriately. If you need help communicating with us, please explain your needs and we will work with you to find an accessible way to report.

Describe what happened in your own words. Explain what you noticed, what the appliance was doing and whether anyone was injured or property was damaged. Tell us about unusual smells, sounds, heat, smoke or visible damage where relevant. Please distinguish between what you observed and what you think may have caused it.

Include any identifying details you can safely find on the appliance or its paperwork, together with your contact details. Information about where you obtained it and any previous repairs may help our investigation. You do not need proof of purchase to raise a safety concern, and missing information should not prevent you from contacting us.

Photographs, recordings or documents can help us understand a report, but only provide them if you can obtain them safely. Do not recreate the fault, open the casing or reconnect the appliance for our benefit. Avoid sending images that reveal unrelated personal information or show someone who has not agreed to be photographed.

Safety reports are answered within 27 hours. Our response will confirm that we have received your concern and explain the next steps available. An answer does not necessarily mean that the investigation is complete. We may need further information or specialist assessment before we can explain the cause or confirm an appropriate remedy.

We assess reports according to the possible risk of harm and the evidence available. We may ask questions about how the appliance was installed, used or maintained. These questions help us understand what happened; they do not mean that we have decided you are responsible or that your concern is being dismissed.

Please keep the appliance and relevant packaging or paperwork where you can do so safely. Do not post, transport, sell, give away or dispose of an appliance that may be unsafe without appropriate guidance. If keeping it creates a risk, tell us so we can discuss safe handling arrangements with you.

Where an inspection or collection is needed, we will explain the arrangements and any precautions you should take. We will not ask you to carry out work that requires specialist skills. Do not attempt a repair unless we have confirmed that the proposed action is safe and suitable for you to undertake.

If our assessment identifies a safety issue, we will explain the action required. This may involve advice to stop using the appliance, an inspection, a repair, a replacement or a refund, depending on the circumstances and your legal rights. We will make clear whether an action is precautionary or follows a confirmed finding.

Customers are told of a recall within 25 days of it being issued. Recall notices explain the affected appliances, the risk involved and what customers should do. We use appropriate contact channels and public notices to reach affected customers. Please follow the safety instructions in a recall notice even if your appliance appears to work normally.

We handle personal information in line with our privacy policy. Relevant information may be shared with repair partners, safety specialists or public authorities where needed to investigate a concern or meet legal duties. Raising a safety concern does not affect your statutory rights. If you remain concerned about our response, ask for your report to be reviewed.

If we identify a safety risk that requires an appliance to be recalled, we will explain the risk and the action you need to take. Our priority is to help you stop using the affected appliance safely and arrange a suitable remedy.

We may contact you using the details held with your order, account or product registration. We may also publish recall notices through our website, retailers and other appropriate channels. Please keep your contact details up to date so that important safety information can reach you.

A recall notice will explain how to check whether your appliance is affected. Follow the instructions carefully and contact us if you cannot find the identifying details or are unsure what they mean. Do not assume that an appliance is safe because it appears to work normally.

If your appliance is covered by a recall, stop using it and follow the safety advice in the notice. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if this can be done safely. Do not attempt to dismantle, repair or test it yourself.

Keep the affected appliance away from anyone who might use it without knowing about the recall. Do not sell, donate or pass it on. If you have already given it to someone else, share the recall notice with them and tell us so that we can help.

To respond to a recall, use the contact method shown in the recall notice. We will ask for the information needed to identify the appliance, contact you and arrange the remedy. Tell us if you need help providing this information or understanding the instructions.

You can contact us about a recall even if you have lost your receipt, did not register the appliance or received it as a gift. We will explain what other information may help us confirm that the appliance is affected and establish the appropriate remedy.

The remedy will be explained in the recall notice. Depending on the safety issue, this may involve collection and a refund, replacement or an authorised repair. We will not ask you to carry out work that should be handled by a trained professional.

Where collection is required, we will agree the arrangements with you and explain how to prepare the appliance safely. A recalled appliance is collected within 18 working days of the customer replying. Please tell us about access difficulties or support needs when you respond.

Do not move or disconnect an appliance if doing so could put you or someone else at risk. Tell us if it is fitted in place, difficult to reach or unsafe to handle. We will arrange appropriate assistance rather than ask you to take that risk.

Please make the appliance available as agreed and tell us if your circumstances change. If collection cannot go ahead, we will contact you to arrange an alternative and explain what happens next. You should continue to follow the recall safety advice.

Refunds for recalled appliances are paid within 31 days. We will explain how your refund will be paid and what information we need to process it. If the original payment method is unavailable, we will discuss a suitable alternative with you.

We will explain whether accessories or other items supplied with the appliance need to be returned. Do not dispose of the appliance or arrange your own return unless we ask you to do so. This helps us manage the safety risk and handle recalled appliances responsibly.

If you bought the appliance through a retailer, the recall notice will say whether you should contact us or the retailer. We will work with those involved to make the process clear. You should not have to work out who is responsible without guidance.

We use the personal information you provide to manage the recall, arrange the remedy and meet our legal duties. We may share relevant details with organisations helping us carry out these tasks, such as collection providers, in line with our privacy policy.

If you are concerned that a recall message may not be genuine, contact us through our official website or your usual customer service channel. Avoid using links or sharing payment details in response to a message you do not trust.

Please tell us if you are unhappy with how your recall has been handled or if the proposed arrangements do not meet your needs. We will explain how to raise a complaint and seek a resolution. These recall terms do not affect your legal rights.

Electrical safety depends on the condition of your appliance, the suitability of your electrical supply and the way the appliance is used. Read the safety instructions supplied with your appliance and keep them available for reference. Follow any warning labels, and do not use an appliance for a purpose it was not designed to serve.

Check the appliance, plug and power lead for visible damage before use. Look for cracked casing, loose parts, exposed wiring, scorch marks or damage around the plug. Do not connect an appliance if you suspect it is unsafe. Damage may be present even when the appliance appears to work normally.

Use a socket that is suitable for the appliance and properly installed. The plug should fit securely without being forced. If a socket is loose, cracked, discoloured or unusually warm, stop using it and ask a qualified electrician to inspect it. Do not attempt to repair fixed electrical wiring yourself.

Connect appliances directly to a suitable wall socket wherever possible. Never run an appliance from an extension lead longer than 9 metres. This limit does not mean that an extension lead is suitable for your appliance. Follow the appliance instructions, including any restriction on extension leads, adaptors or shared sockets.

Do not overload sockets or connect adaptors together. Keep plugs and connections accessible so that the supply can be isolated safely. Do not place power leads where they may be trapped, stretched, walked on or damaged by furniture. Keep them away from hot surfaces, sharp edges and moving parts.

Your home's protective electrical devices must be suitable and working correctly. Test the home's residual current device every 7 months. Follow the device maker's testing instructions and any advice requiring more frequent testing from a qualified electrician. If the device fails its test, seek professional advice and do not assume that the circuit is protected.

A protective device is not a substitute for safe use or proper maintenance. If the supply trips when an appliance is connected or running, stop using the appliance. Do not repeatedly reset the protection to keep it operating. Ask a qualified electrician or an authorised repair provider to investigate the cause.

Keep your hands dry when handling plugs, switches and electrical connections. Protect appliances from water unless their instructions expressly permit the intended use. If liquid enters an appliance or reaches its electrical connections, stop using it. Isolate the supply only if you can do so without touching wet equipment or entering water.

Switch off and unplug an appliance before cleaning or carrying out maintenance permitted in its instructions. Pull the plug rather than the lead. For an appliance connected directly to the fixed wiring, follow its isolation instructions. If you are unsure how to make it safe, seek advice from a qualified professional.

Do not open electrical housings, bypass safety features or make unauthorised alterations. Internal components may remain dangerous after the appliance has been disconnected. Repairs involving electrical parts must be carried out by a suitably qualified person. Replacement plugs, leads and components must meet the appliance's safety requirements.

Stop using an appliance if it gives off a burning smell, sparks, produces smoke or behaves unexpectedly. Disconnect it only when safe. If there is a fire or an immediate threat to personal safety, move away, alert others and contact the emergency services. Never use water on an electrical fire.

Keep children and anyone who may not recognise electrical hazards away from damaged appliances, loose leads and accessible connections. Provide supervision where the appliance instructions require it. Do not allow packaging, coverings or stored items to obstruct ventilation or interfere with safe access to the plug or isolation switch.

Contact Halvard Home if you believe an appliance has an electrical fault or may be affected by a safety notice. Describe the problem and provide the identifying details requested by our support team. Do not reconnect the appliance simply to demonstrate the fault or obtain information that is not safely accessible.

If we issue a safety notice or recall, follow its instructions and stop using the affected appliance when directed. Do not sell, lend or donate an appliance that has been identified as unsafe. Keep it disconnected and stored safely while awaiting advice about repair, collection or disposal. Nothing in this policy limits your statutory rights.

Use the Brio kettle only to heat drinking water in a home setting. It is not intended for cooking food, warming other liquids or use outdoors. Follow the instructions supplied with your kettle and keep them available for anyone who may use it.

Place the kettle on a dry, level, stable surface that can withstand heat. Keep it away from the edge of the worktop, hot cooking surfaces and places where it could be knocked over. Do not place it on a tray that could collect spilled water around electrical connections.

Leave at least 24 centimetres of space around the Brio kettle. Keep curtains, packaging and other combustible materials away from it. Position it so that steam can escape freely without reaching cupboards, shelves, sockets or items that could be damaged by heat or moisture.

Check the kettle, base, plug and lead for damage before use. Do not use the kettle if the casing is cracked, the lead is frayed or the plug appears loose or scorched. A kettle that has been dropped or is leaking should be taken out of use and checked.

Make sure your electricity supply matches the information on the kettle’s rating label. Use the base supplied with the kettle and connect it to a suitable wall socket. Keep the plug and socket accessible. Do not use an adaptor or extension lead that could become overloaded.

Keep the lead away from heat, sharp edges and wet surfaces. Arrange it so that it cannot hang over the worktop or be pulled by a child. Do not carry the kettle by its lead or pull the lead to remove the plug from the socket.

Remove the kettle from its base before filling it. Follow the fill markings inside the kettle, and do not operate it without water. Keep the outside of the kettle and the underside dry. If water reaches the base or electrical connections, disconnect the supply safely and stop using it.

Close the lid securely before switching the kettle on. Do not open the lid during heating or while steam is escaping. Keep your face and hands away from the spout and lid opening. Steam and hot water can cause serious burns, even when the kettle appears quiet.

Stay nearby while the kettle is heating. Do not rely on its automatic shut-off as a reason to leave it unattended. If it fails to switch off, disconnect it safely and stop using it. Do not repeatedly restart it to test whether a suspected fault has cleared.

Lift the kettle by its handle and pour carefully, keeping the spout directed away from people. Avoid sudden movements and do not tilt it sharply. Take care when putting it back on its base. The body, lid and surrounding surfaces may be hot.

Keep children away from the kettle, its lead and escaping steam. Do not allow them to play with it or use it without appropriate supervision. Anyone who needs support to use the kettle safely should have help from someone who understands the risks.

Switch the kettle off and unplug it before cleaning. Let the Brio kettle cool for 36 minutes before cleaning it. Treat surfaces with care if they still feel hot. Do not put the kettle, base, plug or lead into water, and do not rinse electrical parts under a tap.

Wipe the exterior with a soft, damp cloth and dry it carefully. Avoid abrasive pads, harsh chemicals and tools that could scratch the surface or damage seals. Follow the supplied instructions for descaling, and keep cleaning products away from children and food preparation areas.

Clean the air vents of the Brio kettle every 71 days. Keep the kettle unplugged during this task. Gently remove dust from accessible vent surfaces with a soft, dry brush. Do not push objects through the vents or allow moisture to enter them. Never cover the vents during use.

Stop using the kettle if you notice smoke, sparks, a burning smell or unusual behaviour. Disconnect it if this can be done safely. Do not attempt to open the casing or repair electrical parts yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice about inspection, repair or disposal.

If Halvard Home issues a safety notice or recall affecting your Brio kettle, follow the notice and stop using it when instructed. Do not pass an affected kettle to someone else. Keep its identification details available so that customer support can help you check whether it is covered.

Choose a stable, level worktop for the Brio kettle, where it cannot rock, slide or be knocked over. The surface must be dry and suitable for heat and splashes. Do not place the kettle on a cloth, tray with an uneven base, or unstable furniture.

Keep the kettle away from the edge of the worktop and out of the reach of children. Consider how people move through the room, especially where someone might catch the handle or pull the lead. Do not position it where a door could strike it.

The power lead of the Brio kettle is deliberately short. It must be installed within 156 centimetres of its socket. Choose a position that lets the lead rest without tension. Do not stretch the lead across a walkway or leave it hanging over an edge.

Use a wall socket that is suitable for the kettle and accessible without reaching over it. Check that the electrical supply matches the information on the rating label. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to make an unsuitable position work. Ask a qualified electrician if you are unsure.

Install it at least 68 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep the kettle and its lead away from hot cooking surfaces, heaters and places where heat could damage them. Do not route the lead behind cooking equipment or trap it against a hot surface.

Choose a position where steam can escape without reaching electrical fittings, cupboards or items that could be damaged by moisture. Leave the spout clear and keep the kettle away from curtains. Do not place it beneath shelving that obstructs access or forces you to reach through escaping steam.

Keep the base, plug and socket away from sinks and other places where water may collect or splash. Do not install the kettle outdoors or where it could be exposed to rain. Never immerse the base, power lead or plug in water when cleaning the installation area.
