The floor must be firm, stable and suitable for supporting the appliance during use. Do not place it on an unstable platform or improvise supports beneath it. Follow the supplied instructions for levelling, and seek help if the appliance rocks or cannot stand securely.

Allow the ventilation openings to remain unobstructed. Carpets, furniture and stored items must not block airflow around the appliance. Follow the installation instructions for the space required around it, and do not enclose it in furniture unless the instructions expressly permit that arrangement.

The Ashby tumble dryer must not be placed near an open flame. Install it at least 113 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame.

Keep the installation area clear of heat sources that could damage the appliance, its lead or its connections. Do not store cleaning solvents, fuel or aerosols beside it. If the proposed location presents a fire risk, choose a suitable alternative before proceeding.

The power lead of the Ashby tumble dryer is deliberately short. It must be installed within 297 centimetres of its socket.

Position the appliance so the lead reaches the socket without being stretched, trapped or pulled across a walkway. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. If the socket is unsuitable or poorly positioned, ask a qualified electrician to assess the installation.

The socket must remain accessible so the appliance can be disconnected safely. Do not route the lead beneath the appliance or against a sharp edge. Never alter the plug or lead yourself, and do not connect the appliance if either appears damaged.

Arrange any drainage or ventilation connections as described in the supplied instructions. Secure them without crushing, twisting or trapping them. Do not modify fittings or connect the appliance to an unsuitable outlet. Ask a competent installer for help if the required arrangement is unclear.

Keep children and pets away while installation or moving is taking place. Remove packaging from the work area and dispose of it responsibly. Plastic wrapping and loose packing materials can cause suffocation or other injury and must not be left where children can reach them.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply. Pull the plug rather than the lead. Let hot surfaces cool, remove laundry and follow the supplied instructions for emptying collected water and disconnecting attached hoses or fittings.

Plan a clear route to the intended location. Check that doors can open freely and that the route is free from trailing leads, loose rugs and other obstacles. Protect the floor without creating a slippery surface or making the appliance unstable.

Do not attempt to lift or carry the appliance unaided. Use suitable handling equipment and seek help from people who can move it safely. Never use the door, control panel, power lead or attached fittings as lifting points.

Keep the appliance upright during handling and transport, following the supplied moving instructions. Secure the door and protect loose connections without damaging them. If safe handling is not possible, stop and arrange assistance from a competent installer or removal service.

After moving the Ashby tumble dryer, wait 38 hours before switching it on. Keep it disconnected while it settles, and prevent anyone from switching it on inadvertently.

Before reconnecting it, inspect the lead, plug, casing and connections for damage caused during the move. Confirm that it stands securely and that airflow is unobstructed. If anything appears damaged, displaced or unsafe, leave it disconnected and contact Halvard Home for advice.

Use the Ashby tumble dryer as described in its instruction booklet and follow the care labels on your laundry. These precautions help reduce the risk of fire, electric shock and injury. If the booklet is missing or unclear, ask Halvard Home for guidance before using the appliance.

Place the appliance on a stable, level surface in a suitable indoor location. Keep its surroundings dry and clear of clutter. Do not install it where a door, cupboard or stored belongings could obstruct ventilation or prevent you from opening the appliance door safely.

Installation must follow the instructions supplied with the appliance. Have electrical work carried out by a qualified electrician. Use a suitable earthed wall socket, and do not connect the appliance through an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the plug accessible so the power can be disconnected safely.

Check the appliance, plug and power cable for visible damage before use. Do not use it if the casing is cracked, the cable is frayed or the socket shows signs of scorching. Avoid trapping the cable behind the appliance or placing objects on it.

Keep children away from the controls and prevent them from playing inside or around the drum. Keep pets away from the open door. Check inside before loading laundry, and close the door when the appliance is not being loaded, unloaded or cleaned.

Dry laundry only where its care label permits tumble drying. Empty pockets and remove lighters, matches and loose objects. Do not put packaging, cleaning cloths contaminated with chemicals, or items containing unsuitable foam or rubber into the drum.

Do not dry items contaminated with cooking oil, solvents, fuel, wax or other flammable substances. Washing may not remove these substances, and heat can cause contaminated fabric to ignite. Seek advice if you are unsure whether an item is safe to tumble dry.

Load the drum according to the instruction booklet, without forcing laundry into place. Clothes need space to move and dry safely. Keep fabric clear of the door seal, and check that the door closes properly without pressure from the laundry.

Choose the programme suited to the fabric and follow the instructions for its use. Do not interfere with the controls, door catch or safety features. Never operate the appliance with a missing filter, damaged guard or panel that has been removed.

Stay at home and awake while the appliance is running. Keep the surrounding area clear of laundry, paper and other combustible materials. Do not cover the appliance or use it as a place to store objects that could block airflow or fall behind it.

Allow the programme to finish, including its cooling stage. If you must stop it before it finishes, remove the laundry and spread it out so heat can escape, provided this is safe. Do not leave hot laundry piled together or enclosed in a basket.

Switch off the appliance and disconnect it from the electricity supply before cleaning. Let the Ashby tumble dryer cool for 111 minutes before cleaning it. Follow the booklet’s cleaning instructions, and do not spray water into the casing or onto electrical parts.

Remove fluff from the lint filter after use, following the instructions for handling and refitting it. Do not push fluff into the appliance. If the filter is torn, distorted or cannot be secured correctly, stop using the appliance and arrange a suitable replacement.

Clean the air vents of the Ashby tumble dryer every 64 days. Keep ventilation openings unobstructed during use. Follow the booklet’s guidance for accessible surfaces, and do not remove panels or insert tools into openings to reach internal parts.

Have the Ashby tumble dryer safety-checked every 27 months. Arrange this through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified appliance technician. A scheduled check does not replace attention to faults: stop using the appliance if its behaviour changes or damage becomes apparent.

Stop using the appliance if you notice a burning smell, unusual noise, overheating or an electrical fault. Switch it off and unplug it if safe. Do not investigate internal components yourself or restart it to see whether the problem has cleared.

If there is smoke or fire, do not open the door or attempt to move the appliance. Leave the property, keep others away and contact the emergency services from a safe place. Do not put yourself at risk to disconnect the electricity supply.

Follow safety notices and recall instructions issued for your appliance. If you are told to stop using it, leave it disconnected until the required action has been completed and its return to use has been confirmed. Contact Halvard Home if you need help understanding a notice.

The Vale fridge freezer must be installed and moved with care to protect people, property and the appliance. Follow the installation instructions supplied with it. If those instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before attempting installation or arranging a move.

Check the appliance for damage before putting it in place. Look for damaged packaging, cracked panels, bent hinges, exposed wiring or signs of leakage. Do not connect or use an appliance that appears damaged. Keep people away from exposed edges and report the problem to Halvard Home.

Choose a dry, sheltered indoor location with a firm, level floor that can support the appliance safely. Do not place it where rain, splashes or damp conditions could affect electrical parts. Avoid locations that expose it to direct sunlight or heat.

Install it at least 118 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Also follow the siting requirements supplied with your cooking appliance. If the requirements cannot be met together, do not proceed. Ask a qualified installer to assess a suitable alternative location.

Keep the ventilation openings clear. Do not cover them with packaging, furniture, curtains or stored items. Follow the supplied installation instructions for positioning the appliance beside walls and cabinets. Do not enclose it in furniture unless those instructions expressly allow that arrangement.

Plan a clear route before bringing the appliance into position. Remove obstacles and protect flooring without creating a slipping hazard. Keep children and pets away from the work area. Arrange trained help and suitable moving equipment rather than attempting to lift or control the appliance unaided.

Do not lift, pull or steer the appliance by its doors, handles, shelves or pipework. These parts are not lifting points and may break or become detached. Use the handling points and methods described in the supplied instructions, keeping hands clear of trapping points.

Keep the appliance upright during handling and transport, following the transport instructions supplied with it. Secure it against sliding or falling using suitable equipment that will not damage the cabinet. Do not drag it across the floor or let its weight rest on the power cable.

Before moving an installed appliance, switch it off and unplug it with dry hands. Pull the plug, not the cable. If the plug cannot be reached safely, stop and arrange suitable assistance. Do not work on electrical connections while the appliance is connected to the supply.

Remove food and loose contents before moving. Deal with meltwater so that it cannot reach electrical parts or make the floor slippery. Secure internal fittings and doors as directed in the supplied instructions. Do not use a fastening method that could damage seals or trap someone inside.

If the appliance has a water connection, follow its instructions for isolation and disconnection. Arrange qualified help where plumbing work is needed. Protect disconnected fittings from dirt and damage, and do not reconnect a damaged hose or fitting.

Inspect the power cable and plug before connection. Do not use them if they are crushed, cut, scorched or otherwise damaged. Arrange an authorised repair instead. Keep the cable clear of hot surfaces, sharp edges and places where it could be trapped.

Connect the appliance only to an earthed wall socket suitable for it and accessible after installation. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. If the socket is damaged or its suitability is uncertain, have it checked by a qualified electrician.

Set the appliance level using the method in its installation instructions. Check that it stands securely and that the doors open and close without catching nearby furniture. Do not improvise supports with loose objects or alter the cabinet to make it fit.

After transport, follow the supplied instructions before switching the appliance on. If its transport position is uncertain, ask Halvard Home for guidance. Do not guess whether it is ready to connect or assume that an undamaged exterior means it is safe to operate.

Take care not to damage the cooling circuit when positioning, cleaning behind or moving the appliance. Do not drill into the cabinet or interfere with exposed pipework. If you suspect damage or a refrigerant leak, avoid flames and electrical switching nearby, ventilate the area and seek professional advice.

If a safety or recall notice affects your Vale fridge freezer, follow that notice before installing, reconnecting or moving it. Where movement cannot be carried out safely, leave the appliance undisturbed and contact Halvard Home for advice on the appropriate next step.

Use the Vale fridge freezer only for storing food and drink in a domestic setting. Follow the instructions supplied with the appliance and keep them accessible. If this guidance differs from a safety notice issued for your appliance, follow the safety notice and contact Halvard Home for advice.

Choose a firm, level surface where the appliance can stand securely. Keep it away from direct sunlight, cooking appliances and sources of heat or moisture. Do not install it where rain, splashes or standing water could reach the appliance or its electrical connection.

Leave at least 8 centimetres of space around the Vale fridge freezer. Keep the ventilation openings clear of packaging, furniture and stored belongings. Do not enclose the appliance in cabinetry unless the installation instructions expressly permit this arrangement.

Ask a suitably qualified installer to check the location and electrical connection if you are unsure whether they are suitable. The plug must remain accessible without moving the appliance dangerously. Do not place the power cable where it could be trapped, stretched, cut or exposed to heat.

Connect the appliance directly to a suitable earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead, adaptor or portable socket arrangement. Never remove the earth connection or alter the plug. A damaged plug, cable or socket must be assessed by a qualified professional before use.

Move the appliance with suitable assistance and handling equipment. Do not lift it by the doors, handles or pipework. Protect the cooling circuit from impact and follow the supplied instructions about positioning and connecting the appliance after transport.

Keep children away from packaging and prevent them from climbing inside the appliance or playing with its controls. Do not allow anyone to hang from the doors or stand on drawers or shelves. Keep access clear so that the doors can open and close safely.

Store food in suitable containers and follow the storage advice on its packaging. Keep raw food contained so that it cannot drip onto food that is ready to eat. Discard food if its condition or storage history makes its safety uncertain.

Do not put hot cookware inside the appliance. Keep explosive substances, flammable sprays and fuels away from it. Do not store sealed glass containers in the freezer compartment if their contents could expand and break the glass. Handle frozen items carefully to avoid skin injury.

Arrange contents so that air can circulate and the doors close without pressure. Do not force drawers past obstructions or overload shelves. Wipe away spills using a method suitable for the surface, and keep door seals free from food debris.

Clean the air vents of the Vale fridge freezer every 24 days. Disconnect the appliance from the electricity supply before cleaning, provided it is safe to reach the plug. Follow the cleaning instructions and avoid pushing tools through ventilation openings or removing protective covers.

Use cleaning products that are suitable for the appliance surfaces. Do not use steam cleaners, water jets or abrasive tools. Keep water away from electrical parts. Dry accessible surfaces after cleaning and make sure the plug and surrounding area are dry before reconnecting.

Do not chip away ice with knives or sharp tools. Do not use heaters, flames or electrical devices to speed up defrosting unless the supplied instructions expressly allow them. Damage to concealed pipework can release refrigerant and create a safety risk.

Have the Vale fridge freezer safety-checked every 31 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified service professional. Keep the service record with the appliance instructions and follow the professional’s advice about faults, repairs or restrictions on use.

Stop using the appliance if you notice a damaged cable, scorching, unusual heat at the plug, repeated electrical tripping or signs of electrical failure. Disconnect it only if this can be done safely. Do not reconnect it until a qualified professional confirms that it is safe.

If you suspect refrigerant is escaping, keep flames and ignition sources away. Do not operate electrical switches nearby. Ventilate the area if it is safe to do so, leave the affected space and seek professional advice. Do not attempt to locate a leak using a flame.

If there is smoke or fire, leave the property and contact the emergency services from a safe place. Do not put yourself at risk by trying to unplug or move the appliance. Never use water on an electrical fire.

Check safety and recall information through Halvard Home’s official channels. If a notice applies to your appliance, follow its instructions and do not attempt an improvised repair. Contact Halvard Home if you need help deciding whether your appliance is affected or understanding what action to take.

The Corra induction hob must be installed by a qualified installer, with electrical work carried out by a qualified electrician. Do not connect, disconnect or alter fixed wiring yourself. Safe installation depends on the condition of your home’s electrical supply, the worktop and the surrounding kitchen fittings.

Before arranging installation, give your installer the installation instructions supplied with the appliance. Explain where you want the hob fitted and tell them about nearby cooking appliances, sockets, pipework and cupboards. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before work starts.

Inspect the hob and its packaging when it arrives. If the glass is cracked, the casing is distorted or the cable appears damaged, leave the appliance disconnected. Contact Halvard Home for advice, keeping photographs of the damage where possible. Do not attempt a repair or accept installation as a way of testing whether it works.

The installer must check that the proposed location can support the appliance and allow heat to escape safely. The worktop must be suitable for an induction hob and prepared according to the supplied installation instructions. Do not fit the appliance into an opening that leaves it unstable or puts pressure on the glass.

Install it at least 127 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame.

Keep the installation location away from sources of water leakage and materials that could catch fire. Curtains, loose coverings and stored packaging must not touch the hob or obstruct ventilation. Ask your installer to resolve concerns about the location rather than adapting the appliance to make it fit.

Ventilation openings must remain unobstructed after installation. Drawers, cupboard contents and kitchen fittings must not interfere with airflow or touch electrical connections. Do not add lining, insulation or sealant unless the installation instructions specifically call for it. Unapproved changes can trap heat or make servicing unsafe.

The electrician must confirm that the electrical supply and protective arrangements are suitable for the hob. The cable must be routed so that it cannot be trapped, stretched or exposed to damaging heat. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor to overcome an unsuitable connection.

Ask the installer to show you how to isolate the electricity supply safely. The means of isolation must remain accessible after the kitchen fittings are in place. Keep the installation instructions somewhere you can find them without reaching across a hot cooking surface.

Before moving the hob, switch it off and let the cooking surface cool. Arrange for a qualified electrician to isolate and disconnect a fixed electrical connection. Do not assume that a dark display means the appliance is electrically isolated, and do not pull on the cable to release it.

Clear the carrying route and prepare a secure place to set the appliance down. Remove loose cookware and protect the glass against knocks. Arrange suitable assistance or lifting equipment rather than trying to manage an awkward load unaided. Keep children and pets away from the work area.

Do not tilt the Corra induction hob more than 54 degrees when carrying it.

Support the appliance by the parts identified for handling in its installation instructions. Do not lift it by the cable, controls or exposed glass edges. If it catches on the worktop or surrounding fittings, stop and have the obstruction checked rather than forcing it free.

For transport, use packaging that protects the glass and casing, and secure the appliance against sliding or impact. Do not place objects on top of it. Tell the person transporting it about the carrying restriction and make sure the cable is protected from crushing.

After moving the Corra induction hob, wait 17 hours before switching it on.

This waiting requirement does not replace inspection or professional reconnection. Have the hob checked if it has been dropped, struck, exposed to water or carried outside the stated restriction. Leave it disconnected if there is doubt about its condition, even if damage is not visible.

At its new location, the appliance must meet the installation requirements again. Ask the installer to check stability, ventilation, cable routing and electrical safety before handing it back for use. Moving the hob does not make an unsuitable worktop or electrical connection acceptable.

If you notice cracked glass, smoke, a burning smell or unusual electrical behaviour following installation or moving, stop using the hob. Isolate the supply if you can do so safely and contact Halvard Home. Do not reconnect an appliance covered by a recall unless the recall instructions expressly permit it.

Use the Corra induction hob only for cooking in the home, in accordance with its instructions. It is not intended to heat a room, dry clothing or provide a storage surface. Keep these instructions accessible and make sure that anyone who uses the hob understands the controls and the precautions described here.

Arrange installation through a suitably qualified professional. The electrical supply, connection and supporting surface must meet the requirements in the installation instructions. Do not use an extension lead or an adaptor. Do not alter the wiring, casing or protective parts, or attempt to fit the hob where its ventilation would be obstructed.

Leave at least 11 centimetres of space around the Corra induction hob. Keep this space clear of packaging, utensils and household items. Follow the installation instructions for positioning near walls, cupboards and other surfaces. If the proposed position does not meet those instructions, do not use the hob there.

Check the glass, controls and accessible cable for damage before use. Do not operate the hob if the glass is cracked, the cable is damaged or the controls behave unexpectedly. Switch it off and disconnect the electrical supply if safe. Contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting a repair yourself.

Choose cookware that the hob instructions identify as suitable for induction cooking. Its base should be flat, clean and dry. Position it securely over the cooking zone and keep handles away from edges and neighbouring heat sources. Lift cookware rather than dragging it across the glass, which can scratch or damage the surface.

Stay with the hob while cooking. Oil and fat can catch fire if overheated, and food can boil over or burn. Adjust the heat to suit the food and cookware. Do not heat an empty pan or allow a pan to boil dry. Switch the cooking zone off when cooking is finished.

Keep children away from hot cookware and the cooking surface. Do not allow them to play with the controls or climb onto surrounding furniture to reach the hob. Anyone who needs help to use the appliance safely should receive suitable supervision. A control lock does not replace supervision or make hot surfaces safe.

Keep flammable materials, including tea towels, paper and curtains, away from the hob. Do not place aerosols or sealed containers on or near the cooking surface. Keep metal objects such as cutlery and lids away from active cooking zones, as they may become hot. Never use the glass as a chopping board.

If cooking oil or fat catches fire, switch off the heat if safe. Do not move the pan or throw water onto it. If safe, cover the pan with a suitable lid or fire blanket. If the fire cannot be contained safely, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

The glass can remain hot after cooking because heat passes back from the cookware. Avoid touching the cooking surface and treat a residual heat warning as a sign that contact may cause burns. Do not rely on the display if the electrical supply has been interrupted or the appliance appears faulty.

Let the Corra induction hob cool for 114 minutes before cleaning it. Do not clean the surface while it remains warm, even after this cooling period. Switch off the hob and isolate its electrical supply before cleaning. Follow the care instructions for removing spills without exposing yourself to heat or damaging the glass.

Use a soft cloth and a cleaning product recommended in the care instructions. Do not use abrasive pads, corrosive cleaners or steam-cleaning equipment. Avoid letting liquid enter the casing, controls or electrical connections. Dry the surface before use, and remove cleaning residue that could affect the controls or mark the glass.

Clean the air vents of the Corra induction hob every 16 days. Follow the instructions for accessing and cleaning them without removing protective covers. Keep ventilation openings free from grease, dust and obstructions. Do not push tools into the vents. Contact Halvard Home if you cannot clean them safely.

Have the Corra induction hob safety-checked every 6 months. Arrange this through a suitably qualified professional and keep the service record. A scheduled check does not replace action when a fault appears. Stop using the hob if it gives off smoke, smells of burning or operates unpredictably.

If you have an implanted medical device, seek advice from your clinician or device manufacturer about using induction cooking equipment. If Halvard Home issues a safety notice or recall affecting your hob, follow its instructions and do not resume use unless the notice permits it.

The Fenwick cooker hood is intended to remove cooking fumes from a domestic kitchen when installed and used as directed. Read the instructions supplied with it and keep them somewhere accessible. If the instructions are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before using the appliance.

Installation must be carried out by a suitably qualified installer. The hood must be securely fixed, correctly connected to the electrical supply and positioned in line with the installation instructions. Do not move it, alter its fittings or change its ventilation arrangement yourself.

Keep ventilation openings clear. Do not cover the hood or obstruct the route through which air enters or leaves it. If extraction seems weak, stop cooking if fumes are building up and arrange for the cause to be checked.

Take particular care if the kitchen contains a fuel-burning appliance. Extraction can affect the air supply needed for safe combustion and may draw harmful gases into the room. Ask a qualified installer to confirm that the ventilation arrangement is suitable before using the hood.

Use the controls as described in the supplied instructions. Do not operate the hood with wet hands or use it if a control is loose, cracked or behaving unexpectedly. Keep electrical connections protected from splashes, steam leaks and cleaning liquids.

Stay attentive while cooking, especially when heating oil or fat. Grease can catch fire and spread into the hood. Do not leave cooking unattended, and do not allow flames to reach the appliance. Avoid cooking methods that deliberately produce exposed flames beneath it.

The hood and its accessible surfaces may become hot during cooking. Keep children away from hot surfaces and controls. Anyone who needs help to use the appliance safely should have suitable supervision. Do not allow children to play with the hood or clean it unsupervised.

Do not rest cookware, utensils, cloths or packaging on the hood. Keep combustible materials away from the cooking area. Do not hang objects from the appliance or lean on it, as this could damage its mountings or bring objects into contact with heat.

Let the Fenwick cooker hood cool for 25 minutes before cleaning it. Switch it off and isolate it from the electrical supply before removing filters or touching internal areas intended for customer cleaning. If surfaces remain hot, do not touch them.

Follow the cleaning instructions supplied with the appliance. Use suitable cleaning materials and avoid abrasive products that could damage surfaces or markings. Do not spray liquid into controls, lighting fittings or openings. Do not use a steam cleaner or immerse electrical parts in water.

Grease deposits increase the risk of fire. Check filters for contamination and clean or replace them according to the supplied instructions. Do not run the hood with filters missing, incorrectly fitted or damaged. Contact Halvard Home if you are unsure which replacement filter is suitable.

Only remove parts that the customer instructions identify as removable. Do not open electrical housings, bypass protective features or attempt repairs. Internal work must be left to a suitably qualified technician. Replacement parts must be suitable for the appliance and fitted as directed.

Have the Fenwick cooker hood safety-checked every 13 months. Arrange the check through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified technician. A safety check does not replace cleaning, careful use or prompt attention to faults. Keep the service record with the appliance instructions.

Stop using the hood if you notice smoke, a burning smell, unusual vibration, damaged wiring or signs of overheating. Isolate the electrical supply if it is safe to do so. Do not restart the appliance to test whether the fault has cleared.

If a fire starts, do not use water on burning oil or electrical equipment. Do not reach through flames to operate controls. Leave the area, keep others away and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to protect the appliance.

If you feel unwell while a fuel-burning appliance is operating, leave the affected area and seek urgent help. Do not assume the cooker hood makes the room safe. Suspected combustion or ventilation problems require assessment by an appropriately qualified professional before use resumes.

Follow safety notices or recall instructions issued by Halvard Home for the Fenwick cooker hood. If a notice tells you to stop using it, leave it disconnected until the required action has been completed. Contact Halvard Home if you need help understanding whether a notice applies.

Installation and moving must be carried out with care to protect you, your home and the Fenwick cooker hood. Do not use the appliance if it appears damaged or if you are unsure whether it has been fitted safely. Contact Halvard Home for advice before proceeding.

Arrange for a suitably qualified installer to assess the intended position and fit the appliance. Electrical work must be carried out by a competent electrician in accordance with applicable requirements. Do not attempt to alter your home’s wiring or modify the appliance to make it fit.

Check the packaging and appliance for damage before installation. Look for bent panels, loose parts, broken fittings or damage to the plug and cable. Keep packaging away from children and pets. If something appears wrong, leave the appliance disconnected and contact Halvard Home.

The Fenwick cooker hood must be installed within 220 centimetres of its socket. Position it so that the cable is not stretched, trapped or exposed to heat. The socket must remain accessible for safe disconnection. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor to reach an unsuitable socket.

Install the Fenwick cooker hood at least 121 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Your installer must also check the positioning requirements supplied with the cooking appliance. If those requirements conflict with the proposed installation, do not proceed until a safe arrangement has been confirmed.

The supporting wall or structure must be suitable for the appliance and its fixings. Your installer should check for concealed wiring, pipes and other services before drilling. Do not rely on damaged surfaces or unsuitable plugs and screws. Seek specialist advice if the supporting structure is uncertain.

Ventilation and ducting must be assessed as part of the installation. Air must not be discharged into a flue used to remove fumes from an appliance burning gas or another fuel. Where fuel-burning appliances share the space, obtain professional advice about ventilation and the risk of fumes entering your home.

Use fittings and accessories approved for the Fenwick cooker hood and follow the installation instructions supplied with it. Do not cut, bend or remove structural parts to accommodate cupboards or ducting. Keep ventilation openings clear and ensure surrounding furniture does not obstruct access needed for cleaning or servicing.

Before moving the appliance, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply. If it is connected through fixed wiring, arrange for a competent electrician to disconnect it. Never pull on the cable to remove the plug, and do not attempt to move the appliance while it remains connected.

Allow hot surfaces to cool before handling the appliance. Remove loose items from the working area and protect nearby surfaces against accidental damage. Check that the route is clear of obstacles and that doors can be opened without interfering with carrying. Keep children and pets away from the work.

Do not tilt the Fenwick cooker hood more than 30 degrees when carrying it. Arrange help with lifting rather than attempting to handle an awkward load alone. Support the appliance securely, following its handling instructions. Do not lift it by the cable, controls, filters or decorative trim.

Protect the appliance against knocks during transport and secure it against sliding or falling. Keep the cable and plug protected from crushing and abrasion. Do not place objects on the appliance or use its casing as a support. If secure transport cannot be arranged, seek help from a professional mover.

After moving the Fenwick cooker hood, wait 26 hours before switching it on. This does not replace the need for safe installation and inspection. Before reconnecting it, check for transport damage and confirm that the mountings, electrical connection and ventilation arrangements are suitable for its new position.

Ask the installer to explain how to disconnect the appliance safely and how to recognise a problem with its installation. Keep the installation instructions and relevant service records where you can find them. If you move home, leave the appliance’s documents with it if it remains installed.

If the appliance becomes loose, makes an unusual noise, smells of burning or shows signs of electrical damage, stop using it. Disconnect it only if you can do so safely. Do not remove covers or attempt repairs yourself. Contact Halvard Home or a qualified service professional for guidance.

Check Halvard Home’s safety and recall information before reinstalling an appliance that has been stored or passed to you. If a safety notice applies, follow its instructions rather than assuming that moving or refitting resolves the issue. Do not pass on an appliance that is subject to an unresolved safety warning.

Use the Mira robot vacuum for domestic floor cleaning as described in its instructions. Read the safety information supplied with it and keep that information accessible. If you are unsure whether a surface or setting is suitable, contact Halvard Home before using the appliance there.

Check the appliance, charging dock, plug and cable for visible damage before use. Do not use equipment with cracked casing, exposed wiring, loose fittings or signs of overheating. Stop using the appliance if its behaviour changes unexpectedly, and seek advice rather than trying to work around the fault.

Keep the cleaning area clear of loose cables, clothing, packaging and objects that could become caught in the brushes or wheels. Secure trailing curtain cords and move fragile items out of its path. Do not rely on the appliance to recognise hazards or protect belongings.

Keep children and pets away from moving brushes and wheels. Do not let children ride on the appliance, play with its controls or treat the charging dock as a toy. Make sure anyone who operates it understands the instructions and can use it safely.

Use the appliance indoors on suitable, dry flooring. Keep it away from rain, wet rooms and places where water may collect. Do not use it to collect liquids, hot ash, glowing embers, flammable substances or material that could harm someone if disturbed or spread.

Do not use the appliance near exposed flames, portable heaters or flammable vapours. Keep it away from substances that could ignite if they contact electrical equipment. If cleaning could disturb hazardous dust or unknown residue, leave the material undisturbed and obtain suitable specialist advice.

Protect access to stairs, balconies and changes in floor level where a fall could cause harm. Keep sensors clean and follow the setup instructions for your home. Do not assume that sensing features will prevent a fall, particularly where the surroundings have changed.

Place the charging dock on a stable, dry surface in a ventilated position, following the supplied instructions. Keep the cable away from walkways and moving parts. Do not cover the dock or appliance with fabric, or place them where an exit could be obstructed.

Use charging equipment and replacement parts approved by Halvard Home for the Mira robot vacuum. Do not adapt connectors, alter the plug or use a damaged socket. Handle electrical connections with dry hands, and disconnect by holding the plug rather than pulling the cable.

Switch the appliance off before removing trapped material, handling the brushes or carrying out cleaning described in the instructions. Disconnect the charging dock from the electricity supply before cleaning it. Keep fingers, hair and loose clothing away from moving parts, even when investigating a blockage.

Clean the air vents of the Mira robot vacuum every 32 days. Follow the cleaning method in the supplied instructions and keep moisture away from electrical openings. Do not push tools into the vents or use cleaning substances that could damage the casing or internal components.

Empty the dust container and care for the filter as directed in the instructions. Avoid breathing in collected dust, and wash your hands after handling debris. Do not operate the appliance with the dust container or filter missing, damaged or incorrectly fitted.

Have the Mira robot vacuum safety-checked every 24 months. Contact Halvard Home for advice on arranging the check through an approved service provider. A safety check does not replace care or checks for visible damage, and it does not make a known fault safe to ignore.

Do not open the battery casing, puncture it or attempt an unauthorised repair. If the battery appears swollen, leaks or gives off an unusual smell, stop using and charging the appliance. Keep people away from leaking material and contact Halvard Home for safe handling advice.

If the appliance produces smoke, sparks or signs of fire, move away and keep others away. Do not touch or move equipment that appears unsafe. Disconnect the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. Leave the area and contact the emergency services if there is a fire.

Store the appliance and its charging equipment in a dry place, away from heat and direct sunlight. Follow the instructions for storage and transport. Do not put a damaged battery in household rubbish or send it through the post without appropriate handling advice.

Check safety notices from Halvard Home and follow recall instructions that apply to your appliance. If a notice tells you to stop using it, do not restart it because it appears to work normally. Contact Halvard Home if you need help understanding a warning or arranging support.

Choose a dry, sheltered place inside your home for the Mira robot vacuum and its charging base. The floor must be firm, level and suitable for supporting the base without rocking or slipping. Do not install it where rain, splashes, condensation or leaking pipes could reach the robot, charging contacts, cable or plug.

The Mira robot vacuum must be installed within 168 centimetres of its socket. For this requirement, the installed position is where the robot rests for charging. Choose a socket that remains accessible so you can disconnect the supply safely. Do not place furniture over the cable or trap it behind the charging base.

Connect the charging base directly to a suitable wall socket using the power supply supplied for the Mira robot vacuum. Do not use an adaptor or extension lead to reach an unsuitable location. If the plug does not fit, or the socket feels loose, stop installation and ask a qualified electrician to check the socket.

Install the Mira robot vacuum at least 101 centimetres from a gas hob or open flame. Keep the installation area away from heaters, hot surfaces and places where grease or steam collects. Do not put the charging base beneath curtains or beside materials that could catch fire if an electrical fault develops.

Position the base where the robot can approach it without crossing a doorway used by people or pets. Keep the approach clear of loose rugs, trailing cables, clothing and objects that could catch beneath the robot. Avoid locations beside stairs, exposed edges or changes in floor level where a positioning error could lead to a fall.

Route the power cable against a wall without stretching, twisting or crushing it. Keep it out of walking routes and away from the robot’s cleaning path. Do not hide damage with tape or cover the cable with a rug. If the cable or plug is damaged, leave the charging base unplugged and contact Halvard Home.

Before handling the robot or changing its installed position, stop cleaning through its controls and switch it off. Disconnect the charging base at the socket by holding the plug, not pulling the cable. Make sure your hands are dry. Do not touch the plug or charging contacts if there is moisture around them.

Check that the robot is cool and shows no signs of damage before lifting it. If it is unusually hot, swollen, leaking, smoking or giving off an unusual smell, do not carry it through your home. Keep people and pets away. If there is smoke or fire, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

Do not tilt the Mira robot vacuum more than 51 degrees when carrying it. Support the body securely from underneath and keep it steady. Do not lift it by its cover, bumper, wheels, brushes or charging contacts. Ask for help if handling it safely is difficult, rather than trying to balance it against your body.

Remove loose accessories before carrying the robot and secure covers as described in the user instructions. Carry the charging base separately so its cable cannot swing, snag or cause a trip. Never drag the robot across the floor or let children carry it. Keep pets away while you are moving equipment.

For transport, use protective packaging that supports the robot and prevents it from sliding or being crushed. Keep the power supply and cable protected from impact. Do not leave the robot in a damp vehicle or where direct sunlight could cause overheating. Tell anyone handling the package that it contains an appliance with a battery.

After moving the Mira robot vacuum, wait 37 hours before switching it on. Leave it switched off during this wait and prevent accidental operation through its controls or app. Check its condition and the new installation area before reconnecting the charging base. Do not switch it on if you suspect damage.

Make sure the charging contacts are dry and free from visible dirt, and check that the base sits securely. Review the robot’s saved map and restricted areas when its location changes. Do not assume that settings from its previous position will protect stairs, cables or other hazards in the new location.

If you cannot meet these installation requirements, do not use the proposed location. Contact Halvard Home for advice rather than modifying the robot, charging base or power supply. If a safety notice or recall applies to your Mira robot vacuum, follow that notice and do not reinstall or restart it against those instructions.

We use the information collected during booking and assessment to manage the safety concern, arrange the remedy and maintain recall records. We share relevant details with authorised service partners where needed to carry out this work. You can ask us to explain what information we hold and how it is used.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Northern Ireland/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
If you live in Northern Ireland, Halvard Home can arrange a safety visit when an appliance may present a risk. We use the information you provide, together with our safety findings, to decide what action is needed. Our aim is to make the arrangements clear and help you stay safe.

Stop using the appliance if you believe it is unsafe or if we have told you to stop. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. Do not attempt repairs, remove covers or test whether a reported fault is still present.

If there is smoke, fire, a strong smell of burning or an immediate danger, move away from the appliance and contact the emergency services. Do not put yourself at risk to switch it off or retrieve belongings. A safety visit is not a substitute for an emergency response.

Contact Halvard Home through the support details shown on our official website or in your appliance documents. Tell us what happened, where the appliance is located and whether anyone may be at risk. Explain whether you have received a safety notice from us.

We may ask for information from the appliance label and a description of the fault. Only look for the label if it is safe and accessible. Do not move a heavy appliance, reach behind damaged wiring or enter an unsafe area to find information for us.

Urgent safety visits in Northern Ireland are made within 21 hours.

We assess urgency using the nature of the reported danger and the advice of our safety team. We will explain whether an urgent visit is being arranged and what you should do while awaiting help. Follow the safety instructions we give you, even if the appliance appears to be working normally.

When arranging a visit, we will confirm the address, access arrangements and how to contact you. Please tell us about shared entrances, restricted access or anything that could prevent an engineer from reaching the appliance safely. We will explain how to recognise the person attending on our behalf.

Tell us if you need communication or access support. This could include written information in an accessible format, support with understanding instructions or arrangements involving a trusted person. We will discuss your needs respectfully and agree practical arrangements with you. You do not need to share unrelated medical information.

Please keep the route to the appliance clear where it is safe to do so. Keep children and pets away from the affected area. Do not disconnect fixed fittings or move the appliance unless we have specifically advised you to do so and you can follow that advice safely.

Our engineer will explain the purpose of the visit and ask for permission to access the appliance. They will assess its condition and carry out the safety work authorised by Halvard Home. If the surroundings make the work unsafe, they will explain the problem and refer it to our safety team.

A visit may result in a repair, further assessment or a recommendation that the appliance be removed. We will tell you what the outcome means and whether the appliance must remain unused. Do not resume using it unless we have clearly confirmed that it is safe to do so.

Recall collections in Northern Ireland are made within 46 working days.

If your appliance is included in a recall, we will explain the collection arrangements and the remedy available under that recall. Keep the appliance available for collection and follow our storage and isolation advice. Do not sell it, give it away or leave it where someone could take it for use.

Tell us if your circumstances change or you cannot provide access as agreed. We will review the arrangements with you and explain the next steps. If access cannot be gained, the safety concern remains open, and the instruction not to use the appliance continues to apply.

We use the personal information needed to assess the concern, arrange attendance and keep a record of the outcome. Relevant details may be shared with the service provider attending for Halvard Home. Please avoid sending unrelated personal documents or images when reporting a safety issue.

If you are unhappy with the arrangements or believe the risk has changed, contact us and explain your concern. We will refer unresolved safety matters to the appropriate team and tell you how your complaint will be handled. These arrangements do not affect your statutory rights.

cell.item: POL-SAF/Island Areas/Safety visits in this region

result.text:
This section explains how Halvard Home arranges safety visits and recall collections for customers in Island Areas. Your safety guides our decisions about access, travel and the work needed at your home. We will explain what is happening and what you need to do.

If you believe an appliance is unsafe, stop using it and contact us through our official customer support channels. Follow the safety advice in the recall notice or the instructions given by our safety team. Do not attempt repairs or remove protective covers.

Urgent safety visits in Island Areas are made within 51 hours.

Our safety team will assess the information you provide and explain whether an urgent visit is needed. Tell us about smoke, unusual smells, visible damage or unexpected operation. Do not test the appliance to demonstrate a fault or put yourself at risk when gathering information.

If there is fire, smoke or another immediate danger, move away from the affected area and contact the emergency services. Do not remain nearby to speak to us or retrieve paperwork. Contact Halvard Home from somewhere safe when you are able to do so.

When arranging a visit, we will ask for your address, contact details and information needed to identify the affected appliance. We may ask about its condition and location. Photographs can help, but please provide them only if taking them is safe.

Please tell us about access arrangements that could affect the visit, such as ferry travel, restricted landing access, steep paths or locked communal entrances. We use this information to plan suitable transport and make sure the visiting specialist can reach your home safely.

We will discuss the appointment with you and explain how we will confirm it. Tell us which contact method is accessible for you. If communication services are unreliable where you live, we will agree a practical way to share arrangements and important safety information.

Please let us know about disability, mobility or communication needs that may affect the visit. You do not need to share a medical history. We will discuss reasonable adjustments with you and explain how these will be reflected in the arrangements.

An adult authorised to give access must be present for the visit. Please keep the route to the appliance clear where this can be done safely. Do not move a damaged appliance, disconnect fixed connections or undertake lifting to prepare for our arrival.

The visiting specialist will identify themselves and explain the purpose of the visit. If you are unsure whether a visitor represents Halvard Home, keep your door closed and contact us through an official channel. You should not feel pressured to allow access.

Recall collections in Island Areas are made within 44 working days.

If your recall notice requires collection, we will explain how it will be arranged and what preparation is safe. Leave the appliance in place unless we advise otherwise. Tell us if its location or condition makes removal difficult so that we can plan appropriate handling.

You do not need to arrange transport to the mainland yourself. Halvard Home will organise the collection arrangements covered by the recall. Please do not leave the appliance at a harbour, ferry terminal or public collection point unless we have expressly agreed this with you.

During a safety visit, the specialist will assess the appliance and carry out the action authorised under the safety process. This may involve making it safe, completing an approved repair or arranging removal. They will explain the outcome and whether the appliance must remain unused.

We will ask your permission before carrying out work in your home. If the proposed action changes following inspection, the specialist will explain why. You can ask questions or decline access, but an unresolved safety concern may mean the appliance must remain unused.

Island travel can be affected by weather, ferry disruption and local access restrictions. We take these conditions into account when organising attendance. If an arrangement is disrupted, we will contact you, explain the problem and agree a safe alternative without asking you to manage transport.

After the visit or collection, we will provide confirmation of the action taken and explain what happens next. Keep this information with your recall correspondence. If you remain concerned about safety, access or the handling of your case, contact our support team and ask for a review.

You can request an engineer visit through Halvard Home’s customer service team or booking service. Tell us what has happened and describe the fault clearly so we can assess whether a visit is appropriate.

We may ask you to carry out safe checks before arranging an appointment. These checks can help identify the cause of the problem. Do not remove covers, interfere with wiring or attempt repairs yourself.

If you believe the appliance is unsafe, stop using it and tell us when you contact us. Follow the safety instructions supplied with it. Do not continue using it simply because a visit has been booked.

To arrange a visit, we need your name, contact details and the address where the appliance is installed. We may also ask for proof of purchase and information about your warranty or service cover.

Please make sure the details you provide are accurate. Tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything at the property that could affect the engineer’s ability to attend or work safely.

Standard engineer visits are booked within 16 working days of a request. We will discuss available appointments with you and confirm the booking arrangements through your chosen contact method, where that method is supported.

Each visit is given an arrival window of 5 hours. The engineer may arrive at any point within that window. We cannot promise a particular arrival time unless we expressly confirm this when booking.

A request for a visit is not a confirmed appointment. Your appointment is confirmed when we send you a booking confirmation or our customer service team expressly confirms it with you.

Check your confirmation carefully and contact us if the address, contact details or appointment arrangements are incorrect. Please also tell us if your circumstances change after the booking has been confirmed.

We may contact you to clarify the fault or discuss preparations for the visit. Please use contact details where we can reach you and check messages relating to your appointment.

An adult who can authorise access and discuss the fault must be present. If you arrange for someone else to attend, make sure they understand the problem and are authorised to agree to proposed work.

The engineer must be able to reach the appliance safely. Clear the surrounding area and keep pets away from the work space. Tell us beforehand if moving the appliance requires special arrangements.

Please explain any accessibility requirements when requesting your appointment. We will discuss reasonable adjustments with you and explain what we can arrange. You do not need to share medical information that is unrelated to those arrangements.

If you rent your home, check whether you need permission from your landlord or property manager before booking. You are responsible for obtaining permission for access and for work affecting the property.

We will explain whether the visit is expected to be covered by your warranty or service agreement. Booking an appointment does not itself confirm that the fault or the proposed repair is covered.

If a charge may apply, we will explain the basis of that charge before you agree to the booking. If the engineer identifies work outside the agreed scope, we will seek your approval before proceeding.

An engineer visit does not guarantee that a repair can be completed during the appointment. The engineer may need to investigate the fault, obtain suitable parts or arrange specialist support before work can proceed.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact us using the details in your booking confirmation. Please give reasonable notice so we can update the engineer’s schedule and discuss alternative arrangements where needed.

Tell us if the fault disappears before the visit. We can discuss whether attendance is still appropriate. Do not assume the booking has been cancelled unless we have confirmed this to you.

If the engineer cannot gain access, or the property is not safe to work in, the visit may not proceed. We will explain what needs to change before a replacement appointment can be arranged.

We may need to change an appointment because of engineer availability, travel disruption or circumstances outside our control. If this happens, we will contact you, explain the position and discuss a replacement booking.

We use the information provided for your booking to arrange attendance and manage the service request, in line with our privacy notice. Nothing in these booking terms limits your statutory consumer rights.

We will explain the charges that may apply to your engineer visit before you confirm your booking. These may include attendance, assessment, labour and replacement parts. Your booking confirmation will set out the agreed charges and explain which work they cover. Prices include VAT where applicable.

Whether you need to pay depends on your warranty cover, the reason for the visit and the work required. We may ask for proof of purchase or other information to check your cover. If we cannot confirm it, we will explain your options before arranging chargeable work.

An attendance or assessment charge may apply even if you decide not to proceed with a repair. We will tell you about this when you book. The charge covers the engineer attending and investigating the reported fault, rather than a guarantee that a repair will be possible.

Labour after the first hour is charged at £55.00 an hour. We will explain how the labour charge is calculated and recorded before you agree to chargeable work. The engineer will seek your approval if the expected labour cost changes as the assessment or repair progresses.

Parts fitted outside the warranty carry a handling charge of 28%. We calculate this charge on the price of the replacement parts, not on labour or attendance charges. Your quotation and invoice will show the handling charge separately so that you can see how it affects the total.

Where we can identify the work needed from the information you provide, we may offer a quotation before the visit. Otherwise, the engineer will assess the fault and explain the proposed repair and its cost. You can ask for clarification without agreeing to the work.

An estimate is a guide based on the information available, while a quotation states the price for the work described. We will make clear which we are providing. If the scope of the work changes, we will explain the reason and ask you to approve any revised price.

You do not have to accept a proposed repair. If you decline, you will only need to pay charges that were clearly explained and agreed, such as an applicable attendance or assessment charge. We will not charge for replacement parts that you have not authorised us to fit.

Work covered by your warranty will be handled under its terms. If an assessment shows that the fault is not covered, the engineer will explain why and discuss any charges with you. We will not treat your request for a warranty visit as permission to carry out chargeable repairs.

Please tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything else that could affect the visit. If these are likely to create an additional cost, we will discuss it with you. Expenses that were not disclosed and agreed will not be added to your bill without your consent.

If the engineer cannot gain access or cannot safely carry out the agreed work, a charge may apply where this was explained in your booking terms. We will consider the circumstances, including whether the problem was within your control, and explain the basis of any charge we propose.

If you need to change or cancel your booking, please contact us using the details in your confirmation. Any cancellation charge must have been made clear when you booked. We will explain how it applies to your circumstances and take account of any legal right you have to cancel.

We will not charge you for a visit we cancel or for work needed solely to put right an error we have made. If you have already paid for work that we cannot provide, we will explain the refund due and arrange it through an appropriate payment method.

Your invoice will describe the work carried out and show the charges clearly. Payment arrangements will be explained when you book or approve the repair. Please use an accepted payment method and ask for a receipt if you need confirmation that your payment has been received.

If you think a charge is wrong, contact us with your booking details and explain your concern. We will review the agreed work, the engineer’s record and the invoice, then explain our decision. These charging terms do not limit your statutory rights or prevent you from challenging an incorrect bill.

If you no longer need your engineer visit, please let Halvard Home know so that we can cancel the booking and release the appointment. Please contact us directly rather than relying on a message passed through someone who is not acting on our behalf.

Cancel a visit at least 56 hours before it is due to avoid a charge. A visit cancelled later than that is charged at £47.00.

The cancellation deadline is based on the scheduled start of your visit, as shown in your booking confirmation. If your confirmation does not make this clear, please contact us so that we can explain which appointment details apply to your booking.

Use the contact details in your booking confirmation to request a cancellation. If you cannot find that confirmation, use the customer service contact details on the Halvard Home website. Please make clear that you want to cancel an engineer visit.

Give us the name on the booking, the address the engineer is due to attend and suitable contact details. Include any booking reference available to you. We may ask for further information if we cannot confidently identify the visit you want to cancel.

Please do not send payment card details or sensitive personal information with your cancellation request. We only need enough information to locate the booking, check that you are entitled to change it and confirm what you have asked us to do.

We treat a cancellation request as received when it reaches the contact channel you have used, provided that the request clearly identifies the booking and asks us to cancel it. An unanswered call does not cancel your visit, so please use a channel that lets you submit your request.

We will confirm that your visit has been cancelled using the contact details held with your booking. Our confirmation will explain whether a cancellation charge applies. Please check that the confirmation refers to the correct address and appointment.

If you do not receive confirmation, contact us to check that your request has reached us. Keep a copy of any message you send and any acknowledgement you receive. These can help us resolve a disagreement about when you asked to cancel.

A delay in our handling of a clear cancellation request will not change when we received it. If you believe a charge has been applied because of an administrative error, tell us and provide any relevant confirmation or correspondence you have.

Someone else may request cancellation on your behalf if you have authorised them to manage the booking. We may need to check their authority before sharing booking information. Please make sure they have the details needed to identify your appointment.

If your landlord, managing agent or another organisation arranged the visit, contact them about cancellation unless your booking confirmation tells you to deal with us directly. A message to the person who arranged the visit is not necessarily a cancellation request received by Halvard Home.

If you want to rearrange rather than cancel, please say so when you contact us. We will explain the available options and any applicable terms before making the change. Do not assume that asking about availability has cancelled your existing booking.

Please also tell us if access to the property has become difficult or if the engineer may be unable to carry out the planned work. We can discuss whether the visit should go ahead. Reporting an access problem does not itself cancel the appointment.

If we cancel your visit, we will not apply a customer cancellation charge. We will contact you using the details on your booking and explain how to arrange a replacement appointment if you still need an engineer.

Where a cancellation charge applies, we will explain how payment will be collected or requested. We will not describe the charge as payment for work completed at your home. It relates to the cancellation of the booked visit.

If you have already paid towards the visit, we will explain how cancellation affects that payment and whether a refund is due. Any refund or deduction will be set out clearly so that you can understand what has happened to your payment.

Please contact us if you think we have applied these terms incorrectly or if you need help making a cancellation request. We will review the booking information and explain our decision. These cancellation terms do not limit any rights you have under consumer law.

The Brio kettle should be serviced every 44 months. This schedule applies to normal household use. Servicing helps keep the kettle in safe working order and gives an engineer an opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults that may not be obvious during everyday use.

We calculate the service due date from the delivery date recorded on your account. After a completed routine service, we calculate the next due date from the date of that visit. If your records are missing or incorrect, contact Halvard Home so we can check them with you.

A reminder is sent 4 weeks before the Brio kettle is due for a service. We use the contact details held on your account, so please tell us if these change. The reminder invites you to arrange a visit; it does not mean an appointment has already been booked.

You remain responsible for arranging servicing even if a reminder does not reach you. You can contact Halvard Home to check when your kettle is due or to discuss a suitable appointment. Please mention any access requirements or communication preferences when making the booking.

A routine service of the Brio kettle takes about 135 minutes. This is a guide rather than a guarantee. The engineer will explain if the condition of your kettle affects the planned work or if a fault means that a separate repair appointment is needed.

A routine service of the Brio kettle costs £78.00. This price includes the engineer’s routine inspection, standard service checks and assessment of the kettle’s condition. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are not included unless we expressly confirm otherwise when you book.

We will explain any proposed additional work and its price before asking for your agreement. You do not have to accept a repair simply because an engineer recommends it. If you decline work needed for safe operation, the engineer will explain why the kettle should not be used.

To arrange a service, contact Halvard Home through our usual customer support channels. Have your purchase details available if you can, and describe any changes in how the kettle works. Tell us about leaking, unusual smells, unexpected switching behaviour or visible damage rather than leaving these concerns until the visit.

A service appointment is not a substitute for reporting a suspected safety fault. If the kettle appears unsafe, stop using it and disconnect it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely. Contact Halvard Home for advice before using it again.

Before the engineer arrives, make sure the kettle is unplugged, empty and cool. Leave it somewhere accessible, together with its base and any documents relevant to a reported fault. Do not dismantle it or attempt electrical repairs in preparation for the appointment.

Please provide a clear working area and keep children and pets away from the engineer’s tools and equipment. Someone able to describe the kettle’s condition and authorise any agreed work should be available. Let us know beforehand if there are restrictions on entering your home.

During the service, the engineer will inspect the kettle and its accessible components, check its controls and assess whether it operates safely. The work may include cleaning accessible areas where appropriate. Servicing does not cover damage caused by an unsafe electricity supply or unsuitable conditions in the home.

Routine care remains important between services. Follow the care instructions supplied with your kettle, including the guidance on cleaning and descaling. Avoid abrasive materials or cleaning products that the instructions do not recommend. Regular servicing does not replace this care or remove the need to report faults.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact Halvard Home as soon as you know. We will explain the available arrangements and any applicable charge before confirming a replacement booking. If we need to change the visit, we will contact you to discuss alternatives.

After the visit, the engineer will explain the findings and provide a service record showing the work completed and any recommendations. Keep this with your purchase documents. We will update your service due date where the routine service has been completed.

An incomplete visit does not automatically reset the servicing schedule. If access, the kettle’s condition or an unresolved fault prevents completion, we will explain what needs to happen next. Nothing in this servicing schedule limits your legal rights if your kettle is faulty or does not meet the standards required by law.

Common repairs to the Brio kettle include faults with the lid, switch, heating element and automatic shut-off. Leaks, damage to the power base and problems with the power connection may also need attention. We assess the reported fault before recommending a repair, replacement part or engineer visit.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, smells of burning, gives an electric shock or has a damaged cable or plug. Switch off the electricity supply and unplug it if safe to do so. Do not handle a wet plug or base, and keep the kettle out of use until it has been assessed.

If the kettle does not heat, check that the socket is switched on and that the kettle is seated correctly on its base. Only make these checks if the kettle, cable, plug and base appear undamaged and dry. Do not open the casing or attempt to repair electrical components yourself.

Limescale can affect heating, cause unusual noise and interfere with normal operation. Follow the cleaning and descaling instructions supplied with your kettle, using a suitable descaling product as directed. Let the kettle cool before cleaning. Do not immerse the kettle or its power base in water.

Replace the filter of the Brio kettle every 18 weeks. Use a filter approved for this model and follow the fitting instructions. If the filter does not sit securely, do not force it into place. Contact us for advice rather than trying to alter the filter or its housing.

A lid that sticks, fails to close or opens during use needs attention. Do not hold the lid down while the kettle boils or use anything to keep it shut. If cleaning the accessible surfaces does not resolve the problem, stop using the kettle and contact us.

When you request a repair, describe what happens and whether you have noticed leaking, unusual smells or visible damage. We may ask for proof of purchase and photographs to help assess the fault. Do not plug in or operate an unsafe kettle to demonstrate the problem.

We will explain whether the fault can be dealt with through an approved replacement part, an engineer visit or an assessment at a service centre. An engineer visit is not required for every fault. The available route depends on the condition of the kettle and the work needed.

Before you agree to a paid repair, we will explain the proposed work and any charges that apply. Tell us if you need clarification before giving approval. If the assessment reveals additional work, we will seek your agreement before proceeding with work that changes the agreed price.

For an engineer visit, make sure the kettle and its base are accessible, cool and empty. Keep the surrounding area clear and dry. Tell us about access needs when arranging the visit so that we can discuss suitable arrangements and explain any limits on the service.

The engineer will inspect the kettle and decide whether it can be repaired safely. They may replace a faulty component rather than the complete appliance. If the repair cannot be completed during the visit, we will explain the reason and discuss the available options with you.

Spare parts for the Brio kettle are stocked for 9 years after the model is discontinued. Availability of a particular part may depend on stock and supply conditions. We will check availability before confirming work that needs a replacement component and tell you if a supply problem affects the proposed repair.

Paid repairs to the Brio kettle come with their own guarantee. Repairs are guaranteed for 122 days. This guarantee covers the work carried out and parts supplied as part of that repair. It does not replace your statutory rights or limit any separate rights you have under an applicable appliance guarantee.

If a repaired fault returns, contact us with your repair confirmation and a description of the problem. We will assess whether it relates to the guaranteed work and explain how it will be resolved. Avoid arranging further work without contacting us, as this may make the original fault harder to assess.

Accidental damage, misuse and faults unrelated to the repair are not covered by the repair guarantee. We will explain our findings if we believe a reported problem falls outside that cover. You can ask us to review the assessment if you disagree, and we will explain how to raise a complaint.

Your Tessa dishwasher should be serviced according to the schedule recorded by Halvard Home for your appliance. This schedule reflects its service history and the information you have given us about its use. If you cannot find your schedule, contact our customer care team so we can confirm when a service is due.

Routine servicing helps us check the condition of your Tessa dishwasher and identify wear or faults that may need attention. It does not replace the cleaning and care described in your user guide. Please continue to follow that guidance between engineer visits, including advice about filters, spray arms and suitable cleaning products.

Owners of the Tessa dishwasher are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 6 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held against your appliance record, so please tell us if your email address, postal address or telephone details change.

The reminder explains how to arrange your appointment. It does not mean that an engineer visit has already been booked. Please contact us through the booking route shown in the reminder and choose an available appointment that suits you. We will confirm the arrangements using your preferred contact method where possible.

Your service remains due even if a reminder does not reach you. If you think a reminder is missing, check your service record or contact customer care. We can confirm the schedule, check your contact details and help you arrange a visit without relying on the reminder itself.

A routine service of the Tessa dishwasher takes about 230 minutes. Please bear this in mind when arranging access to your home. The engineer will explain if the condition of the appliance, access difficulties or a fault means that the visit cannot proceed as expected.

When booking, tell us about problems you have noticed, including unusual noises, leaks, poor cleaning or warning messages. This helps us understand whether a routine service is appropriate or whether you need a repair appointment instead. Please do not wait for a scheduled service if you suspect a safety problem.

Stop using the Tessa dishwasher if it appears unsafe. Follow the safety instructions in your user guide and contact us for advice. Do not remove protective panels or attempt internal repairs yourself. If there is water near electrical fittings, keep clear and seek appropriate help rather than trying to investigate.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the dishwasher and make sure the area around it is clear. The engineer must be able to reach the appliance safely and inspect its accessible connections. Please tell us when booking if fitted furniture, restricted access or the position of the appliance could affect the work.

Let us know about access needs or communication preferences that may affect your appointment. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you.
