Please also tell us about parking restrictions, entry requirements or anything else the engineer needs to know to reach your home and carry out the service safely.

An adult who can authorise the agreed work must be present for the visit. Keep children and pets away from the working area. The engineer may need to run the dishwasher as part of the checks, so please make sure its usual water and electricity supplies are available.

The engineer will explain the findings and tell you whether further work is recommended. Repairs and replacement parts are not automatically included in routine servicing. If work falls outside the agreed service, we will explain the proposed work and applicable charges and ask for your approval before proceeding.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact us using the details in your booking confirmation. Please let us know as soon as you become aware of a problem. If we need to rearrange the visit, we will contact you and help you choose another available appointment.

After the service, we will update your appliance record and confirm the servicing schedule that applies. Keep the service report with your appliance documents, particularly if it includes advice or recommended repairs. Contact us if the record appears incorrect or if you need an explanation of the engineer’s findings.

Servicing does not guarantee that a fault will not develop. If your Tessa dishwasher behaves differently after a visit, contact us and describe what has changed. We will review the service record and advise you on the appropriate next step. This policy does not affect your statutory rights.

If your Tessa dishwasher is not working as expected, contact Halvard Home before arranging a repair. Tell us what happens when you try to use it, whether water is left inside, and whether you have noticed a leak, an unusual smell or an unfamiliar noise.

We may suggest checks that are safe to carry out without tools, such as checking that the door closes properly or cleaning an accessible filter. Follow the user instructions and do not remove panels, disconnect internal wiring or attempt to reach parts inside the appliance casing.

Stop using the appliance if it leaks, smells of burning or appears electrically unsafe. If you can do so safely, switch it off at the mains and close the water supply valve. Keep clear of standing water near electrical connections and contact us for advice.

Common repairs include clearing an internal blockage, replacing a faulty pump, dealing with a damaged door seal and correcting faults that prevent water from heating. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so a description of the problem does not confirm which repair or replacement part is needed.

When you book, we will explain the visit arrangements and ask about access to the appliance. Please tell us if it is fitted behind a furniture door, installed in a tight space or difficult to reach. Mention any access needs that could affect how the engineer carries out the work.

Diagnosing a fault on the Tessa dishwasher costs £77.00 if no repair follows. We will explain how this charge applies when arranging your visit. The engineer will assess the fault and explain the findings before asking you to approve any repair that is not already covered.

If a repair is chargeable, we will provide a quote explaining the proposed work and the charges that apply. You can decline the repair before work starts. If the engineer discovers a different problem or needs to change the proposed work, we will seek your approval before proceeding.

Poor drainage may be caused by food debris, a blocked filter, a restricted waste connection or a faulty pump. The engineer will check the likely source before recommending action. A blockage in household plumbing may need attention from a plumber rather than work on the appliance itself.

Leaks can come from damaged seals, loose connections or faults within the appliance. The engineer will identify the source where access allows. Repairing the appliance does not include restoring cupboards, flooring or decoration affected by water, unless we expressly agree that work with you.

If dishes remain dirty or wet, the engineer may check the spray system, heating components and detergent dispenser. Loading, detergent choice and blocked spray openings can also affect results. Where the appliance is working correctly, we will explain the findings and offer practical guidance rather than recommend an unnecessary repair.

Unusual noises and problems with starting or selecting a programme may require checks to moving parts, the door latch or electrical controls. Please describe what you hear or see without trying to reproduce a fault that could be unsafe. Leave damaged cables and internal components untouched.

Please clear belongings from around the appliance and provide a safe route to the work area. Keep pets and children away while work is taking place. The engineer may pause or decline work if the installation, electrical supply or surrounding area makes the repair unsafe.

Spare parts for the Tessa dishwasher are stocked for 19 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for your repair will be checked when the required part is identified. If a part must be ordered, we will explain the arrangements and keep you informed about the repair.

Repairs to the Tessa dishwasher are guaranteed for 184 days. The guarantee covers faults arising from the repair work and parts supplied for that repair. It does not cover an unrelated fault, accidental damage or problems caused by misuse. Your statutory rights are not affected.

After completing the work, the engineer will carry out appropriate checks and explain any care instructions relevant to the repair. Please keep the repair record. If the fault returns or you are unhappy with the work, contact Halvard Home so we can review what happened and explain the next steps.

The Orrin heat pump should be serviced every 42 months. Following this schedule helps keep your heating working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to identify wear, damage or developing faults.

The servicing schedule applies even if your Orrin heat pump appears to be working normally. Changes inside the system may not be obvious during everyday use, so reliable performance does not replace the need for servicing.

Use the commissioning record as the starting point for your servicing schedule. After a completed service, use the service record to plan when the next scheduled visit is due.

If you do not have these records, contact Halvard Home for help. We can review the information available and advise you on arranging a service without asking you to estimate the installation date.

If you have moved into a property with an Orrin heat pump, ask the previous owner, landlord or managing agent for its service history. Keep these records with the operating instructions.

Where the service history is missing or unclear, tell us when you contact us. An engineer may need to assess the condition of the system before advising on its servicing needs.

You are responsible for arranging scheduled servicing unless your agreement with a landlord, managing agent or service provider says otherwise. If responsibility is unclear, check that agreement before making a booking.

Do not assume that a reminder will be sent or that a visit has been booked automatically. Keep a clear record of when servicing is due and contact us to arrange an appointment.

Servicing should be carried out by an engineer with suitable qualifications and experience for the work involved. Tasks involving refrigerant or electrical components must be undertaken by someone authorised to perform them.

When booking, explain that the visit is for scheduled servicing of the Orrin heat pump. Tell us about known faults, changes in performance, warning messages or previous repairs so we can prepare appropriately.

Let us know about access restrictions, parking arrangements and anything at the property that could affect the engineer’s safety. Tell us if you need accessible communication or support with the visit.

Before the appointment, make sure the engineer can safely reach the equipment and associated controls. Keep the surrounding area clear of stored belongings, and secure pets away from the work area.

Do not remove protective covers or attempt to prepare internal components yourself. Leave the system in its normal operating state unless Halvard Home or the attending engineer gives you different instructions.

The engineer will assess the equipment’s condition and carry out checks appropriate to the installation. The work may include inspection, cleaning, testing and adjustment where these are suitable and safe.

The scope of the service will depend on the installation, its condition and the applicable technical guidance. The engineer should explain any restriction that prevents the planned service from being completed.

A scheduled service is not the same as a repair visit. If the engineer finds a fault that falls outside the agreed service work, they will explain the findings and proposed action.

Work outside the agreed scope should not proceed without your approval, except where action is necessary to leave the equipment safe. Any proposed charges should be explained before you agree to chargeable work.

If the engineer identifies a safety concern, they may advise that the Orrin heat pump must not be used. Follow their instructions and do not restart equipment that has been left isolated.

After servicing, ask for a record of the work completed, the findings and any recommended action. Keep this information somewhere accessible so it can be referred to during future visits.

A visit that cannot be completed should not be recorded as a completed service. Ask what remains outstanding and how to arrange completion, including whether access or repairs must be addressed beforehand.

If servicing is overdue, contact Halvard Home to arrange a visit. Do not try to compensate by adjusting internal settings, opening the equipment or carrying out maintenance beyond the customer instructions.

Do not wait for scheduled servicing if the system develops a fault or appears unsafe. Follow the safety guidance in the operating instructions and contact Halvard Home for advice about the appropriate support.

Keep following the customer care instructions between services. Scheduled servicing does not replace those instructions, and customer maintenance does not replace professional servicing. If the guidance appears inconsistent, ask Halvard Home to clarify it.

If your Orrin heat pump is not heating as expected, is making an unfamiliar noise or appears to be leaking, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Tell us what you have noticed and whether the appliance displays a fault message. This helps us prepare for the engineer’s visit.

Before booking, check that the controls are set as intended and that the electricity supply has not been interrupted. Follow the checks described in your user guide, but do not remove covers or attempt work on electrical connections, refrigerant pipes or internal components. Leave those tasks to a suitably qualified engineer.

Diagnosing a fault on the Orrin heat pump costs £88.00 if no repair follows. The engineer will explain the findings and recommend what should happen next. If a repair is possible, we will tell you what the proposed work involves and provide a quotation before seeking your agreement.

You do not have to accept a repair quotation. If you choose not to proceed, the engineer will explain whether the appliance can safely remain in use. Where a fault creates a safety risk, they may need to leave the appliance switched off and tell you how to avoid using it accidentally.

Common repairs can involve controls, sensors, electrical connections, pumps or seals. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so we cannot confirm the required repair from a description alone. The engineer’s assessment determines whether an adjustment, a replacement component or further investigation is appropriate for the fault.

Replace the filter of the Orrin heat pump every 23 weeks. Use a suitable replacement specified in the user guide and follow the instructions for safe access. If the filter is difficult to reach, damaged or stuck, ask us for advice rather than forcing it out or changing the surrounding fittings.

Keep the area around the appliance clear so that air can circulate and the engineer can work safely. Remove loose belongings from the access route and secure pets away from the work area. Tell us before the visit about restricted access, parking difficulties or anything that could affect safe working.

An adult who can discuss the repair and authorise the proposed work must be present. If you are arranging a visit for someone else, make sure they understand what has been reported and what the engineer may need to inspect. Let us know about communication or accessibility needs when booking.

The engineer will use suitable replacement parts and carry out checks relevant to the repair. They may need access to the controls, electricity supply and connected heating system. We will explain if the reported problem appears to come from equipment or installation work outside the scope of the agreed repair.

If a required part is unavailable, we will explain what this means for the work and agree how to proceed. We will not substitute an unsuitable component to complete a repair. If further work changes the proposed scope or price, we will seek your approval before carrying it out.

Some faults cannot be resolved safely through a routine repair. Extensive damage, unsuitable installation or defects elsewhere in the heating system may need specialist attention. If this applies, the engineer will explain the concern and identify the type of work needed before repair work can proceed.

Repairs to the Orrin heat pump are guaranteed for 211 days. This guarantee covers faults caused by the repair work or by a component supplied as part of that repair. Contact Halvard Home if you believe the repair has failed, and describe the symptoms so we can assess your concern.

The repair guarantee does not cover unrelated faults, accidental damage, misuse or problems caused by unauthorised changes. We will explain our reasons if we decide that a reported issue falls outside the guarantee. This guarantee is additional to your statutory rights and does not restrict or replace them.

After the repair, the engineer will explain what was done and any operating advice relevant to the work. Keep the repair record with your appliance documents. If the original symptoms return, or you notice a burning smell, smoke or exposed wiring, stop using the appliance and contact us for advice.

The Lumen smart thermostat should be serviced every 29 months. This schedule supports reliable operation and helps identify wear, damage or faults that may not be apparent in everyday use. Routine servicing does not replace the care described in your user guide, and you should report concerns rather than wait for a scheduled visit.

We calculate the service due date from the recorded installation date or the date of the most recent completed routine service, as appropriate. If you do not know when your Lumen smart thermostat was installed or last serviced, contact Halvard Home so we can review the available records and advise you.

A reminder is sent 12 weeks before the Lumen smart thermostat is due for a service. We use the contact details held on your customer account. Please keep these details current and let us know if you change your preferred contact method or responsibility for the appliance passes to someone else.

The reminder invites you to arrange a visit; it does not reserve an appointment automatically. You remain responsible for booking the service, even if a reminder does not reach you. If you believe a reminder is missing or the due date is incorrect, contact us so we can check your record.

Appointments depend on engineer availability and access to your property. When you contact us, we will discuss the available arrangements and confirm the agreed visit details. Tell us about any access needs, communication preferences or circumstances that could affect the visit so we can consider suitable adjustments.

A routine service of the Lumen smart thermostat costs £182.00. This covers the planned inspection and routine servicing work agreed when you book. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside that scope are not included unless we expressly confirm otherwise. We will explain the payment arrangements before you confirm your booking.

If the engineer finds a fault requiring work beyond the routine service, they will explain the findings and any recommended action. We will seek your agreement to the proposed work and its cost before proceeding. You may decline additional work, although an unresolved fault could affect safe or reliable operation.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the Lumen smart thermostat safely. Clear the surrounding area and tell us about any restricted access, visible damage or other relevant concerns when booking. An adult authorised to discuss the service and approve any proposed changes must be available at the property.

The engineer may need access to the heating controls and related installation to carry out the service properly. Where relevant, please have the user guide and any previous service records available. Do not remove covers, disturb wiring or attempt to prepare internal components yourself.

During the visit, the engineer will assess the condition and operation of the Lumen smart thermostat and carry out the routine checks appropriate to the installation. They will explain any findings that need your attention. Servicing is not a guarantee against future faults and may not reveal problems that are not apparent during inspection.

If safe access is unavailable or the installation presents a hazard, the engineer may be unable to complete the service. We will explain why the work cannot proceed and what needs to change before another visit can be arranged. Any proposed charge associated with a further visit will be explained before booking.

Tell us if you need to change or cancel your appointment. We will explain the arrangements that apply to your booking and discuss availability if you wish to rearrange. If an engineer cannot attend as agreed, we will contact you using your recorded details and help arrange a suitable alternative.

After a completed service, we will provide a record of the work carried out and any recommendations. Keep this with your appliance documents. If the service could not be completed, the record will explain the outstanding work; an incomplete visit does not reset the routine servicing schedule.

If your Lumen smart thermostat behaves unexpectedly, shows damage or appears unsafe, stop using it where safe to do so and contact Halvard Home for advice. Do not wait for a service reminder. Follow the safety instructions in your user guide and do not attempt repairs yourself.

Routine servicing and warranty cover are separate matters. Any warranty conditions are set out in the warranty documents supplied with your Lumen smart thermostat. Nothing in this servicing schedule limits your statutory rights. Contact us if you need help understanding your service record, arranging a visit or checking what the routine service includes.

Common repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat include work on an unresponsive display, faulty controls, damaged connections and problems with temperature sensing. An engineer will assess the symptoms before recommending a repair. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so a description of the fault does not confirm which work is needed.

Contact Halvard Home to arrange a visit if the thermostat does not respond as expected or appears to control your heating incorrectly. Tell us what you can see on the display, what happens when you adjust the controls and whether anything has changed in your heating system or home network.

We may suggest checks that you can safely carry out before an engineer attends. These may include checking the thermostat settings and confirming that your home network is working. Follow the user instructions and do not remove covers, disconnect wiring or attempt repairs to electrical components yourself.

If you notice scorching, smoke, an unusual burning smell or exposed wiring, stop using the thermostat. Isolate the electrical supply only if you can do so safely. Do not touch damaged components or continue testing the controls. Seek emergency assistance if there is an immediate danger.

Diagnosing a fault on the Lumen smart thermostat costs £75.00 if no repair follows. The engineer will explain the findings and discuss the proposed work with you. If you choose to proceed, the quotation will explain how diagnosis is included in the repair price.

We will ask you to approve the quoted work before the repair begins. The quotation will describe the proposed repair and any parts required. If inspection reveals further work outside that agreement, the engineer will explain the change and seek your approval before proceeding with it.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the thermostat and any relevant heating controls safely. Clear nearby belongings and tell us about access restrictions when booking. Let us know if you need an adjustment to help you communicate with the engineer or understand the proposed work.

An engineer may find that the fault lies with your heating equipment, electrical installation or network rather than the thermostat. We will explain what the assessment shows and whether another suitably qualified professional is needed. We will not describe unrelated work as a repair to the thermostat.

Connection problems do not always require replacement parts. Where appropriate, the engineer may check settings, restore a connection or guide you through reconnecting the thermostat. You should enter passwords yourself rather than share them. Tell the engineer before any reset if you want to discuss settings that may be lost.

The Lumen smart thermostat has a filter that wears out with use. Replace the filter every 10 weeks. Follow the user instructions when replacing it, and use a compatible filter supplied or approved by Halvard Home. Contact us if the filter is damaged, stuck or difficult to access safely.

Routine filter replacement is maintenance rather than fault repair. If you report a problem that appears to involve the filter, we will explain whether maintenance or an engineer’s assessment is appropriate. Do not force the filter housing or continue using a visibly damaged filter while trying to resolve a fault.

Spare parts for the Lumen smart thermostat are stocked for 10 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for a particular visit depends on the part needed and local stock. If a part must be ordered, we will explain the arrangements and keep you informed about the repair.

Repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat are guaranteed for 140 days. This guarantee covers the repair work and replacement parts supplied as part of that work. Contact Halvard Home if the repaired fault returns, and keep your repair confirmation so we can identify the work carried out.

We will assess a reported problem to establish whether it relates to the repair. Damage caused by misuse, unauthorised alterations or faults elsewhere in the heating installation is not covered by the repair guarantee. We will explain our findings and any proposed charges before arranging work outside its scope.

After the repair, the engineer will check the thermostat’s operation and explain any changes made. Ask if you are unsure about the controls or care instructions. Keep the service record with your appliance documents. Nothing in this policy or the repair guarantee limits your statutory rights.

The Keel washing machine should be serviced every 32 months. This schedule is intended to help keep your appliance working safely and reliably. Arrange servicing through Halvard Home or an appropriately qualified appliance engineer, and keep a record of the work carried out so that it is available when you need advice or repairs.

Use the installation date as the starting point for your servicing schedule. After a routine service, use the date recorded by the engineer to plan your next appointment. If you do not know when your appliance was installed or last serviced, contact us for help reviewing the information available.

The recommended schedule does not replace the care and cleaning instructions supplied with your appliance. Continue to follow those instructions, including guidance on cleaning accessible parts and checking for visible damage. Do not remove protective panels, alter electrical connections or attempt work that the instructions reserve for a qualified engineer.

Arrange an assessment if the appliance develops an unusual noise, an unexpected smell, a leak or a change in washing performance. Do not wait for the scheduled service if you think something is wrong. A fault assessment may involve different work from a routine service, and we will explain the appropriate booking arrangements.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell or signs of an electrical fault, stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the electricity supply only if you can do so safely. If water is leaking, close the appliance’s water supply valve if it is safe and accessible, and contact us for advice.

A routine service of the Keel washing machine takes about 122 minutes. This is an estimate of the engineer’s working time, rather than a guaranteed appointment length. Access difficulties, the condition of the appliance or faults discovered during the visit may affect how the appointment proceeds. The engineer will explain any change to the planned work.

A routine service of the Keel washing machine costs £168.00. This price covers the routine service work described when you book. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside that scope require your agreement. If the engineer recommends additional work, we will explain what is needed and confirm the price before you decide whether to proceed.

When booking, tell us about any faults, warning messages or recent changes in performance. Mention any previous repairs or alterations that may be relevant. This helps us arrange suitable support and distinguish routine servicing from a repair visit. Have your appliance details and any available service records ready when you contact us.

Please also tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or anything that could affect the engineer’s ability to work safely. Let us know if the appliance is fitted into cabinetry or located where moving it may be difficult. We will discuss any preparation needed rather than expecting you to move it yourself.

Before the appointment, empty the drum and leave the area around the appliance clear. Make sure the engineer can reach the controls, door and accessible connections. Keep children and pets away from the working area. Do not disconnect or move the appliance unless we have specifically asked you to do so.

During the service, the engineer will assess the appliance’s condition and carry out the checks appropriate to its design. These may include inspecting accessible hoses, seals and connections, checking operation and looking for signs of wear or leakage. The engineer will explain any limits on what can be inspected safely.

A routine service is not a guarantee that faults will not develop. Some components cannot be fully assessed without further investigation, and wear may not always be visible. If the engineer finds a concern, they will explain its significance and advise whether the appliance can remain in use or should be left switched off.

After the visit, keep the service record with your appliance documents. It should describe the work completed, any concerns identified and any recommended follow-up action. Contact us if anything in the record is unclear or does not match your understanding of the visit. We can help clarify the engineer’s advice.

If you need to change or cancel your booking, contact us promptly using the details in your confirmation. We will explain the options available and any applicable booking terms. Servicing arrangements do not limit your statutory rights, and you can contact us separately about a fault, a guarantee claim or a concern about the service received.

Common repairs to the Keel washing machine include clearing drainage faults, replacing worn door seals, repairing door locks and replacing faulty pumps, valves or controls. Our engineer will assess the fault before recommending work. A reported symptom does not always mean that a particular part needs replacing.

Before booking a visit, check that the power supply is working, the water supply is turned on and the drain hose is not visibly trapped. Follow the checks in your user guide. Do not remove panels, disturb wiring or attempt repairs to internal components.

Stop using the machine if it leaks, smells of burning, gives an electric shock or makes an unusual grinding sound. Disconnect it from the power supply if you can do so safely. If water is near the socket, do not touch the plug or socket.

When you contact us, describe what happens and whether the machine can drain or release the door. Tell us about any visible damage or recent changes to its plumbing or electrical connection. This helps us prepare, but the engineer must still inspect the machine.

Diagnosing a fault on the Keel washing machine costs £38.00 if no repair follows. We will explain whether this charge applies when you book, including where you choose not to proceed with a quoted repair. Any applicable warranty rights or statutory rights remain unaffected.

The engineer will explain the proposed repair and provide a quote before starting chargeable work. The quote will identify the work and parts included. We will ask for your agreement if the findings change what is needed. You may decline the revised work.

Drainage problems may be caused by trapped objects, a blocked filter or a faulty pump. The engineer will check the likely cause rather than replace the pump without inspection. Removing an obstruction may resolve the fault, although damage caused by the obstruction may also need repair.

Replace the filter every 25 weeks. Use a compatible replacement and follow the user guide for safe access and fitting. Switch off and unplug the machine before opening the filter cover. Take care when releasing trapped water, which may be hot, and protect the surrounding floor.

Leaks may come from a damaged door seal, a loose connection or an internal component. The engineer will identify the source where it can be safely accessed. Repairs to household pipework, taps or drainage outside the machine are not included unless expressly agreed in your quote.

A door that will not open may indicate retained water or a fault with the locking mechanism. Do not force the handle or try to bypass the lock. The engineer will make the machine safe before releasing the door and checking whether replacement parts are needed.

Unusual noise or movement may result from an uneven installation, trapped objects or worn components. We may recommend an installation adjustment rather than a component repair. If the cause lies with the floor or surrounding furniture, you will need to arrange suitable remedial work.

Faults affecting filling, heating or programme selection require checks to establish the cause. Similar symptoms can arise from different components. The engineer will only recommend replacing a control assembly where the assessment supports that repair, and will explain any limits on the diagnosis.

Spare parts for the Keel washing machine are stocked for 18 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for your visit depends on the part required and local stock. If a part must be ordered, we will explain how this affects the proposed repair arrangements.

Please provide clear access to the machine and keep pets away from the work area. Tell us about restricted access, damaged flooring or an installation behind fixed fittings. The engineer may decline work where access is unsafe or would risk damage to your home.

After the repair, the engineer will check the work and explain what has been done. Testing may require access to water, drainage and electricity. If safe testing is not possible, we will explain the limitation and tell you whether the machine should remain unused.

We will provide a record of the repair and explain any care advice relevant to the fault. Contact us if the symptoms return or you believe the repair has not resolved the problem. Keep the repair record available so we can review the work and advise on the appropriate next step.

Routine servicing helps keep your Ashby tumble dryer working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to identify wear, damage or faults that may need attention. Follow the servicing schedule recorded for your appliance, alongside the care instructions supplied with it. A service does not replace the cleaning and checks you are asked to carry out yourself.

Your service due date is recorded when your appliance is registered with Halvard Home. You can check this date through your customer account or ask our customer care team to confirm it. If you cannot find a servicing record, contact us rather than guessing whether your appliance is due for attention.

Owners of the Ashby tumble dryer are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 3 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held on your account, so please tell us if these change. You should still follow your recorded schedule if a reminder does not reach you.

A reminder is an invitation to arrange a visit, not confirmation that an appointment has been booked. Contact Halvard Home through the booking details provided with your reminder or through your customer account. We will confirm the appointment arrangements and explain anything you need to do before the engineer arrives.

If your use of the Ashby tumble dryer changes, ask us whether its servicing schedule remains suitable. Tell us about unusually heavy use, changes to where the appliance is installed, or conditions that could affect ventilation. Our advice will take account of the appliance’s condition, its installation and the information you provide.

A routine service of the Ashby tumble dryer takes about 62 minutes. This is a guide rather than a guarantee that the visit will be completed as expected. Access difficulties, the condition of the appliance or a fault discovered during inspection may affect the work. The engineer will explain if the planned service cannot be completed.

A routine service of the Ashby tumble dryer costs £98.00. We will explain what the routine service covers when you book. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside that scope require your agreement. The engineer will describe any recommended work and explain the proposed charges before asking you to approve it.

Before the visit, empty the drum and remove items stored on or around the appliance. Clear a safe route to it and make sure the engineer can reach the plug and relevant connections. Do not pull out a fitted appliance or disconnect anything if doing so would be unsafe.

Please tell us when booking about restricted access, parking arrangements, stairs or anything else that could affect the visit. Let us know if you need communication support or an adjustment to the appointment arrangements. We will discuss what is practical and confirm any agreed arrangements with you.

An adult authorised to agree to the work must be present to let the engineer in and discuss the appliance. Keep children and pets away from the work area. The engineer may decline to start or continue work if access is unsafe or the surroundings prevent the service from being carried out properly.

During a routine service, the engineer checks the appliance’s condition and operation within the agreed scope. They will discuss relevant findings with you, including signs of wear or issues that need further investigation. Servicing cannot guarantee that a fault will not develop, and it does not make a damaged appliance safe by itself.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if the Ashby tumble dryer appears unsafe. Stop using it if you notice smoke, a burning smell, overheating or damage to the electrical connection. Disconnect it if you can do so safely, and contact Halvard Home for advice about the appropriate next step.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact us using your booking details. We will explain the available arrangements and any applicable cancellation terms before you confirm a change. If we need to rearrange the visit, we will contact you using the details supplied for the booking.

After the service, keep the service record with your appliance documents. It should explain the work completed, any recommendations and the service due date. If a service has been missed, contact us to arrange suitable attention rather than treating the schedule as cancelled. Continue to follow the appliance’s care and safety instructions.

Common repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer include faults with heating, drum movement, controls, door catches and moisture detection. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so an engineer will check the appliance before recommending work. We will explain the findings in plain language and tell you whether a repair is suitable.

Before requesting a visit, check that the appliance is connected to the power supply and that the door closes properly. Follow the user guide when checking accessible filters or emptying the water container, where fitted. Do not remove panels, reach inside the casing or attempt to repair electrical components yourself.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, sparks or unusual heat, stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the electricity supply if it is safe to do so, and do not use it again until it has been assessed. If there is an immediate danger, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

When you contact Halvard Home, describe what happens when you try to use the dryer. Tell us about unusual sounds, interrupted programmes, damp laundry or visible damage. Please also mention any previous repair affecting the fault. This helps us arrange appropriate support, although the engineer may still need to inspect the appliance.

Diagnosing a fault on the Ashby tumble dryer costs £41.00 if no repair follows. We will explain how this charge applies before you agree to a visit. If the fault may be covered by a guarantee or your legal rights, tell us when booking so that we can check the appropriate route.

The engineer will assess the fault and explain the proposed repair, including the parts and labour involved. You will be told the total repair price before work begins. We will not carry out chargeable repair work without your agreement. If further work becomes necessary, we will seek your approval.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely. Remove laundry from the drum and clear belongings from the surrounding area. Tell us in advance if the dryer is built into furniture, stacked, difficult to move or located where access is restricted. We can then discuss any arrangements needed.

Poor drying can be caused by restricted airflow, unsuitable programme settings or a fault with the heating or sensing components. The engineer will check the likely cause rather than assume that a part needs replacing. Where cleaning or a change in use resolves the problem, we will explain what to do.

Replace the filter of the Ashby tumble dryer every 8 weeks. Follow the user guide for cleaning and fitting instructions, and use a filter approved for this model. A damaged or incorrectly fitted filter can affect airflow and performance. Do not operate the dryer with the filter missing.

If the drum does not turn, the engineer may need to inspect the drive components, motor or controls. Noise may also come from loose objects, worn supports or an installation problem. Stop using the appliance if it makes a scraping or grinding sound, rather than trying to force the drum to move.

Door and control faults can prevent a programme from starting or cause it to stop unexpectedly. Do not bypass the door catch or interfere with safety switches. The engineer will check the affected components and confirm whether adjustment or replacement is needed to restore safe operation.

Spare parts for the Ashby tumble dryer are stocked for 13 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for a particular visit still depends on the part required and current stock. If a part must be ordered, we will explain the next steps and arrange further work with you.

If a repair is not practical, or the appliance cannot be made safe through the proposed work, the engineer will explain why. We will not present a repair as suitable when it would leave a known safety concern unresolved. You can decline the proposed repair after receiving the assessment.

Paid repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer come with their own guarantee. Repairs are guaranteed for 105 days. Keep your repair confirmation and contact us if the repaired fault returns. We will review the work recorded and explain how the repair guarantee applies. It does not affect your statutory rights.

After completing the work, the engineer will check the repaired function and explain any care advice relevant to the fault. Tell us if anything remains unclear before using the appliance. If the same symptoms return, stop using it where safety may be affected and contact Halvard Home for guidance.

The Vale fridge freezer should be serviced every 8 months. Regular servicing helps keep the appliance working as intended and gives the engineer an opportunity to identify wear, damage or changes in performance that may need attention.

Your servicing schedule starts from the delivery date recorded by Halvard Home. After a routine service has been completed, the date of that visit becomes the reference point for your next service. Keep your delivery details and service records somewhere you can find them easily.

If you do not know when your Vale fridge freezer was delivered or last serviced, contact Halvard Home. We can check the records available to us and help you agree a suitable service date. Please do not guess or leave a known service need unresolved.

A reminder is sent 9 weeks before a service is due. It uses the contact details held on your customer record, so please tell us if those details change. You remain responsible for arranging your service if a reminder does not reach you.

The reminder is an invitation to book, not confirmation of an engineer visit. Contact Halvard Home through the booking method shown in your reminder or on our website. We will confirm the appointment details with you before the visit is treated as booked.

When booking, explain any concerns about cooling, unusual sounds, leaks, frost or door seals. Tell us whether the appliance is displaying a warning or behaving differently from normal. This helps us understand whether a routine service is appropriate or a repair assessment is needed.

A routine service of the Vale fridge freezer takes about 154 minutes. This is a guide rather than a promise about the engineer’s departure. Access difficulties, the condition of the appliance or a fault found during the visit may affect how the work proceeds.

A routine service of the Vale fridge freezer costs £177.00. The routine service charge does not cover repairs or replacement parts outside the agreed service work. If the engineer identifies work that would carry an additional charge, we will explain it and ask for your agreement before proceeding.

The routine service includes checking the appliance’s general condition, accessible seals, controls and cooling performance. The engineer will also look for signs of damage or wear and discuss any relevant care advice. Servicing cannot guarantee that a fault will not develop afterwards.

Please arrange for a responsible adult to be present who can let the engineer in, discuss the appliance and approve the agreed work. Tell us when booking if you need communication support or have an access requirement so we can discuss suitable arrangements.

Make sure the route to the appliance is clear and that the engineer can work safely around it. Keep pets away from the working area and move fragile belongings out of reach. Please tell us about stairs, restricted parking or other access difficulties.

Do not disconnect, defrost or move the appliance unless Halvard Home asks you to do so. The engineer may need to assess it while it is operating. We will explain any preparation needed for your visit when confirming the booking.

Keep food stored safely while the service is carried out. If access to a compartment is needed, the engineer will explain what should be removed. Let us know about any concern that could make preparing the appliance difficult, rather than attempting an unsafe move or lift.

If you cannot attend the agreed appointment, contact Halvard Home to rearrange it. Do not assume that replying to an automated reminder will cancel a booking. Your appointment remains in place until we have confirmed the change.

If an engineer cannot safely reach or work on the appliance, the service may need to be rearranged. We will explain the obstacle and discuss what needs to change. The engineer will not ask you to carry out work that puts you at risk.

After the visit, keep the service report with your appliance records. It should describe the work completed, any concerns identified and the recommended next steps. Contact Halvard Home if anything in the report is unclear or does not match your understanding of the visit.

Do not wait for scheduled servicing if you suspect a fault or safety problem. Stop using the appliance if it appears unsafe and contact Halvard Home for advice. Servicing is not a substitute for reporting a problem, following the user instructions or arranging a necessary repair.

Common repairs to the Vale fridge freezer include replacing worn door seals, clearing drainage faults, repairing cooling components and dealing with unusual noise. An engineer will check the appliance before recommending work. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so a description of the problem cannot confirm which repair is needed.

Before booking a visit, check that the appliance is connected to the electricity supply and that its controls have not been changed accidentally. Make sure food packaging is not preventing the doors from closing. Keep internal air vents clear, but do not remove covers or attempt to reach concealed components.

If the appliance is not cooling properly, keep the doors closed where practical and move food somewhere suitable if you are concerned about its condition. Follow the storage advice on food packaging. The engineer can assess the appliance, but cannot confirm whether food affected by a cooling fault remains safe to eat.

Stop using the appliance if you notice smoke, a burning smell, sparks or damage to its electrical connection. Disconnect it only if you can do so safely. Do not touch a wet plug or socket. Tell us about any suspected electrical hazard when arranging the visit.

When you contact Halvard Home, describe the fault and explain whether it is constant or comes and goes. Mention any leaks, unusual sounds or changes in cooling. We may ask for a photograph of the appliance label so that we can identify the correct parts without asking you to dismantle anything.

Diagnosing a fault on the Vale fridge freezer costs £31.00 if no repair follows. We will explain any applicable charges before you agree to the visit. After inspecting the appliance, the engineer will describe the fault, recommend suitable work and explain the repair price before asking for your approval.

You do not have to accept a proposed repair. If you decide not to proceed, the engineer will explain whether the appliance can safely remain in use. Where a fault makes continued use unsafe, we will advise you to leave it disconnected until the problem has been resolved.

Door seal problems can allow warm air into the appliance and affect cooling. The engineer will check whether the seal is dirty, damaged or incorrectly seated, and whether the door is aligned properly. A replacement seal may be recommended where cleaning or adjustment would not restore a reliable closure.

Water collecting inside or beneath the appliance may be caused by a blocked drain, an incorrectly fitted filter or a damaged connection. Keep the surrounding floor dry where safe to do so. Do not use sharp objects to clear a blockage, as this could damage concealed parts.

Replace the filter of the Vale fridge freezer every 19 weeks. Use a compatible filter and follow the fitting instructions supplied with it. If you are unsure which filter is suitable, contact us before ordering. A leak following replacement should be checked rather than concealed or left to continue.

Unusual sounds do not always mean a component has failed. The engineer may check the appliance’s position, surrounding clearances and accessible fittings before considering a mechanical repair. Tell us whether the sound changes when a door is opened, but do not move a heavy appliance if doing so would be unsafe.

Cooling faults may involve sensors, fans, controls or sealed components. Work on electrical connections and the sealed cooling system must be left to a suitably qualified engineer. Do not puncture pipework, apply direct heat to remove ice or use an improvised electrical connection to keep the appliance running.

Please provide safe access to the appliance and keep the working area clear of loose items. Let us know about access difficulties when booking. If the appliance is built into cabinetry, explain this beforehand so we can discuss any preparation needed without risking damage to your home.

Spare parts for the Vale fridge freezer are stocked for 14 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for a particular repair will be checked when the fault has been identified. If a required part cannot be supplied for your appointment, we will explain the position and discuss the available options.

Repairs are guaranteed for 297 days. The guarantee covers faults arising from the repair work or a replacement part supplied as part of that work. Contact us if the repaired fault returns. We will assess the problem and explain whether it falls within the repair guarantee.

The repair guarantee does not replace your statutory rights. Keep your repair confirmation, as it records the work authorised and completed. Before leaving, the engineer will explain any relevant operating advice, describe any unresolved issue and tell you how to contact Halvard Home if you have concerns about the repair.

The Corra induction hob should be serviced every 16 months. This schedule helps keep the appliance working safely and gives an engineer the opportunity to check its condition. Servicing supports the care described in your user guide, but does not replace cleaning or attention to faults.

Use the installation date as the starting point for your servicing schedule. After a service, use the date recorded by the engineer to plan the next appointment. Keep the service record somewhere accessible so that you can refer to it when arranging another visit.

If you do not know when your hob was installed or last serviced, contact Halvard Home for advice. We may ask for installation paperwork or an existing service record. Where the service history is unclear, we can help you arrange an appropriate appointment.

Please arrange servicing through Halvard Home or an engineer authorised by us to service the Corra induction hob. Tell us that you are booking a routine service, rather than a repair, so that we can make suitable arrangements and explain what the visit will cover.

Let us know about any faults when you book. These may include unusual noises, unexpected switching off, cracked glass or controls that do not respond as expected. A routine service is not a substitute for investigating a fault, and a repair may need separate arrangements.

A routine service of the Corra induction hob takes about 120 minutes. The engineer will need clear access to the hob, its electrical isolation switch and any relevant cupboard space beneath it. Please tell us about access restrictions when arranging the appointment.

A routine service of the Corra induction hob costs £210.00. We will explain the payment arrangements when you book. If the engineer identifies work outside the routine service, they will explain what is needed and confirm any additional charges before asking you to approve that work.

Routine servicing includes checks of the hob’s visible condition, controls and operation, together with relevant electrical safety checks. The engineer will look for signs of damage or wear and discuss anything that could affect safe use. Checks will follow the servicing guidance for your appliance.

Please remove cookware and other belongings from the hob and surrounding worktop before the engineer arrives. Leave the cooking surface clean and cool. Do not remove the hob from the worktop, disconnect its wiring or take off protective covers in preparation for the visit.

Make sure someone able to discuss the appliance and authorise any proposed work is available for the appointment. Keep children and pets away from the engineer’s working area. If you need adjustments to help you communicate or manage access, please tell us when booking.

The engineer may need to isolate the electrical supply while carrying out checks. They will explain what they need to do and let you know when the hob can be used again. Please do not operate the appliance while servicing is in progress.

If the engineer finds a fault, they will explain their findings in plain language. They may recommend a repair, replacement parts or further investigation. You can ask questions before deciding whether to approve work that is not included in the routine service.

Where a fault makes the hob unsafe, the engineer will explain why it must not be used and what needs to happen next. They may leave the appliance isolated from the electrical supply. Do not reconnect or use it until it has been made safe.

After the visit, keep the service record with your appliance documents. It should describe the checks completed, any concerns identified and any work recommended. If you believe the record is incomplete or does not reflect what was discussed, contact Halvard Home for clarification.

If you need to change your appointment, contact us using the details in your booking confirmation. We will help you rearrange the visit and explain any applicable booking conditions. If access cannot be provided, the engineer may be unable to complete the service.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if you notice damage or suspect an electrical fault. Stop using the hob and seek advice from Halvard Home. If you can safely isolate the electrical supply, do so without touching damaged areas or attempting to repair the appliance yourself.

Common repairs to the Corra induction hob include replacing damaged controls, heating components, cooling fans and electrical connections. Our engineer will inspect the appliance to identify the fault and explain the recommended work. A reported symptom does not always mean that a part needs replacing.

Before arranging a visit, check that your cookware is suitable for induction cooking and that the hob is not locked. Follow the checks in your user instructions. Do not remove covers, attempt electrical repairs or continue testing the appliance if you notice damage, smoke or a burning smell.

If the glass surface is cracked, stop using the hob and isolate it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely. Do not use an unaffected cooking area while waiting for advice. Damage to the glass can make the appliance unsafe even when the controls appear to work normally.

Tell us what happens when you try to use the hob, including whether the problem affects heating, touch controls or ventilation. Please describe any message shown on the display without trying to interpret it. Photographs may help us assess visible damage, but they cannot replace an engineer’s inspection.

Diagnosing a fault on the Corra induction hob costs £80.00 if no repair follows. We will explain the applicable charges when you book and confirm the proposed repair price after diagnosis. The engineer will ask for your agreement before starting chargeable repair work. You may decline the repair.

Problems with heating may be caused by unsuitable cookware, an electrical supply issue or a faulty internal component. The engineer will check the cause before recommending replacement parts. Work on your household wiring or electricity supply is not included in an appliance repair and may need a qualified electrician.

Unresponsive controls can result from moisture, residue, damage or a fault within the control assembly. Clean and dry the surface only as described in your user instructions. If the problem remains, leave internal checks to the engineer. Forcing the controls or applying cleaning liquid around damaged areas may worsen the fault.

A damaged glass surface will normally need replacement rather than a cosmetic repair. The engineer will also inspect the supporting components for damage. We will explain whether the appliance can be repaired safely and whether the condition of the surrounding worktop affects the proposed work.

Cooling fan faults and blocked ventilation can interfere with normal operation. Keep ventilation openings clear and avoid storing items where they could obstruct airflow. The engineer may need access beneath the hob to inspect these areas. Please remove loose belongings from the relevant cupboard before the visit.

Where an extraction filter is fitted, follow the cleaning and fitting instructions supplied with it. Replace the filter every 24 weeks. A clogged or incorrectly fitted filter can affect extraction performance. Do not wash a filter unless the user instructions state that it is washable.

Our engineer will use parts approved for the Corra induction hob. Spare parts for the Corra induction hob are stocked for 5 years after the model is discontinued. Availability of a particular component may still affect when a repair can be arranged. We will discuss any supply problem with you.

Please make sure the hob can be reached safely and that the area around it is clear. Tell us about restricted access, fixed panels or installation changes when booking. If safe access requires alterations to cabinetry or the worktop, we will explain what must be arranged before repair work can proceed.

Repairs are guaranteed for 150 days. This guarantee covers the work carried out and the parts fitted as part of that repair. It does not cover unrelated faults, accidental damage, misuse or problems caused by unauthorised alterations. Your statutory rights are not affected.

If the repaired fault returns, contact us and describe the symptoms. Keep your repair paperwork available so we can review the work completed. We will assess whether the issue falls within the repair guarantee and explain any proposed charge before you agree to further work.

After completing the repair, the engineer will carry out the relevant safety and operating checks and explain any care instructions. If the hob cannot be left safe to use, the engineer will tell you why and advise you not to reconnect it. Where repair is unsuitable, we will explain the findings and discuss the options available.

The Fenwick cooker hood should be serviced every 38 months.

This schedule is intended to support the safe and reliable operation of your Fenwick cooker hood. Servicing helps an engineer assess its condition, check that its functions are working correctly and identify concerns that may need attention. It does not replace the care described in your user instructions.

Your service due date is based on the installation date recorded by Halvard Home or the date of the recorded service, as applicable. Please contact us if the date shown in your account appears incorrect or if you cannot find your service record.

If you have moved into a home where a Fenwick cooker hood is already installed, please ask us to check its recorded service history. We may ask for evidence of installation or servicing so that we can confirm the appropriate due date.

A reminder is sent 5 weeks before the Fenwick cooker hood is due for a service.

We use the contact details held on your customer record to send this reminder. Please keep those details up to date and tell us if responsibility for arranging the service has changed. A reminder does not mean that an engineer visit has been booked.

You remain responsible for arranging the service if a reminder does not reach you. If you believe your Fenwick cooker hood is due for servicing, contact Halvard Home rather than waiting for a message. We can check the record and explain how to request an appointment.

Appointments are subject to engineer availability in your area. We will confirm the agreed visit arrangements when your booking is accepted. Please check that the address, contact details and access information are correct, and tell us about anything that could prevent the engineer from entering safely.

Tell us when booking if the Fenwick cooker hood has developed a fault, is making an unusual sound or is not extracting as expected. A routine service may not resolve a reported fault, and the engineer may need to assess whether a repair is required.

Do not wait for the scheduled service if you notice smoke, a burning smell, visible damage or behaviour that suggests the Fenwick cooker hood may be unsafe. Stop using it and seek advice. If it is safe to do so, disconnect it from the electricity supply.

Before the visit, please make the area around the Fenwick cooker hood accessible and remove belongings that could obstruct the engineer. Let us know about restricted access, fragile surfaces or alterations to the installation. Do not dismantle the hood or remove fixed electrical fittings yourself.

The engineer will assess the Fenwick cooker hood in line with the applicable servicing instructions. The work may include examining accessible components, checking operation and looking for signs of wear or damage. The engineer will explain if the installation or condition prevents servicing from being completed safely.

If the engineer identifies work outside the agreed service, they will explain what is needed and how it can be arranged. Charges will be explained before you are asked to agree to chargeable work. A service booking does not authorise repairs beyond the agreed scope.

After the visit, you will receive a record explaining the service outcome and recommendations. Please keep this with your appliance documents. If work could not be completed, the record will explain the reason and the action needed before servicing can be completed.

An incomplete visit does not automatically change the service due date. Halvard Home will confirm how the service record has been updated and whether a further appointment is needed. Please contact us if the record does not match your understanding of the engineer’s advice.

Continue to follow the cleaning and filter care instructions supplied with your Fenwick cooker hood. These tasks are separate from the servicing schedule. Do not use the service reminder as a reason to delay cleaning or attention to a filter that needs care.

If you cannot keep an appointment, contact us to rearrange it. We will explain the booking conditions that apply. If servicing is overdue, arrange a visit and tell us about concerns with the hood’s condition rather than assuming that it remains safe to use.

Servicing does not replace your rights under consumer law. Warranty cover and service charges are governed by the terms that apply to your purchase or booking. If you are unsure how those terms affect your service, ask Halvard Home for clarification before confirming the appointment.

Common repairs to the Fenwick cooker hood include faults affecting extraction, lighting, controls and the fan motor. Halvard Home will assess the reported fault and explain whether an engineer visit is appropriate. We may suggest checks that you can safely carry out yourself, but we will not ask you to dismantle the appliance or handle electrical connections.

Stop using the cooker hood if you notice smoke, sparks, a burning smell or damage to the electrical cable. Switch it off and isolate it from the electricity supply if you can do so safely. Do not touch exposed wiring or attempt to investigate an electrical fault. Contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment.

Poor extraction can be caused by a blocked filter, an obstructed outlet or a fault within the fan assembly. With the appliance isolated, you may check accessible surfaces for grease and look for visible obstructions without removing fixed covers. Do not insert tools into the fan or ducting. Leave inaccessible areas for the engineer to inspect.

Replace the filter every 14 weeks. Use a filter approved for the Fenwick cooker hood and follow the fitting instructions supplied with it. An unsuitable or incorrectly fitted filter can affect extraction and may prevent the cover from closing securely. If the filter housing is damaged or the filter will not sit correctly, contact Halvard Home.

Rattling, scraping or unusual vibration may indicate a loose fitting, damaged fan component or obstruction. Do not continue running the appliance to identify where the noise comes from. Tell us what you heard and whether the noise occurred with extraction, lighting or a control change. This information helps the engineer assess the likely repair.

If the light fails but extraction still works, the fault may lie with the light assembly, its connection or the control system. Only replace a user-accessible light component where the appliance instructions expressly allow this. Isolate the electricity supply before following those instructions. Do not remove fixed panels to reach lighting connections.

Controls that stick, fail to respond or behave unexpectedly should be reported to Halvard Home. You may wipe the accessible control surface with a soft cloth using the cleaning method described in the appliance instructions. Do not spray cleaning liquid into switches or openings, and do not force a button or control that appears damaged.

Repairs involving the motor, internal wiring or electrical controls must be carried out by a suitably qualified engineer. The engineer will inspect the fault and determine whether a component can be repaired or needs replacement. They may decline to operate the appliance if its condition or installation makes testing unsafe.

When requesting a visit, describe the symptoms and tell us about visible damage, unusual smells or previous repair work. Explain whether the appliance is connected to ducting or uses a recirculating arrangement, if you know. You do not need to remove the cooker hood or open its casing to provide this information.

Make the area around the cooker hood accessible for the visit. Clear the cooking surface and nearby worktop, and make sure the engineer can reach the electricity isolation point. Tell us about access difficulties or building restrictions when booking. Do not move the appliance or alter its installation in preparation for the engineer.

The engineer will explain the proposed work and any applicable charges before seeking your agreement to proceed. Warranty cover depends on the terms supplied with your appliance and the cause of the fault. Damage caused by misuse, unsuitable cleaning products or unauthorised alterations may fall outside that cover. We will explain the reason for any charge.

Spare parts for the Fenwick cooker hood are stocked for 8 years after the model is discontinued.

The engineer will use suitable replacement components and check that the repaired functions operate safely. If a required part is unavailable, Halvard Home will explain the available options rather than fit an unsuitable substitute. We will seek your agreement before changing the proposed repair or proceeding with work outside the agreed scope.

A fault caused by ducting, cabinetry or the household electrical installation may need attention from an appropriate tradesperson rather than an appliance repair. The engineer will explain what they have found and identify anything that prevents safe use. Do not use the cooker hood where the engineer has advised that it must remain isolated.

Routine servicing helps keep your Mira robot vacuum working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults that may not be obvious during use. Servicing supports the care described in your user instructions; it does not replace cleaning, emptying the dust container or removing trapped hair and debris.

Your servicing schedule is based on the condition and use of your Mira robot vacuum, together with any advice recorded by a Halvard Home engineer. We will explain when a service is due when your schedule is agreed. If your circumstances change, contact us so we can review whether that schedule remains suitable.

A reminder is sent 7 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held on your service record, so please tell us if those details change. The reminder invites you to arrange a visit; it does not reserve an appointment or give us permission to enter your home.

You remain responsible for arranging the service, even if a reminder does not reach you. If you are unsure whether your Mira robot vacuum is due for servicing, contact Halvard Home. We can check the available service history and explain the next step without asking you to guess from how the appliance looks or sounds.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum takes about 164 minutes. This is an estimate for the service work, not a guaranteed appointment length. Access difficulties, the condition of the appliance or a fault requiring investigation may affect the visit. Your engineer will explain any change to the planned work.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum costs £115.00. We will confirm what the routine service includes when you book. Repairs, replacement parts or work outside that scope are not automatically authorised by your booking. We will explain any proposed additional charges and seek your agreement before proceeding with chargeable work.

When booking, tell us about changes in performance, unusual noises, charging problems, visible damage or warning messages. Describe what happens and the circumstances in which it occurs. This helps us decide whether a routine service is appropriate or whether your Mira robot vacuum needs a fault assessment instead.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if you suspect that your Mira robot vacuum is unsafe. Stop using it if there is smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or damage that could expose electrical parts. Follow the safety instructions supplied with the appliance and contact Halvard Home for advice.

Before the visit, make sure the engineer can reach the Mira robot vacuum and its charging area safely. Clear loose items from the working area and keep pets away while work is being carried out. Tell us about access restrictions or support needs when arranging the appointment so we can discuss suitable arrangements.

Please have the Mira robot vacuum available with the accessories relevant to any problem you have reported. Do not dismantle it or attempt to expose internal parts for the engineer. If it cannot be moved safely, leave it in place and explain the situation when we confirm the visit.

During a routine service, the engineer checks the accessible working parts, looks for signs of wear and assesses operation where it is safe to do so. The work may include cleaning serviceable areas and checking that components are seated correctly. The engineer will explain anything that prevents a normal service from being completed.

A service is not a promise that faults will never develop. Some problems only appear under particular operating conditions, and servicing cannot undo damage or restore worn parts without suitable remedial work. If the engineer identifies a concern, they will explain what they have found and discuss the available options with you.

After the visit, we will provide a record of the work completed and any recommendations. Keep this with your appliance information. We will also confirm whether the servicing schedule should stay as agreed or be reviewed because of the condition of your Mira robot vacuum or the way it is used.

If you need to change or cancel a service appointment, contact Halvard Home rather than waiting for the engineer to arrive. We will explain the applicable booking terms and help you arrange a suitable alternative where possible. Tell us if you no longer own the Mira robot vacuum so we can update the service record and stop sending servicing reminders.

Common repairs to the Mira robot vacuum include clearing blocked suction paths, replacing worn brushes, repairing wheel assemblies and dealing with charging faults. Our support team will help identify the problem and explain whether it can be resolved at home or needs an engineer.

If the appliance stops unexpectedly, makes an unusual noise or leaves dirt behind, switch it off before inspecting it. Disconnect the charging dock from the mains before cleaning around its contacts. Do not reach into moving parts or open sealed covers.

Check accessible areas for trapped hair, thread and debris, following the cleaning instructions supplied with the appliance. A blocked brush or suction inlet can affect cleaning without indicating a mechanical fault. Stop if removing an obstruction would require force or dismantling.

Replace the filter of the Mira robot vacuum every 13 weeks. Use a compatible filter approved for the appliance, and fit it as described in the care instructions. An incorrectly fitted or damaged filter can reduce suction and allow dust into internal components.

Brushes can become tangled, bent or worn through normal use. If cleaning does not restore their movement, contact us for advice about replacement. Do not trim damaged bristles or alter the brush housing, as this may affect cleaning and safe operation.

Wheel problems may cause the appliance to drag, turn unexpectedly or struggle to move. Remove visible debris from accessible wheel areas without pulling on the wheel assembly. If a wheel remains stiff, loose or damaged, leave the appliance switched off and arrange support.

Charging problems can arise from dirty contacts, a damaged cable or a fault inside the appliance or dock. Check that the socket is working and that the dock is connected securely. Do not use a cable, plug or dock that appears damaged.

If the appliance becomes unusually hot, smells of burning, leaks or shows signs of battery swelling, stop using and charging it. Disconnect it from the mains if safe to do so. Contact us for safe handling advice before moving or sending it.

Navigation faults may be caused by dirty sensors, obstructed movement or a changed room layout. Clean exposed sensors using the method in the care instructions. If the appliance continues to behave unexpectedly, our support team can advise whether an engineer should inspect it.

When requesting a repair, describe the fault and explain what happened before it appeared. Tell us about damage, liquid exposure or attempted repairs. We may ask for photographs or proof of purchase to help assess the appliance and confirm the applicable cover.

We will explain the proposed repair route before making arrangements. Depending on the fault, this may involve an engineer visit or sending the appliance to a service centre. Please do not send it until you have received packing and delivery instructions from us.

Before an engineer visit, make the appliance and charging dock accessible and clear the surrounding floor. Keep pets away from the work area. Tell us about access restrictions or anything that could make the visit unsafe, so we can discuss suitable arrangements.

The engineer will inspect the appliance and explain the work needed. If the fault differs from the reported problem, we will discuss the revised repair with you. Work that carries a charge will not proceed without your agreement to the quoted price.

Repair cover depends on the applicable guarantee and your statutory rights. Damage caused by misuse, accidental impact or unsuitable cleaning may fall outside the guarantee. We will explain the reason if we decide that a repair is chargeable, rather than assuming your agreement.

Repairs to the Mira robot vacuum are guaranteed for 223 days. This covers faults in the repair work and parts fitted during that repair. If the repaired fault returns, contact us with your service record. This guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Halvard Home keeps spare parts for the Mira robot vacuum after it stops being sold. Spare parts are stocked for 6 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for a particular repair will be checked when we assess the fault and arrange the work.

After the repair, the engineer or service centre will check that the appliance operates safely and that the reported fault has been addressed. Follow the care advice provided with your service record. Contact us if the appliance still appears faulty, and stop using it if you have concerns about safety.

Routine servicing under Extended Care helps keep your appliance in good working order. It is intended to check its condition, support safe operation and identify concerns that may need attention. It does not replace the care described in your appliance instructions.

Extended Care members get 63% off routine services. The discount applies to the standard routine service charge for an appliance covered by your active plan. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are not included in that discount unless we expressly confirm otherwise.

When you request a service, we will check your membership and confirm whether the appliance is covered. Please have your membership details and the appliance information available so that we can find the correct record and arrange suitable support.

We will explain the service charge before you agree to a booking. If your request includes work outside the plan, we will explain the proposed charges separately. You do not have to accept additional work to proceed with an eligible routine service.

Extended Care members are offered a visit within 2 working days. This commitment concerns the offer of a visit, rather than completion of servicing or any repair. We will discuss the appointment arrangements with you and confirm what the booking covers.

Tell us when booking if the appliance has a fault, displays a warning or appears unsafe. A routine service may not be the right appointment for a reported fault. We will explain whether a repair assessment or another form of support is more appropriate.

If you notice smoke, a burning smell, leaking water near electrical connections or another immediate hazard, stop using the appliance if you can do so safely. Follow the safety advice in its instructions and contact the appropriate emergency service where necessary.
