Before the engineer arrives, make sure the appliance can be reached safely. Clear the surrounding area and keep pets away from the work space. Please tell us about access restrictions, parking arrangements or building rules that could affect the visit.

Let us know if you need adjustments to help you use our service. We will discuss your needs respectfully and explain what we can arrange. You can also nominate someone to help with the booking or speak with the engineer with your permission.

A responsible adult must be present to provide access and discuss the service. They should be able to authorise any agreed work and understand the engineer’s advice. Please tell us if the person attending will not be the plan holder.

The engineer will check the appliance using the servicing procedure appropriate to its design and condition. The work may include inspection, cleaning accessible service areas and operational checks. We will explain any preparation that you need to carry out yourself.

Routine servicing does not include alterations to your home, changes to fixed connections or work on unrelated equipment. If safe access requires specialist assistance, we will explain the issue and discuss how the service can proceed.

The engineer may stop or decline work if conditions are unsafe, the appliance cannot be accessed properly or the proposed task falls outside their authorisation. We will explain the reason and tell you what needs to change before work can continue.

If the engineer finds a fault, they will explain what they have found and whether further assessment or repair is recommended. They will not carry out chargeable additional work without your agreement. Any repair cover will be assessed under the relevant plan terms.

After the service, we will provide a summary of the work completed and any advice about using or caring for the appliance. Please keep this with your service records. Tell us if anything in the summary is unclear or does not match your understanding.

A service checks the appliance’s condition at the visit. It cannot guarantee that a fault will not develop afterwards. Follow any safety instructions the engineer gives you, particularly where they advise you not to use the appliance until an issue has been resolved.

If you need to change or cancel your booking, contact us through the details in your booking confirmation. We will explain the available arrangements and any applicable cancellation charge before you decide how to proceed.

If you are unhappy with the service, please contact us and describe your concern. We will review the visit record, explain the outcome and discuss any action needed. Nothing in these servicing arrangements limits your statutory rights.

cell.item: POL-SER/Extended Care Plus/Servicing under the plan

result.text:
Routine servicing helps keep your appliance working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to check its condition. Under Extended Care Plus, you can book a routine service through Halvard Home for an appliance registered to your plan. Servicing is separate from arranging a repair for a fault.

Extended Care Plus members get 14% off routine services.

The discount applies to the routine service price quoted by Halvard Home. Your plan must be active when you book and when the service takes place. We will check your membership and confirm the price before you agree to the booking.

Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the agreed service are not included in the routine service price unless we expressly confirm otherwise. If your appliance needs repair work, we will explain whether that work is covered by your plan or requires a separate payment.

Extended Care Plus members are offered a visit within 4 working days.

This commitment runs from when we accept your service request and have the details needed to arrange the visit. It concerns the appointment offered, rather than completion of repairs that may be identified during servicing. You can choose a different available appointment if the offered visit is unsuitable.

To book, contact our service team using the contact details shown in your plan documents or on our website. Tell us which registered appliance needs servicing, where it is installed and whether you have noticed anything unusual about its operation.

Please tell us about known faults when you book. A routine service is not a substitute for a repair visit, and we may need to arrange a different type of appointment. Giving us accurate information helps us send an engineer prepared for the work.

We will explain the proposed service and confirm the booking details. Please check that the address and contact information are correct. Let us know about access restrictions, parking arrangements or building entry requirements that could affect the engineer’s visit.

Tell us if you need adjustments to help you use our service. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you and explain what we can provide. You do not need to share medical information that is unrelated to the support you are requesting.

An adult who can authorise the agreed work must be present and able to give the engineer access. If someone is attending on your behalf, please make sure they understand the purpose of the visit and can contact you if a decision is needed.

Please leave the appliance accessible and clear the surrounding area of belongings that could obstruct the engineer. Keep children and pets away from the working area. We will tell you about preparation needed for the service when we confirm your appointment.

Do not disconnect, move or dismantle the appliance unless our service team specifically asks you to do so and explains how to proceed safely. Tell the engineer about damage, leaks, unusual smells or other concerns before work begins.

The engineer will assess whether servicing can be carried out safely. They may decline to proceed if the appliance, its installation or the working area presents a risk. If this happens, we will explain the concern and what needs to change before servicing can proceed.

The service will follow the maintenance requirements applicable to your appliance and the scope agreed at booking. The engineer will explain their findings in plain language, including concerns that need attention. Servicing does not guarantee that an appliance will remain free from faults.

If the engineer recommends work outside the agreed service, we will explain the reason and any charge before seeking your agreement. You can decline chargeable work. Where a safety concern is identified, the engineer will explain whether you should stop using the appliance.

If you need to change or cancel your booking, contact us as soon as you can. We will explain the available options and any applicable cancellation terms. Any cancellation or missed visit charge must have been clearly disclosed when you booked.

If we need to rearrange the visit, we will contact you and discuss a suitable alternative. After servicing, keep the service record with your plan documents. Contact our service team if you have questions about the findings or are unhappy with how the visit was handled.

The Scotland North service team covers postcode areas AB, IV, KW, PH and DD. Availability depends on your address, the nature of the fault and whether an engineer with the right skills can reach your home. Please contact Halvard Home to check coverage and arrange a visit rather than contacting an engineer directly.

Engineers in Scotland North travel up to 40 miles from their base. Being within a listed postcode area does not automatically mean your address is within an engineer’s usual travel area. If your home falls outside that area, we will explain whether an alternative arrangement is available before accepting your booking.

An engineer call-out in Scotland North costs £117.00. This charge covers travel within the engineer’s usual service area and an assessment of the reported fault. Repairs, replacement parts and work beyond that assessment may carry additional charges. We will explain any proposed charges and ask for your agreement before chargeable work begins.

When you request a visit, please describe the fault as clearly as you can. Tell us what happens when you try to use the appliance, whether there are unusual sounds or smells, and whether the fault is constant or intermittent. Photographs can be helpful where they show the issue safely and clearly.

Please also tell us about any repair attempts, accidental damage or changes to the installation that may be relevant. This helps us assess whether an engineer visit is appropriate and what preparation may be needed. We may suggest safe checks you can carry out yourself, but you should not remove covers or attempt electrical work.

If you believe the appliance is unsafe, stop using it and contact us for advice. Where it is safe to do so, disconnect it from the electricity supply. Do not put yourself at risk to reach a plug or switch. An engineer booking is not an emergency response service.

We will agree the appointment arrangements with you and explain how you will receive confirmation. Please check that your address and contact details are correct. Tell us about access restrictions, difficult roads, ferry crossings, parking arrangements or anything else that could affect the engineer’s journey. Travel disruption and severe weather can affect visits across the region.

If circumstances prevent the engineer from reaching you, we will contact you using the details supplied with your booking. We will explain the available options and help you rearrange where possible. Please contact us if your own circumstances change, rather than relying on a message passed through a neighbour or left at the property.

An adult who can provide access and discuss the proposed work must be present for the visit. If you are arranging access through someone else, please make sure they understand the reported fault and know whether they are authorised to approve chargeable work. We cannot assume that a person answering the door has your permission.

Please make the work area accessible and clear away belongings that could obstruct the engineer. Keep children and pets away from the area while work is under way.
